Other: This is the reference assessment of when the ubiquitous minimal active space is good enough. Spin-orbit coupling constants: reproduced to within about 200 cm-1 of experimentally derived values, which is usually under 10 percent error for 4dn, 5dn and 4fn configurations but up to 30 percent for 3dn; the abstract-level summary is overestimation by 5-30 percent for 3d ions, within plus or minus 10 percent for 4d and 5d ions, and overestimation by 2-10 percent for trivalent 4f ions. The Slater-Condon error is systematic for divalent 4d and trivalent 4f ions, so simple scaling may be viable there when resources are limited, but this does not hold for 3d ions. The spin-orbit coupling constant varies quadratically with atomic number Z at fixed dn configuration, and also for the trivalent lanthanides even though the configuration changes with Z; SOC detail: yes, spin-orbit coupling introduced by state interaction after variational spin-free orbital optimization

point_group: reduced to the highest available symmetry implementable for each molecule
geometry_source: QUESTDB benchmark geometries
method: state-averaged CASSCF with MC-PDFT (tPBE) and NEVPT2, using automated entropy-ranked active-space selection

active_space_orbital_description: Automated 'max(n,m)' spaces capped by a maximum CSF count: max(4,4) (N_max_CSF = 20), max(5,5), max(12,12) and others. Orbitals are ranked by occupancy and entropy pairs (n_j, S_j) and pruned until the CSF count falls under the cap.
active_space_protocol: Approximate pair-coefficient (APC) automated selection with a 'max(n,m)' cap set by a maximum CSF count: orbitals carry an occupancy and an approximated entropy (n_j, S_j) and are admitted in entropy order until the CSF count would exceed N_max_CSF. A worked example takes a max(4,4) target (cap 20 CSFs) and returns a (5,4) space with exactly 20 CSFs. Critically, the authors then FILTER: 20-30% of the automatically generated active spaces were poor and were eliminated by applying a threshold to the SA-CASSCF absolute error, leaving 373 of the 542 excitations for the method comparison.
electronic_structure_description: Largest benchmarking of MC-PDFT and HMC-PDFT to date, over the QUESTDB set of 542 vertical excitations. After discarding the 20-30% of automatically chosen active spaces that were poor, HMC-PDFT performs about as well as NEVPT2 and CC2 on the remaining 373 excitations. The optimal fraction of SA-CASSCF energy to mix into HMC-PDFT with the tPBE on-top functional was found to be 25%, i.e. the value already used in tPBE0. NEVPT2 performance is significantly affected by active-space quality, and at normal grid size tPBE is on average about 114x cheaper than NEVPT2 for large max(12,12) spaces.

software: a development branch of OpenMolcas, version v18.09-617-g5a96a25e
basis_set: as in Thiel's benchmark set (TZVP)

active_space_protocol: the molecules were taken from Thiel's benchmark set, excluding ethene and cyclopropene because no singlet excited state was considered for those two; the first singlet vertical energy gap was computed with XDW-CASPT2 and compared with MS-CASPT2
electronic_structure_description: When the ground state and the first excited state are separated by more than zeta^(-1/2), the dynamical weighting leaves the two density matrices essentially unmixed and state-specific, the rotated reference states stay close to the originals, and XDW-CASPT2 should reproduce MS-CASPT2 accuracy - which is what this benchmark confirms. The same argument extends to model spaces larger than two provided all the states stay well separated; the difficult regime is many model states packed into a narrow energy window and interacting strongly at zeroth order, where the rotated states are linear combinations of the originals and the physical content of the Fock operator becomes hard to read off the weights.

compound_name: extended benchmark set of doubly excited states in small and medium organic molecules (QUEST double excitations, improved and extended)
formula: small and medium organic molecules of the QUEST doubles set
geometry_source: ground-state geometries of the QUEST benchmark protocol
method: CASSCF references followed by CASPT2 and CASPT3, both with and without the IPEA shift (default 0.25 Eh) and with a 0.3 a.u. level shift, plus partially contracted and strongly contracted NEVPT2; the Fock operator in the zeroth-order Hamiltonian is systematically built from the state-specific density. Benchmarked against selected-CI (CIPSI) and the high-order coupled cluster hierarchy EOM-CC3, EOM-CCSDT, EOM-CC4 and EOM-CCSDTQ, with the %T1 diagnostic from CC3/AVTZ used to classify a state as singly or doubly excited

active_space_orbital_description: a separate active space per system, per symmetry representation and per transition; the full description is given in the Supporting Information
active_space_protocol: active spaces are chosen individually for each system, each symmetry representation and each transition, following the protocol of the authors' earlier work; the SI carries the complete listing. The paper stresses that careful selection is what makes doubly excited states reachable at manageable cost, and that 0.1-0.2 eV accuracy is achievable with appropriate spaces. Whether the 3s Rydberg orbital is included in the space materially changes the answer: leave it out and a single genuine double excitation appears, put it in and the doubly excited configuration mixes with the Rydberg one.
electronic_structure_description: For one of the difficult cases the two computed states at 7.979(40) and 8.170(41) eV from CIPSI agree well with the reference 7.979 and 8.185 eV. Both states carry important singly and doubly excited configurations, combined in phase for the lower state and out of phase for the upper one; the mixing is weak at CASSCF and becomes pronounced only after the perturbative correction. Enlarging the basis from 6-31+G* to aug-cc-pVDZ or aug-cc-pVTZ stabilizes the (n -> 3s) Rydberg configuration relative to the (n,n -> pi*,pi*) one and suppresses the strong mixing - 6-31+G* is simply too compact to model it. Downgrading to CC4 or CCSDT also unmixes the two configurations, giving one genuine double and one Rydberg single; oddly the mixing returns at CC3, but for the wrong reason.
reference_short: Loos, Boggio-Pasqua, Jacquemin et al., Reference Energies for Double Excitations: Improvement and Extension

compound_name: Thiel's benchmark set of 28 closed-shell organic molecules: 223 vertical excitation energies evaluated with fourth-order NEVPT
formula: the 28 closed-shell organic molecules of the Thiel benchmark set
geometry_source: the geometries of the original Thiel benchmark study
method: approximate fourth-order N-electron valence perturbation theory, NEVPT4(SD): the fully internally contracted fourth-order NEVPT with the excitation space restricted to the first-order interacting space of internally contracted singles and doubles from the CASSCF reference, with the fourth-order renormalization terms dropped to keep size consistency in the absence of quadruples; compared against lower-order NEVPT variants, published CASPT2 results, and CC3 reference data
basis_set: TZVP
active_space_orbital_description: the active spaces of the earlier NEVPT study of Schapiro et al. on this benchmark set, chosen per molecule and not restated here
active_space_protocol: the protocol follows Schapiro et al., with state-averaged CASSCF used whenever several roots of the same symmetry are needed; although ORCA can state-average across different spatial and spin symmetries, the calculations were deliberately run separately per symmetry to allow direct comparison with the original work. Two protocols for the vertical energies: for excitations within the ground-state irreducible representation the ground-state energy comes from the state-averaged calculation, and a different route is used otherwise.
electronic_structure_description: Across 223 vertical excitation energies spanning pi -> pi*, n -> pi* and sigma -> pi* transitions in 28 molecules, NEVPT4(SD) systematically outperforms both the lower-order NEVPT variants and previously reported CASPT2 results, for singlets and triplets alike. The residual error is structured rather than random: n -> pi* transitions are overestimated by about 0.1 eV while pi -> pi* transitions are underestimated by about 0.04 eV. That shift persists at every NEVPT order but shrinks as the order increases.

compound_name: Schreiber (Thiel) benchmark set of organic molecules: correlated oscillator strengths and triplet excitation energies from adiabatic connection approaches on CAS wave functions
formula: the organic molecules of the Schreiber et al. benchmark set
geometry_source: the geometries of the Schreiber et al. benchmark set
method: adiabatic connection (AC) correlation energy methods AC0 and AC0D built on extended random phase approximation (ERPA) with complete active space reference wave functions, plus a new perturbation-corrected ERPA transition density matrix for the oscillator strengths; benchmarked against CASPT2, LR-CC2, LR-CCSD, CCSD and FCI values
basis_set: the basis sets of the Schreiber et al. benchmark protocol (TZVP)
active_space_orbital_description: complete active spaces per molecule as in the benchmark protocol; the methods are designed so that cost grows more slowly with the number of active orbitals than CASPT2 or NEVPT2 do
active_space_protocol: state-averaged CASSCF reference states from the ground state up to the target state I are required for an AC0D excitation energy; because AC0 and AC0D depend only on reduced density matrices up to second order, they scale far better in the number of active orbitals than CASPT2 and NEVPT2, whose cost confines them in practice to roughly 20 active electrons
electronic_structure_description: Oscillator strengths computed from the perturbation-corrected ERPA transition density matrices, together with AC0 and AC0D excitation energies, match CASPT2 accuracy at lower cost, and the corrected transition dipole moments come essentially free because every intermediate is already available from the AC0 energy calculation. For triplet excitations on the Schreiber set, the deexcitation correction in AC0D genuinely improves on AC0, especially for the lowest excited states, where the accuracy becomes comparable to LR-CC2 and LR-CCSD - with the difference that AC0 and AC0D remain multireference methods. The perturbation-corrected transition density matrices also beat the uncorrected ERPA ones against CCSD and FCI in matching basis sets.
reference_short: Drwal, Pernal & Pastorczak, Multireference Correlated Oscillator Strengths from Adiabatic Connection Approaches Based on Extended Random Phase Approximation, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2024, 20, 3659-3668

active_space_protocol: one tailored space per system and transition, with state averaging over the states of the same spin and spatial symmetry that are being targeted; CASPT2 with the standard level shift 0.3 and IPEA 0.25. PC-NEVPT2 is preferred over SC-NEVPT2 on theoretical grounds - more perturbers and greater flexibility - and was run systematically for QUEST#3.
electronic_structure_description: The TBEs/aug-cc-pVTZ assembled here benchmark a long list of lower-order wave function methods: CIS(D), ADC(2), CC2, STEOM-CCSD, CCSD, CCSDR(3), CCSDT-3, ADC(3), CC3, NEVPT2 and their spin-scaled variants. The accuracy of CASPT2 and NEVPT2 turns out to be the hardest to predict of any method in the set, because it depends on both the system and the chosen active space; the pattern that does emerge is that they are more accurate for transitions with a very small percentage of single-excitation character (error usually below 0.1 eV) than for the single-excitation-dominated ones, where the error approaches 0.1-0.2 eV. The whole data set is published through a website.
reference_short: Veril, Scemama, Caffarel, Loos, Jacquemin et al., QUESTDB: a database of highly accurate excitation energies for the electronic structure community

Only TPSSh-D3 (10% HF exchange) approaches the XMS-CASPT2 energetics, and even then its singlet is the closed-shell state rather than the correct multiconfigurational one; increasing HF exchange favours the triplet. XMS-CASPT2 overestimates saddling while all the DFT functionals underestimate it. method: state-averaged extended-active-space CASSCF(6,12) followed by state-specific multireference Moller-Plesset perturbation theory (MRMP) for each individual state; oscillator strengths use CASSCF transition moments and MRMP transition energies
software: MOLPRO for CASSCF reference wave functions; MR2D Version 2 for MRMP perturbation calculations; IBM RS6000-590 workstations at IMS
basis_set: Dunning cc-pVTZ on carbon and cc-pVDZ on hydrogen, with H polarization omitted in the production calculations; the explicit test compared [4s3p2d/2s] with [4s3p2d/2s1p] and changed valence excitation energies by <0.03 eV. No Rydberg functions were included.
active_space_orbital_description: Six pi electrons distributed among twelve pi orbitals. Starting from the six-valence-pi-orbital CAS (three bonding pi plus three antibonding pi* orbitals), the authors doubled the active orbital count in every symmetry. The paper does not print a complete symmetry-by-symmetry list of the six added pi orbitals. Sigma electrons remain outside the CAS and their dynamic sigma-pi polarization is introduced by MRMP.
active_space_protocol: (6,6): six pi electrons in the six valence pi/pi* orbitals; (6,12): active orbital count doubled in every symmetry and the same state calculations repeated. This row records the converged extended (6,12) results.

electronic_structure_description: The enlarged pi space primarily improves the ionic plus states by moving part of the important sigma-pi polarization/nondynamical response into the reference. Covalent-state CASSCF energies change little, while ionic-state CASSCF excitations decrease by about 0.3-0.5 eV. The resulting MRMP spectrum reaches <=0.23 eV error for the tabulated singlets and <=0.29 eV for triplets. Detailed CASSCF configuration coefficients are printed only for the smaller CAS(6,6), not for this extended reference.
Other: TOTAL ENERGY: ground-state MRMP energy with twelve active pi orbitals = -231.62903 Eh; the authors note that the smaller-space MRMP energy is paradoxically 0.00170 Eh lower because second-order perturbation theory can overestimate correlation when its zeroth-order Hamiltonian is incomplete. VERTICAL SINGLET RESULTS (Table VII; D6h state [D2h component], CASSCF/MRMP eV, oscillator strength): 1^1B2u- [1^1B3u-] 4.89/4.67, f=0; 1^1B1u+ [1^1B2u+] 7.57/6.14, f=0; 1^1E1u+ components [1^1B3u+ and 2^1B2u+] both 8.78/6.84, f=0.8599 for each printed component; 1^1E2g- components [2^1Ag-,1^1B1g-] both 8.04/7.71, f=0. VERTICAL TRIPLETS: 1^3B1u- [1^3B2u-] 3.85/3.83; 1^3E1u- [1^3B3u-] 4.83/4.47, with the degenerate 2^3B2u- component printed at CASSCF 4.83 but no separate MRMP number in Table VII; 1^3B2u+ [1^3B3u+] 6.78/5.45; 1^3E2g- components [1^3Ag-,1^3B1g-] both 7.15/6.92 eV. EXPERIMENTAL COMPARISONS printed in Table VII are 4.90 (1B2u), 6.20 (1B1u), 6.94 (1E1u), 7.80 (1E2g), 3.95 (3B1u), 4.76 (3E1u), 5.60 (3B2u), and 6.83 eV (3E2g). The extended MRMP deviations are therefore -0.23, -0.06, -0.10, -0.09, -0.12, -0.29, -0.15, and +0.09 eV, respectively. ACTIVE-SPACE EFFECT: relative to CAS(6,6), CASSCF ionic-state excitations fall by 0.34 eV (1B1u), 0.51 eV (1E1u), and 0.46 eV (3B2u), while corresponding MRMP predictions rise toward experiment by 0.31, 0.51, and 0.38 eV. No Rydberg functions/states are included.

active_space_orbital_description: The same minimal seven-electron seven-orbital and eleven-electron nine-orbital spaces as the quartet, enlarged along a different sequence: eleven orbitals adding virtuals with iron dxz and dxy character, twelve adding one with dyz character, and finally fourteen including the fourth iron dz2 double-shell orbital together with an additional empty ligand orbital.
active_space_protocol: The same construction and enlargement strategy as for the quartet but with a different order of orbital admission, reflecting which double-shell orbitals could be stabilised in this state. The largest space contains the four iron dxz, dxy, dyz and dz2 double-shell orbitals. The contributions of the iron double-shell orbitals to the natural orbitals are noted to be significantly larger for this state than for the quartet.
electronic_structure_description: For the doublet state the spin density shows larger deviations with respect to the size of the active space than the quartet does, converging gradually toward the largest reference as the space is enlarged. The minimal seven-electron seven-orbital and eleven-electron nine-orbital spaces, without double-shell orbitals, are qualitatively similar to the reference and suffice for a qualitative estimate, but quantitatively correct spin densities require the iron double-shell orbitals to be included. Spaces containing thirteen active electrons give very similar spin densities. The same bonding picture applies as for the quartet, with one iron d orbital non-interacting and three interacting covalently with the nitrosyl orbitals.
Other: The space is built up from a qualitative molecular orbital picture: four metal 3d orbitals plus both nitrosyl pi-star orbitals, extended by a fifth metal d orbital, giving a minimal seven electrons in seven orbitals; adding both nitrosyl pi orbitals gives eleven electrons in nine orbitals. It is then systematically enlarged toward a double shell, one metal d orbital at a time, through eleven, twelve, thirteen and fifteen orbitals for the quartet and eleven, twelve and fourteen for the doublet. The obstacles encountered are reported rather than glossed: identifying the double-shell orbitals is described as not trivial because they mix considerably with antibonding ligand orbitals, so additional ligand orbitals had to be admitted to keep the space stable; in one case a double-shell orbital rotated into an empty ligand orbital and a further virtual had to be added to recover it; the fifth metal double-shell orbital could not be included at all because its destabilization by the point-charge environment would require many more ligand orbitals; and an alternative route adding a ligand sigma and sigma-star pair proved incompatible with including the remaining double-shell orbitals. The result is that convergence depends on which state is asked about. For the quartet the spin density depends only weakly on the space, and the minimal seven-orbital and nine-orbital calculations without any double-shell effect already agree qualitatively with the largest reference. For the doublet the deviations are larger, the spin density converging gradually toward the reference as the space grows, and the authors state the distinction precisely: the minimal spaces suffice for a qualitative estimate while quantitatively correct spin densities require the metal double-shell orbitals. Consistently, the double-shell contributions to the natural orbitals are noted to be significantly larger for the doublet than for the quartet. So the same molecule, same property, different spin state, and the answer to whether a double shell is needed flips. The bonding picture the space reveals is stable across all of them: one metal d orbital does not interact with the ligand at all, while three others interact strongly and covalently with the nitrosyl orbitals to give two bonding, two antibonding and one nonbonding combination. One structural caveat: the ligand field is modelled by point charges rather than real ligands, and the authors note that the modelled field is not strong enough, so the environment that destabilises the fifth double-shell orbital is itself an approximation.

Other: The active space here is specified by three stated rules rather than by a number, and the rules are what make the five species comparable. All ruthenium 4d orbitals and their electrons must be in the space; the ruthenium 5d-like orbitals that correlate with them must also be in, to capture the double-shell effect; and the four porphyrin pi orbitals of the classic Gouterman set -- two occupied, in the totally symmetric and one of the antisymmetric blocks, and two unoccupied -- must be in. That gives fourteen orbitals, itemized by symmetry block as five, three, three and three, and the SAME fourteen orbitals are used for the neutral singlet, the neutral triplet, the cation and the anion, with only the electron count changing to follow the charge: fourteen, fourteen, thirteen and fifteen. Holding the orbital set fixed while the electron count tracks the charge is exactly the design needed to compare oxidation states, since any difference between species then cannot be blamed on a different choice of orbitals. Only for the oxo anion is the set enlarged, by one further orbital added specifically to represent the ruthenium-oxygen antibonding interaction -- an enlargement made because a specific bond is being broken, not to recover more correlation. The space is used as a DIAGNOSTIC rather than as a source of energetics. Two independent checks pointing the same way is a stronger licence for the cheaper method than either alone. The second finding is chemical and cuts against the experimental proposal that motivated the calculation: the leading configuration assigns ruthenium the +II oxidation state in ALL five species, including the cation and both anions, so the experimentally proposed +I-to-+III change is not what the wave function shows -- the added or removed electron sits on the porphyrin ring, not on the metal. The scope limit is that these are CASSCF wave functions with no perturbative correction, so the weights speak to static correlation only, and a fourteen-orbital space concentrated on the metal d shell and the Gouterman four cannot report multireference character arising anywhere outside it. The calculations were run in the smaller correlation-consistent basis under C2v symmetry even for the species whose optimized geometry is C4v.

active_space_protocol: CASSCF was run for an explicitly diagnostic purpose — "to check the viability of such a single-determinant approach and to describe the nature of the singlet and triplet H2NC6H4+" — after the bulk of the study had been done at B3LYP. The test is the weight of the ground-state reference determinant in the CASSCF wave function, read from the coefficient of the lowest eigenvector and from the fractional populations of the eight active orbitals. The same test had been applied to the parent phenyl cation, where the reference determinant contributes more than 90% (eigenvector coefficients 0.94 for the singlet and 0.95 for the triplet), justifying B3LYP there.
electronic_structure_description: Excited singlet lying at least 10 kcal/mol above the triplet in the gas phase. Its CASSCF wave function "is poorly described by any single configuration" and cannot be properly represented by a single determinant, so the B3LYP description of this state is not reliable — in contrast to the parent phenyl cation, whose singlet has a reference determinant weight above 90% (eigenvector coefficient 0.94). Geometrically the singlet differs from the planar triplet: the nitrogen is slightly pyramidalized and the divalent carbon C1 is slightly bent out of plane and puckered.
Other: The (8,8) space — six ring pi orbitals, the nitrogen lone pair, and the sigma orbital on the divalent carbon — is used to answer a single question: can a single-determinant method be trusted for this ion? The answer differs by spin state, and that difference is the paper's finding. For the 3B2 triplet the CASSCF wave function is dominated by one configuration, with the leading coefficient above 0.93 and fractional populations of the eight active orbitals close to 0, 1 and 2 — so B3LYP is adequate there, and indeed the CASSCF and UB3LYP geometries and charges "are in excellent agreement only for the 3B2 state". For the 1A' singlet the wave function "is poorly described by any single configuration" and "cannot be properly described by a single-determinant" treatment, so the B3LYP singlet results are not reliable. This is a clean case of an active space being used to bound the validity of a cheaper method rather than to produce numbers. The orbital populations also carry chemical content that a single-determinant picture would hide: in the triplet, the sigma and one pi orbital are each singly occupied, with the sigma electron highly localized on C1 but the pi electron delocalized over the ring and onto nitrogen. Combined with UB3LYP spin densities showing nitrogen carrying the second highest spin density (0.35), this makes the triplet "65% diradical, 35% carbene character at divalent C1" — which explains why it does not react with neutral sigma nucleophiles (there is no cation at C1, the largest positive charge being +0.37 on C4) but adds readily to pi nucleophiles as an electrophilic radical. For the parent phenyl cation the same diagnostic gave >90% single-reference character for BOTH states, so amino substitution is what breaks the single-determinant description of the singlet.

The space was validated by enlarging it with one additional virtual orbital of each of the two symmetries; the resulting optimized geometry was close to the original, and the added orbitals were found to carry occupation numbers below 0.003.
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 2A2, the upper Jahn-Teller component, lying a few kcal/mol above the 2B1 state. The starting reference configuration is (9a1)2(6b2)2(1b1)2(2b1)2(1a2)1, and the same active space is used as for the lower component. In the optimized geometry only the carbon-carbon bond perpendicular to the binary symmetry axis shows double-bond character, in contrast to the diene-like structure of the lower component. Its total energy is -193.146453 hartree, and in combination with the magnesium cation -392.510536 hartree, giving a binding energy of 74.3 kcal/mol against 74.0 for the lower component. The geometry agrees with previous theoretical work on the same footing as the lower component.
Other: The multiconfigurational treatment here is confined to one species for one reason -- orbital degeneracy -- and the paper says so directly: the main problem in the cyclopentadienyl radical is the degeneracy of the valence orbitals, which produces a Jahn-Teller split of a few kcal/mol between the two components. That is precisely the situation a single-determinant method cannot handle, and it is why this fragment alone is treated multiconfigurationally while everything else in the study, including the magnesium complexes that are its subject, is handled by single-reference perturbation and composite methods. The space is specified by symmetry block rather than by total: five valence electrons distributed over four orbitals of b1 symmetry and two of a2 symmetry. Crucially the same space is used for both Jahn-Teller components, each started from its own open-shell reference configuration, which is what makes the small energy difference between them meaningful -- the two states differ by which orbital carries the single electron, and comparing them across differently constructed spaces would confound the splitting with the reference. The validation is a proper enlargement test with a stated criterion. The space was extended by one further virtual orbital of each symmetry, and the resulting optimized geometry came out close to the original; the authors connect the two observations by noting that the added orbitals carry insignificant occupation numbers, less than 0.003. Reporting the occupation numbers rather than just the geometric agreement is what turns this from an assertion into evidence, since an orbital with occupation below 0.003 cannot be contributing to the wave function regardless of what the geometry does. The geometries the space produces are chemically interpretable in a way that supports the assignment: one component shows a large contribution from a diene-like structure while in the other only the carbon-carbon bond perpendicular to the symmetry axis has double-bond character, and both agree with previous theoretical work to within 3 percent in bond lengths and 1 percent in angles. One limitation of scope worth recording: the multiconfigurational energies enter the reaction thermochemistry only through this fragment, so the computed dissociation energies pair a multiconfigurational description of the radical with a single-reference description of everything else, and the two Jahn-Teller components differ by only 0.0004 hartree in the tabulated total energies.

active_space_protocol: Full valence active space - six electrons in six orbitals - used identically for the state-specific multiconfigurational calculations, for the state-averaged orbitals feeding the configuration-interaction spin-orbit step, and for the coupling calculation inside the functional-based dynamics. Because the program cannot compute spin-orbit coupling from density functional theory, that coupling is obtained from a configuration-interaction calculation in the same space using the high-spin alpha functional orbitals, so the active space is not eliminated even in the nominally functional treatment. electronic_structure_description: The 3B1 state, on which every trajectory is initialized and whose lifetime is the quantity being predicted. Its barrier to the crossing point is the one that matters for the rate, and the two methods differ substantially: 1051 reciprocal centimetres by functional against 717 by the multiconfigurational treatment, a difference large enough on its own to change the rate constant appreciably. That it does not is the paper's central observation, because the functional simultaneously overestimates the spin-orbit coupling relative to the multiconfigurational values, and the two errors offset.
Other: The authors give three named reasons for replacing the multiconfigurational treatment with a functional in their dynamics: choosing a space that describes all the geometries accessible during a trajectory is 'a very challenging task'; the multiconfigurational method recovers little dynamic correlation, which 'could result in very inaccurate electronic state energies, and hence in flawed nonadiabatic simulations'; and the functional is a black-box method that 'eliminates the need for constructing the active spaces'. But the elimination is INCOMPLETE, and the reason is a software limitation the authors name: because their program cannot compute spin-orbit coupling with density functional methods, the coupling in the functional-based dynamics is STILL obtained from a configuration-interaction calculation in the SAME six-electron six-orbital space, using the high-spin alpha set of functional orbitals. So the 'active-space-free' method still requires an active space for the very quantity that drives the process being simulated. The headline result is an explicit, quantified error cancellation that the authors identify themselves rather than presenting as agreement. The two methods give excellent agreement on the rate constants, and the explanation is that two effects cancel: the functional gives higher barriers, which would slow the crossing, and stronger spin-orbit coupling, which would speed it up. Both are quantified - the barrier from the triplet to the crossing point is 1051 reciprocal centimetres by functional against 717 by the multiconfigurational method, the barrier from the singlet is 2217 higher, and the singlet-triplet minimum separation is nearly 2000 higher. A reader should not conclude from the agreement that either method has the barrier or the coupling right; the two errors happen to oppose each other for this molecule, and there is no reason to expect the cancellation to survive a change of system. The active space itself is the FULL VALENCE space, six electrons in six orbitals, so it is set by a rule rather than by tuning and is identical between the two treatments and between the multiconfigurational dynamics and the coupling calculation - which is what makes the comparison clean. Geometries and harmonic frequencies from the two methods agree well, so the disagreement is specifically in relative energies and couplings, not structures. The authors also explain a discrepancy with their OWN earlier work: a tighter coupling threshold of 0.1 was used previously against 0.2 here, so the multiconfigurational rates and lifetimes differ slightly between the two papers - a numerical parameter, named, rather than a silent revision. Finally, both dynamics treatments give rate constants about a FACTOR OF TWO larger than the statistical transition-state estimate, which the authors attribute to nonlocal interstate transitions absent from the statistical description - so the dynamical and statistical pictures differ by more than the two electronic-structure methods do.
reference_short: Fedorov, Lykhin & Varganov, J. Phys. Chem. A 2018, 122, 3480
notes: Part of a study of intersystem crossing between the lowest singlet and triplet states of germylene, used as a test system for a new implementation of ab initio multiple spawning dynamics interfaced with density functional theory, compared against the authors' earlier multiconfigurational implementation and against statistical nonadiabatic transition state theory. The initial state of every trajectory; its barrier to the crossing seam differs by 334 reciprocal centimetres between the two methods.

method: CASSCF potential energy surface scans and geometry optimizations, with second-order multireference Moller-Plesset perturbation corrections computed at several conformations including all valence and virtual orbitals; the conical intersection was optimized in a reduced space and verified in the larger one
software: GAMESS for most calculations; Gaussian 03 for the conical intersection optimization
basis_set: Huzinaga-Dunning double-zeta with polarization functions added on the skeletal carbons (exponent 0.75) and on nitrogen (exponent 0.80), a double-zeta plus polarization quality set; the polarization functions on the skeletal carbons are stated to be necessary to obtain a reasonable intersection
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in the highest five occupied and lowest five unoccupied pi orbitals. These were selected from all seven occupied and lowest seven unoccupied pi orbitals by a configuration interaction calculation including up to triple excitations, discarding the two lowest occupied orbitals whose occupations exceeded 1.98 and the two highest unoccupied whose occupations fell below 0.02, a criterion verified for all sampled conformations.
active_space_protocol: Reduced in two stages from the fourteen-electron fourteen-orbital full pi space, declared desirable but unrealistic for surface scanning. The ten-orbital space serves the scans and the minima; an eight-orbital space, justified by the same preliminary calculation, was used for the conical intersection search and then checked by a ten-orbital calculation at the located geometry confirming the state gap remained small enough. All work is confined to Cs symmetry, so a planar structure has C2v symmetry and nonplanar distortion is allowed only within the mirror plane.
nroots_per_mult: the ground and first excited singlet states
electronic_structure_description: The relaxed geometry on the first excited singlet surface, optimized in the same ten-orbital space under the Cs constraint. The excited molecule reaches this region after vertical excitation and then travels onward to the intersection with the ground state.
Other: The space here is arrived at by a two-stage reduction from a stated ideal, with each stage justified numerically rather than by assertion, and the criterion is occupation numbers taken from an independent calculation. The desirable space is named first: fourteen electrons in fourteen orbitals, since the molecule has fourteen pi electrons, ten from the bicyclic skeleton and four from the nitrile group. That is declared unrealistic for scanning potential energy surfaces, so a configuration interaction calculation including up to triple excitations was run over all seven occupied and the lowest seven unoccupied pi orbitals, and the resulting occupation numbers used to prune. The lowest two occupied orbitals came out above 1.98 and the highest two unoccupied below 0.02, so those four were dropped, leaving ten electrons in ten orbitals. The crucial detail is that the occupation criterion was checked for all sampled conformations, not just at equilibrium -- a space pruned on occupation numbers at one geometry can easily fail elsewhere on a surface that runs to a conical intersection, and the authors closed that gap explicitly. A second reduction follows for the intersection search alone, down to eight electrons in eight orbitals on the basis of the same preliminary calculation showing that four occupied and four unoccupied pi orbitals suffice where the two states are nearly degenerate. This one is validated after the fact rather than before: the intersection was optimized in the eight-orbital space, then a ten-orbital calculation was performed at that geometry and the gap between the two states confirmed small enough to still be an intersection. Optimizing in a small space and verifying in a larger one at the located point is a cheap and honest way to use a reduced space for a geometry search, and the authors draw the right conclusion, that the larger space would give a similar structure rather than that it would give the same one. The whole scheme rests on a symmetry constraint that is itself a modelling choice: calculations are confined to Cs, so a planar structure has the full two-fold symmetry while nonplanar distortions are permitted only within the mirror plane. Since the central question is whether the intersection is nonplanar in the seven-membered ring, constraining the allowed distortions is a substantive restriction, and the paper devotes an appendix to defending it. A second appendix defends the basis: polarization functions on the skeletal carbons are stated to be necessary to obtain a reasonable intersection at all for this family of molecules, so the intersection geometry is sensitive to the one-electron basis as well as to the space. Dynamical correlation enters only as single-point corrections at several conformations, with all valence and virtual orbitals included in the perturbation, so the surfaces that were scanned and the geometries that were optimized carry no correlation beyond the ten-orbital space.

Other: The space here is arrived at by a two-stage reduction from a stated ideal, with each stage justified numerically rather than by assertion, and the criterion is occupation numbers taken from an independent calculation. The desirable space is named first: fourteen electrons in fourteen orbitals, since the molecule has fourteen pi electrons, ten from the bicyclic skeleton and four from the nitrile group. That is declared unrealistic for scanning potential energy surfaces, so a configuration interaction calculation including up to triple excitations was run over all seven occupied and the lowest seven unoccupied pi orbitals, and the resulting occupation numbers used to prune. The lowest two occupied orbitals came out above 1.98 and the highest two unoccupied below 0.02, so those four were dropped, leaving ten electrons in ten orbitals. The crucial detail is that the occupation criterion was checked for all sampled conformations, not just at equilibrium -- a space pruned on occupation numbers at one geometry can easily fail elsewhere on a surface that runs to a conical intersection, and the authors closed that gap explicitly. A second reduction follows for the intersection search alone, down to eight electrons in eight orbitals on the basis of the same preliminary calculation showing that four occupied and four unoccupied pi orbitals suffice where the two states are nearly degenerate. This one is validated after the fact rather than before: the intersection was optimized in the eight-orbital space, then a ten-orbital calculation was performed at that geometry and the gap between the two states confirmed small enough to still be an intersection. Optimizing in a small space and verifying in a larger one at the located point is a cheap and honest way to use a reduced space for a geometry search, and the authors draw the right conclusion, that the larger space would give a similar structure rather than that it would give the same one. The whole scheme rests on a symmetry constraint that is itself a modelling choice: calculations are confined to Cs, so a planar structure has the full two-fold symmetry while nonplanar distortions are permitted only within the mirror plane. Since the central question is whether the intersection is nonplanar in the seven-membered ring, constraining the allowed distortions is a substantive restriction, and the paper devotes an appendix to defending it. A second appendix defends the basis: polarization functions on the skeletal carbons are stated to be necessary to obtain a reasonable intersection at all for this family of molecules, so the intersection geometry is sensitive to the one-electron basis as well as to the space. Dynamical correlation enters only as single-point corrections at several conformations, with all valence and virtual orbitals included in the perturbation, so the surfaces that were scanned and the geometries that were optimized carry no correlation beyond the ten-orbital space.

To describe it, three a' orbitals were added -- the singly occupied in-plane p orbital of nitrogen and two combinations of the in-plane oxygen and nitrogen lone pairs -- to the eight a''-type pi and pi* orbitals. So one orbital was traded out of the pi block to admit the in-plane orbital the transition actually uses. This is a clean example of the space being chosen by which transitions must be representable rather than by a uniform recipe, and of holding the total size fixed so that the two states' reference weights remain comparable: they sit at 0.74 to 0.77 across both tables. The consequence for the paper's conclusion is direct. The computed triplet spectrum shows several intense bands in the visible and near ultraviolet that bear no relation to the experimental spectrum, and that mismatch is what the authors take as confirming the absence of the triplet nitrene among the photolysis products. A negative identification of this kind is only as good as the space's ability to produce those bands in the first place, which is precisely why the in-plane orbitals had to be admitted. A second and independent caveat concerns intruder states rather than orbital selection. To obtain a satisfactory description of all excited states at the CASPT2 level it was necessary to resort to level shifting, and the authors state that they carefully assured no artifacts were introduced, reporting in supplementary tables the results of calculations with level shifts ranging from 0 to 0.3 au; the tabulated energies use 0.25 au. That is the right way to use a level shift -- scanned and reported rather than fixed by default -- but it means the excitation energies carry a chosen parameter, and a few entries show how much CASSCF and CASPT2 can disagree in a single reference: for the triplet the 2 3A' state moves from 3.38 eV at CASSCF up to 4.48 eV at CASPT2, and the 3 3A' state from 4.03 to 5.15 eV, both shifting upward while every other state shifts downward. Finally, note that the multiconfigurational treatment was applied only at geometries obtained elsewhere, at the B3LYP/6-31G* level, and that the electronic spectra of the substituted acetyl derivative were predicted with time-dependent DFT rather than with this space at all.

electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 6H15/2 for Dy(III), 4f9. The magnetic anisotropy axis lies along the axial O-Dy-O bond, perpendicular to the ground-state beta electron density, minimizing electrostatic repulsion. Ground and first-excited Kramers doublets are strongly axial (gx = gy ~ 0.0), and the angle between the ground and first-excited anisotropy axes is under 6 degrees, so relaxation proceeds via higher excited states. Significant thermally-activated QTM at the second excited state sets the relaxation path |-15/2> -> |-13/2> -> |-1/2> -> |+1/2> -> |+13/2> -> |15/2>. Axial crystal-field parameters (k = 2, 4, 6; q = 0) exceed the non-axial ones, confirming substantial axiality in all three. For complex 1 (Cl): gz = 19.857 in the ground Kramers doublet; the eight ground Kramers doublets from 6H15/2 span up to 902.0 K; Ucal = 606.3 K. This is the smallest barrier of the series, attributed to the smaller, strongly hydrogen-bonded chloride and the correspondingly smaller axial B2-0 crystal-field parameter.
reference_short: Deciphering the role of anions and secondary coordination sphere in tuning anisotropy in Dy(III) air-stable D5h SIMs
notes: The three complexes differ only in the halide counter-anion in the secondary coordination sphere; the Dy coordination sphere itself is essentially identical. Computed Loprop charges on the equatorial water oxygens rise 1 < 2 < 3 while the counter-anion charge falls 1 > 2 > 3, the latter effect dominating and rationalizing the Ucal/Ueff trend. Average Dy-halide distances are 4.56 A (1, Cl), 4.80 A (2, Br) and 5.04 A (3, I).

active_space_protocol: (14,10) with first 10 roots in the SA-CASSCF calculations, following the active spaces and root counts of an earlier study. The paper's contribution is the correction step: for each MD snapshot the molecular-orbital overlap matrix against a reference-geometry wavefunction (e.g. the vacuum equilibrium geometry with the desired active space) is computed, and where the optimized active space has drifted, orbital pairs are swapped and a second CASSCF optimization is run using the previous wavefunction as the initial guess. The orbitals analysed are the state-averaged natural orbitals from OpenMolcas. Thymine and guanine were among the worst offenders for active-space drift across the ensemble.
electronic_structure_description: Uracil sampled over force-field MD geometries in explicit water, with SA-CASSCF excitation energies computed per snapshot. The active space is not automatically preserved across an MD ensemble - a substantial fraction of snapshots converge to the wrong active space unless corrected.
reference_short: An Algorithm to Correct for the CASSCF Active Space in Multiscale QM/MM Calculations Based on Geometry Ensembles (ChemRxiv preprint, 2020)
notes: Mined from a PDF supplied by hand (automated OA fetch had failed). Metal-free organic nucleobases in explicit water. active_space_protocol: CAS(12,9) assembled by the fragment merging procedure, then NEVPT2. Getting the copper 3d_xy orbital into the active space proved hard enough that the authors built the space by hand from fragments: the copper corrole was split into a Cu(III) fragment at charge +3 and a corrole(3-) fragment at the same coordinates, separate CASSCF calculations were run on each - (8e,5o) for the metal and (4e,4o) for the ligand - the resulting wavefunction files were merged with orca_mergefrag, and a (12e,9o) CASSCF with maxiter set to 1 was run on the merged file to inspect the orbitals without optimisation before manually reordering the copper 3d orbitals with the rotate keyword and reconverging. That procedure is the methodological content of the paper as much as the chemistry is: a space that will not form by automatic selection is assembled from pieces whose composition is known. The payoff is a quantitative decomposition of the ground state into metal and ligand oxidation states, which is exactly what the closed-shell versus open-shell controversy in copper corroles needs, and the authors are careful to say the question is not settled in general because substituent electronics and ring distortion both shift the balance.

method: SA-CASSCF vs XS-CASSCF (globally optimized [0.0,0.5] and molecule-specific [mu,nu]) benchmarked against QUESTDB theoretical best estimates; TDDFT/CAM-B3LYP and MS-CASPT2 for comparison

active_space_protocol: the 11-molecule set reuses the per-molecule active spaces of the group's earlier ionic-diagnostic study (10.1021/acs.jpca.3c05559): ethene (2,2), butadiene (4,4), hexatriene (6,6), octatetraene (8,8), naphthalene (10,10) etc. XS-CASSCF is the corrective follow-up to this group's Qat ionic-character diagnostic (10.1021/acs.jpca.3c05559): SA-CASSCF overestimates singlet ionic pi-pi* states by 1-2 eV because the transition-density self-repulsion (two-electron exchange integrals) is not screened by sigma-correlation. XS-CASSCF scales those exchange terms down with two parameters [mu, nu] to mimic sigma-correlation at NO extra cost - mu scales the diagonal exchange (controls the ionic S1), nu the off-diagonal coupling (controls multiconfigurational covalent states). Practical guidance the paper establishes: mu = 0.0 (simply dropping the exchange integral g_pq,qp) is usually optimal and makes the S1 energy independent of the exchange integral, halving the CASSCF singlet-triplet gap to one exchange integral rather than two; nu = 0.0 is best when only the HOMO-LUMO transition matters, but nu = 0.5-0.7 is safer when higher multiconfigurational covalent states are of interest. The recommended default is [0.0, 0.5].

geometry_source: Geometry from the QUESTDB database, optimized at CC3/aug-cc-pVTZ
method: State-averaged CASSCF and the exchange-scaled variant XS-CASSCF[mu,nu], in which selected diagonal and off-diagonal Hamiltonian contributions are scaled by two adjustable parameters to mimic sigma correlation without additional cost
basis_set: aug-cc-pVDZ
active_space_orbital_description: 6 electrons in 6 orbitals, a standard valence active space
nroots_per_mult: the ground state plus the states listed, all included in the state averaging
electronic_structure_description: States included in the state averaging alongside the ground state: 1Ag, two 1Bu, 3Ag, 3Bu. One of the two illustrative cases. Excitation energies in eV at SA-CASSCF, XS-CASSCF[0,0] and XS-CASSCF[0,0.5] against theoretical best estimates: 2 1A-g 5.57, 5.61, 5.34 against 5.62; 1 1B+u 7.39, 5.32, 5.59 against 5.37; 1 1B-u 6.79, 8.49, 7.07 against 6.96; 1 3A+g 4.31, 4.32, 4.33 against 4.36; 1 3B-u 2.72, 2.72, 2.73 against 2.73. Standard SA-CASSCF agrees with the best estimates to within 0.05 eV for the covalent states and overestimates the ionic 1 1B+u by 2 eV. The Qta diagnostic from the same CAS(6,6)/aug-cc-pVDZ wavefunction separates the two state types cleanly, 0.63 against 0.06.
Other: The problem this method addresses is an active-space problem stated plainly: with standard valence active spaces state-averaged CASSCF severely overestimates the energies of ionic pi-pi* states, typically by 1-2 eV, and the known remedies - a large increase in active-space size, or extensive dynamic correlation - are both expensive. Exchange scaling instead scales down the integrals that mimic sigma correlation, leaving the space untouched. Across 21 pi-pi* excitation energies of hydrocarbons the root-mean-square error against theoretical best estimates falls from 0.96 eV to 0.27 eV; on a harder set containing heteroatoms and more n-pi* states the improvement is smaller. States are labelled by Pariser's plus and minus nomenclature to separate ionic from covalent character, and a Qta diagnostic computed from the same CASSCF wavefunction distinguishes them numerically.

active_space_protocol: The paper's CASVB analysis transforms the canonical single-space CAS(6,6) exactly: all electron distributions and all Rumer spin couplings are retained, so CASVB and canonical CASSCF have identical energy/density. A previously reported double active space CAS(6,12), adding a second/diffuse pi shell, and MRMP on both spaces diagnose polarization/dynamic-correlation errors in ionic states. Nonorthogonal Rumer structures are assigned occupation n_I=C_I* sum_J S_IJ C_J, not naively squared coefficients.
electronic_structure_description: The 1A1g ground state is a covalent minus state dominated individually by Kekule structures, with Dewar and orthopolar/other ionic mixing; CASVB contains 175 structures in 22 D6h bonding classes, including five covalent structures. Covalent excitations rearrange spin coupling: 1B2u is the opposite-sign Kekule combination and 1E2g is predominantly Dewar. Ionic 1B1u and 1E1u states contain polar structures but no covalent structures and require sigma-pi polarization/diffuse active flexibility. CAS(6,6) vertical energies for 1B2u/1B1u/1E1u/1E2g are 4.82/7.91/9.29/8.01 eV; MRMP(6,6) gives 4.71/5.83/6.33/7.73 eV.
Other: CAS(6,12) energies are 4.89/7.57/8.78/8.04 eV and MRMP(6,12) gives 4.67/6.14/6.84/7.71 eV, versus experimental 4.90/6.20/6.94/7.80 eV. Thus enlarging the space barely changes covalent states but is essential for ionic 1B1u/1E1u, while MRMP supplies the missing dynamic sigma-pi response. The CAS(6,6) ground energy is -230.82572 Eh and MRMP(6,6) -231.63073 Eh. Ground-state total occupations for the Kekule and Dewar covalent classes are 0.1565 and 0.0771; the large 0.2528 orthopolar class reflects compensation required by orthogonal, non-reoptimized LMOs. Electronic terms, resonance structures, and polarities remain components of one molecule record rather than separate entries.

electronic_structure_description: TS1 is a five-member-ring C1 doublet transition structure for acidic-H abstraction by proton-coupled electron transfer. The OH lone pair points at the acidic proton while the OH unpaired electron interacts with the carbonyl oxygen. CASSCF wavefunction analysis supports electron transfer from the carbonyl-oxygen lone pair to OH coupled to proton transfer from HCOOH to OH. QCISD spin populations are O1=0.603 and carbonyl O3=0.386; both C-O distances are about 1.258 A at the QCISD geometry, consistent with pi redistribution. TS1 is well characterized by B3LYP, MP2, CASSCF, and QCISD. | formic acid + hydroxyl radical acidic-H abstraction TS2 (conventional H abstraction): TS2 is a planar six-member-ring Cs doublet transition structure for conventional acidic-hydrogen radical abstraction: concerted O5-H6 breaking and H6-O1 formation. CASSCF wavefunction analysis and QCISD spin populations (O1=0.532, O5=0.428) support sharing of the unpaired electron between donor and acceptor oxygens. At the QCISD geometry the transferred H is closer to OH, r(O1-H6)=1.117 A versus r(O5-H6)=1.219 A, and a secondary H2...O3 hydrogen bond is 2.071 A. | formic acid + hydroxyl radical double-proton-transfer TS3: TS3 is a symmetric six-member-ring C2v doublet transition structure for simultaneous double proton transfer: acidic H transfers from formic acid to OH while the OH hydrogen transfers to the carbonyl oxygen, producing no net chemical reaction. Its 2B1 symmetry keeps the unpaired electron in an out-of-plane orbital mainly localized on the hydroxyl-radical oxygen, so the unpaired electron does not participate in the proton transfers. Both C-O distances are equal (about 1.264 A at the non-CASSCF comparison geometry), reflecting pi redistribution.

Main Table 3 gives displayed CASSCF(6,6) occupations 1.974, 1.697, 0.306, and 0.025 for HOMO, SOMO+1, SOMO-1, and LUMO.

CAS(2,2) overestimates the magnitude because it isolates the dominant SOMO-SOMO overlap while omitting balanced spin-polarization/dynamic-correlation effects. The model is a radical-pair/intermediate covalent bond rather than a conventional closed-shell dimer. | A, CAS(6,6): The larger CAS worsens agreement with experiment because inclusion of only part of the pi manifold is unbalanced; the authors caution that CAS(6,6) remains insufficient for spin polarization and electron correlation. CASPT2 is discussed only as a future correction on an infeasible CAS(26,26), not as a performed result.

electronic_structure_description: At CASSCF(12,12), the leading closed-shell configuration contributes 82.7% for cis and 82.0% for trans; the largest deviations of natural occupations from 0 or 2 are only about 0.13, so the multiconfigurational analysis does not support the proposed high diradical character. Shifted CASPT2 at the CASSCF geometries predicts the strongest visible transitions at 3.00 eV/413 nm for cis and 2.77 eV/448 nm for trans, consistent with assignment of the observed 425- and 460-nm matrix bands. Spectra at the CASSCF geometries agree better than those at B3LYP structures.

Although the restricted B3LYP trans solution is unstable and unrestricted optimization lowers it by 1.7 kcal/mol with spin contamination, CASSCF occupations and configuration weights argue against substantial ground-state diradical character. The planar-NH2 constraint costs only 0.13 kcal/mol (cis) or 0.24 kcal/mol (trans) at B3LYP and does not materially change the Ph-NOO geometry. Triplet nitroso-oxide thermochemistry was B3LYP/composite-method work, not a separate CASSCF system.

active_space_protocol: CASSCF energies were evaluated for stationary structures 1-5, 7-9, and 11. No CASSCF value was produced for cyclic structures 6 and 10 because ring formation turns two pi_y orbitals into a new sigma bond, so the authors judged that the same active space could not be defined consistently. For bent triplet 1, single-reference SDCI+Q was checked by four- and nine-reference pi-space SDCI+Q; vertical 3A'' to 1A'/1A'' excitations use CASSCF(6,7), while SDCI uses CASSCF(6,6) natural orbitals.

electronic_structure_description: CASSCF places triplet bent HCCN structure 1 lowest and overestimates the linearization gap at 6.56 kcal/mol; dynamic correlation reduces it to 1.39 kcal/mol at single-reference SDCI+Q and 2.1 kcal/mol in the nine-reference calculation. Final SDCI+Q relative energies for structures 1-11 are 0.0, 1.39, 25.0, 31.2, 35.8, 7.74, 13.8, 22.7, 24.6, 38.5, and 57.5 kcal/mol. CASSCF vertical excitations from bent 3A'' to 1A' and 1A'' are 0.95 and 1.33 eV; SDCI+Q gives 0.93 and 1.11 eV. The near-degenerate pi-like HOMOs retain carbene-like pi character on bending.
Other: All eleven fixed-composition stationary structures, connectivity arrangements, spin states, and bent/linear reaction-path points are consolidated as one HC2N system. Only structures 1 and 2 received frequency calculations: 1 is a minimum, whereas linear 2 has a doubly degenerate 481i-cm-1 bending mode; the other nine may include unrecognized transition states. Zero-point/thermal corrections nearly erase the enthalpic linearization barrier (0.0-0.7 kcal/mol), while the free-energy estimate is 1.2-1.9 kcal/mol. The inability to carry one CAS through ring formation makes CASSCF and final SDCI+Q ladder values methodologically nonuniform for structures 6 and 10.

geometry_source: B3LYP/6-31G* and CASSCF/6-31G* optimizations/frequency characterizations of ground-state reactant/products, triplet and singlet biradicals, conformers, and transition states; B3LYP IRC for one transition state
method: CASSCF(4,4), CASSCF(6,6), and CASSCF(8,8) mechanistic calculations compared with unrestricted/restricted B3LYP
active_space_orbital_description: For triplet t3 conformers, CAS(4,4) contains pi/pi-star of the newly formed C1-C2 pi bond and sigma/sigma-star of C2-C3; CAS(6,6) adds sigma/sigma-star of C1-O; CAS(8,8) further adds the C3- and N-centered nonbonding orbitals carrying the odd electrons. For [2+2] t2 formation, CAS(6,6) contains sigma/sigma-star of the forming C3-C4 bond, the C2/C5 odd-electron orbitals, and pi/pi-star of C2-C3. For [3+2] path a it instead includes forming N6-C4 sigma/sigma-star, C2/C5 radical orbitals, and C2-C3 pi/pi-star; path b uses forming C3-C4 sigma/sigma-star, C5/N6 radical orbitals, and the same C2-C3 pi pair.
active_space_protocol: The four t3 conformers were explicitly checked with nested CAS(4,4), (6,6), and (8,8) spaces; relative ordering is stable except that the largest space increases the penalty for d-t3. Production reaction-path stationary points and singlet-triplet gaps use CAS(6,6). The source describes optimized state-specific stationary points and does not report state averaging or multiple roots in one optimization.
nroots_per_mult: one targeted singlet or triplet root for each reactant, biradical, conformer, or transition structure
electronic_structure_description: CASSCF(6,6) places the hydrogen-shifted triplet t3 6.81 kcal/mol below t1 and gives adiabatic 1-to-t1 and 1-to-t3 excitation energies of 59.37 and 52.56 kcal/mol. Across CAS(4,4)/(6,6)/(8,8), doubly hydrogen-bonded a-t3 remains the lowest of four t3 conformers; b-, c-, and d-t3 lie 3.16, 26.60, and 16.77 kcal/mol above it at CAS(8,8). For ethylene addition, CASSCF(6,6) transition barriers are 13.2-13.9 kcal/mol on the t1 [2+2] channel; on the t3 [3+2] channel, N attack (16.0-16.3) is lower than C3 attack (18.4-18.8). Optimized singlet biradicals lie much higher (18.3-21.1 relative to the corresponding triplet reactant-plus-ethylene references), leading the authors to favor triplet cyclization.
Other: The photoexcited quinone, t1-to-t3 hydrogen shift, four t3 conformers, six ethylene-attack conformers per channel, all transition structures, singlet/triplet biradicals, fragmentation alternatives, and three final cycloadduct connectivities are consolidated as one overall fixed-reactant reaction system. Important caveats: the paper calls unrestricted-B3LYP singlet biradicals with <S^2> near 1.0 'pure singlets,' although a spin-pure singlet has <S^2>=0; those broken-symmetry DFT states are substantially spin contaminated. No spin-orbit coupling, minimum-energy crossing seam, or ISC rate is computed, so the claim that intersystem crossing is impossible follows only from energy differences. The conclusion that gauche-out is always most stable is also not supported uniformly by the CASSCF tables: for t2 and path-a t4, the CASSCF intermediate energies are lowest for anti, while only the t2 formation barrier slightly favors gauche-out. Ground-state product stabilization energies (-20.7, -2.6, +1.7 kcal/mol) are B3LYP-only and not separate entries.

CASSCF/CASPT2 calculations are single points on DFT geometries.
method: M06-2X, BP86, and B97D geometry/frequency calculations followed by CASSCF and CASPT2 spin-state energetics and vertical spectra; Cholesky-decomposed two-electron integrals
software: Gaussian 09 for DFT; MOLCAS 7 for CASSCF/CASPT2

active_space_orbital_description: Primary spin-state space: eight Ni(II) 3d electrons plus two electrons in an equatorial porphyrin-N sigma-donor combination, distributed over five predominantly Ni 3d orbitals, their five diffuse 4d-like double-shell partners, and the porphyrin-N sigma orbital. The ESI plots every orbital. A CAS(12,12) test adds both equatorial and axial sigma-donor orbitals to the double d shell in five-coordinate species. The optical CAS(10,8) instead contains four porphyrin/PAPy bonding pi or N-lone-pair orbitals and four antibonding orbitals, omitting metal-centered excitations.
active_space_protocol: CAS(10,11)/CASPT2 single points compare singlet and triplet roots of trans-sqp, trans-spy, and cis-spy on M06-2X geometries. CAS(12,12) checks the singlet-triplet splittings of the two five-coordinate conformers without unbalancing the four-coordinate complex. A separate state-averaged CAS(10,8)/CASPT2 treatment gives the spin-allowed vertical spectrum of trans-sqp; four reported excited singlet states describe the Q/near-UV region. All conformers, coordination numbers, spin roots, dissociation-scan geometries, active-space tests, and DFT variants are consolidated into this one chemical row.
nroots_per_mult: One low-spin singlet and one high-spin triplet per coordination conformer for spin energetics; at least four singlet vertical excited roots in the CAS(10,8) spectrum
electronic_structure_description: Four-coordinate square-planar Ni(II) has paired d8 electrons and a singlet ground state, whereas axial pyridyl coordination narrows the 3dz2/3dx2-y2 gap and stabilizes a triplet square-pyramidal state. Dispersion-driven porphyrin-PAPy stacking mixes the accepting porphyrin pi-star and azo pi-star character. The calculated Q-band promotion therefore weakens N=N and can trigger trans-to-cis isomerization, after which pyridyl-N coordination locks the high-spin form. Intersystem crossing is part of the proposed mechanism, but no explicit spin-orbit matrix elements are computed.
Other: M06-2X places cis-spy triplet at 0.00 eV, trans-spy at 0.28, trans-sqp at 0.42, trans-sqp-open at 0.72, cis-sqp at 0.91, and cis-sqp-open at 1.32. CAS(10,11)/CASPT2 energies relative to cis-spy triplet are: trans-sqp singlet/triplet 0.26/0.39 eV, cis-spy singlet/triplet 1.07/0.00, and trans-spy singlet/triplet 1.32/0.29; CAS(12,12) preserves the five-coordinate ordering. Trans-spy pyridine dissociation is nearly barrierless, while cis-spy rises by 0.84 eV at Ni-N=3.3 A, excluding a stable all-trans switching mechanism. The two lowest CAS(10,8)/CASPT2 Q-band excitations are 2.59 and 2.65 eV with oscillator strengths 0.0370 and 0.0560 and populate mixed porphyrin/azo antibonding orbitals. A direct azo pi-to-pi-star root is near 7.25 eV at SA-CASSCF and suffers severe CASPT2 intruder states, so it cannot explain 500-nm switching.
reference_short: Alcover-Fortuny, de Graaf, and Caballol, Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. 17, 217-225 (2015)

active_space_protocol: Present CASVB wave functions are exact transforms of the single active space CAS(4,4). The quantitative excitation benchmarks use a double active space CAS(4,8), adding a second pi set, followed by MRMP; the cis geometry is also optimized with CAS(4,8). Trans/cis isomers and their state-specific roots are consolidated because the paper's central result is their directly paired electronic comparison.
electronic_structure_description: The ground state is predominantly the Kekule covalent coupling with smaller Dewar and ionic contributions. The covalent 2 1Ag/2 1A1 state reverses this balance and is predominantly Dewar-like, representing coupled local triplet excitations and bond-order inversion. The bright 1 1Bu/1 1B2 state is purely ionic in CASVB, with no covalent structures. MRMP(4,8) vertical energies are 6.31 eV (trans 2 1Ag), 6.21 eV (trans 1 1Bu), 6.30 eV (cis 2 1A1), and 5.59 eV (cis 1 1B2); corresponding CASSCF(4,8) values are 6.67, 7.73, 6.56, and 6.88 eV.
Other: MRMP predicts trans-butadiene 2.76 kcal mol^-1 below cis. Covalent excitation is essentially isomer-insensitive (6.31 versus 6.30 eV), but folding the chain stabilizes the ionic state by 0.62 eV (6.21 versus 5.59 eV) because oppositely charged termini approach; the leading cis ionic VB combination has occupation 0.2146. Oscillator strengths are 0/0.803 for trans 2Ag/1Bu and 0.004/0.337 for cis 2A1/1B2. Experimental bright-state values are about 5.92-6.25 eV trans and 5.5 eV cis. Ground CASVB occupations quoted in the discussion include Kekule 0.3960 and two major ionic pairs 0.1970/0.1812. These resonance terms are wave-function components, not distinct compounds.

method: CASSCF active-space/basis benchmarks; Davidson many-body CASMP2 and Roos CASPT2; ROHF/UHF-MP2, QCISD, QCISD(T), and G2//QCI comparisons; electron-density topology
software: HONDO-95 for CASSCF/CASMP2; MOLCAS-3 for CASPT2; Gaussian 94 for MP2/QCI/G2; AIMPAC for density topology

active_space_protocol: The study compares full-valence neutral CAS(13,8), three alternative compact CAS(9,6) definitions, and enlarged CAS(9,11). The chosen CASSCF-a CAS(9,6) has irreps (2,0,2,2), 18 configurations, and is the reference for CASMP2/CASPT2; CASSCF-b CAS(9,11) has (4,1,3,3), 19,070 configurations, and explicitly restores Br 4d-O 2p backbonding. electronic_structure_description: Compact CASSCF-a is unbalanced: four active orbitals are doubly occupied, one singly occupied, and only one antibonding orbital is empty, yielding neutral Re=1.789 angstrom and omega=603 cm^-1. Adding five Br 4d correlators gives CASSCF-b Re=1.740 and 709 cm^-1, close to experiment, because 4d occupations reach about 0.016 and recover d-p/pi-p backbonding. CASMP2/ECT+(2df) gives neutral 1.726 angstrom/720 cm^-1 and BrO- 1.828/598; CASPT2 with Br 3d correlation gives 1.722/715. Experiment is approximately 1.720/727 for neutral and 1.814/575-620 for the anion.
Other: BrO-/BrO detachment or ionization energies are 21.0 kcal mol^-1 at CASSCF-a, 34.0 at CASSCF-b, 51.8 at CASMP2/ECT+(2df), 50.5-50.6 at CASPT2, 50.3 at QCISD(T), and 54.3 experimental: variational orbital completion fixes structure but dynamic correlation remains essential for energy. BrO- 3Pi is repulsive at CASSCF but dynamically correlated methods find a long-bond minimum: CASMP2 Re=2.398 angstrom, omega=284 cm^-1, binding 14.4 kcal mol^-1; QCISD(T) gives 2.473/181. The ground anion bond has lower critical-point density/ellipticity than neutral. Diffuse functions shift structure little but change the detachment energy by about 15%; correlating Br 3d changes Re by 0.005 angstrom but reaction energies by under 0.4 kcal mol^-1.

Spin-orbit coupling was not included: experimental 2Pi3/2-2Pi1/2 structure/frequency differences (0.013 angstrom/14 cm^-1) are comparable to residual theoretical errors, and an estimated BrO energy correction is -2.2 mEh. software: HONDO-95 for CASSCF/CASMP2; Gaussian 94 for MP2/QCI/G2; AIMPAC for topology

relativistic_treatment: ECP/all-electron basis comparisons; explicit relativistic and spin-orbit effects omitted.
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF-a contains the selected valence sigma/pi, lone-pair, and antibonding orbitals needed for the O-Br-O doublet/singlet-anion wave functions. The paper does not enumerate a triatomic electron/orbital count, so no scalar CAS is inferred from the BrO definition.
active_space_protocol: State-specific CASSCF-a references were used for neutral 2B1 OBrO and anion 1A1 OBrO-, followed by Davidson CASMP2. Neutral/anionic leading CASSCF configuration coefficients are 0.936/0.958, demonstrating stronger static correlation in the neutral. Large-basis QCISD(T) is used for frequencies because analytic CASMP2 triatomic gradients were unavailable.

electronic_structure_description: Neutral OBrO has substantial configuration mixing (leading CASSCF coefficient 0.936, close to ozone's 0.903), so HF/MP2 structures and frequencies vary strongly. CASSCF-a/ECT(2d) gives 1.682 angstrom/118.9 degrees and 769/703/282 cm^-1; CASMP2 gives 1.674/117.1. Best QCISD(T)/ECT+(2df) gives 1.659/115.2 and asymmetric/symmetric/bend frequencies 850/786/308 cm^-1, within about 10 cm^-1 of gas/matrix data. The anion is less multiconfigurational; CASMP2 gives 1.756/115.9, while QCISD(T)/ECT+(2df) gives 1.739/112.9 and 698/680/266 cm^-1.
Other: Adding an electron populates an antibonding pi orbital, lengthening both Br-O bonds and lowering critical-point density/ellipticity. MP2/6-311+G(3df) topology gives neutral Br-O rho=0.241, Laplacian=+0.085, H=-0.235, ellipticity=0.188; anion rho=0.201, Laplacian=+0.046, H=-0.162, ellipticity=0.043. Negative energy density establishes polar-covalent bonding despite the small positive Laplacian, and OBrO bonds are stronger/more covalent than BrO. Calculated anion-to-neutral energy differences are 47.4 kcal mol^-1 CASMP2, 52.4 QCISD(T), and about 60.1-60.3 G2//QCI. Theory predicts the anion asymmetric stretch above the symmetric stretch, opposite an aqueous assignment.

point_group: no symmetry imposed; planar/aromatic starting structures, with strongly nonplanar dissociative p-isomer T1
geometry_source: Ground S0, first singlet S1, and lowest triplet T1 geometries of all three positional isomers were optimized without symmetry constraints at CASSCF(8,7)/6-311G**. method: state-specific CASSCF geometry optimization for S0, S1, and T1; CIS transition electronic dipole moments; crossed-molecular-beam photofragment translational spectroscopy with forward convolution
software: Gaussian 98 revision A.9 for CASSCF and CIS; CMLAB2/KELVIN for beam-spectrum analysis
basis_set: 6-311G** for CASSCF geometries; 6-311G* for CIS geometries and S0-to-S1 transition electronic dipole moments
active_space_orbital_description: All six aromatic ring pi orbitals containing six pi electrons plus one Cl 3p lone-pair orbital containing two electrons; the space therefore permits both ring pi-to-pi* and Cl n-to-pi* configurations.
active_space_protocol: The identical state-specific CAS(8,7) is used to optimize S0, the first singlet excited state S1, and T1 for each meta/ortho/para isomer without symmetry restrictions. The paper reports no state averaging, root weights, or post-CASSCF dynamic-correlation correction. CIS/6-311G* is a separate single-reference calculation for transition-dipole direction, not the source of the recorded CAS.

electronic_structure_description: For all isomers, S0-to-S1 shortens C-Cl and C-CH3 while lengthening the aromatic C-C framework; orbital analysis assigns the transition predominantly as pi-to-pi*. Meta and ortho T1 retain bound C-Cl bonds (figure values: meta 1.779 angstrom versus S0 1.750; ortho 1.754 versus S0 1.782). Para T1 is qualitatively dissociative: C1-Cl=3.925 angstrom, an alternative C2-Cl contact=3.636 angstrom, and the C1-Cl direction leaves the ring plane by 54.4 degrees, suggesting coupled Cl migration/bond cleavage.
Other: CIS S0-to-S1 transition-dipole/C-Cl angles evaluated at S0/S1/T1 geometries are meta 23.0/22.8/17.8 degrees, ortho 6.1/26.6/25.7, and para 54.3/54.2/63.0, matching positive experimental anisotropy for meta/ortho and negative para anisotropy. At 266 nm, meta has beta=+0.5+/-0.2 and mean translation 3.15 kcal mol^-1 (28% of available energy); para beta=-0.6+/-0.2 and 3.28 (29%). Ortho requires two channels: about 60% slow o-tolyl+Cl with beta=+0.7+/-0.2, 2.06 kcal mol^-1 (18%), and 40% fast proposed benzyl+Cl with beta=+0.1+/-0.1, 5.09 (46%). The source proposes meta predissociation through T1 or internal conversion, direct dissociation on repulsive para T1, and for the ortho fast channel pre-dissociation H transfer to 1-methylene-2-chloro-3,5-cyclohexadiene (MCC) followed by Cl loss. Ortho S0 has a reported intramolecular Cl...H contact of 2.651 angstrom, suggested to facilitate transfer.

method: full-pi CASSCF geometry and Mulliken spin-population calculations, benchmarked against ROHF, UHF, UBLYP, UB3LYP, UQCISD, RCCSD, RCCSD(T), and UCCSD(T) where computationally feasible
software: MOLCAS 4.0 for full-pi CASSCF; Gaussian 98 for ROHF/UHF/DFT/UQCISD; ACES II for coupled-cluster calculations
basis_set: 6-31G* throughout
active_space_orbital_description: For each C_nH_(n+2) odd polyenyl radical, all n pi electrons and all n carbon 2p_pi orbitals are active: one occupied/nonbonding/virtual pi orbital per conjugated carbon, including a bonding and an antibonding orbital for every paired pair of pi electrons.
active_space_protocol: Full-pi CAS(n,n): CAS(3,3) for allyl C3H5, CAS(5,5) for pentadienyl C5H7, CAS(7,7) for heptatrienyl C7H9, CAS(9,9) for nonatetraenyl C9H11, CAS(11,11) for C11H13, and CAS(13,13) for C13H15. The numeric fields are blank because no single (nel,norb) describes the homologous series. A C13H15 test showed that deleting even one occupied/unoccupied pi-orbital pair materially changed the optimized geometry, so reduced spaces were rejected and no CASSCF calculation was attempted beyond C13.
nroots_per_mult: ground doublet only; no state-averaging or root count is reported
electronic_structure_description: The full-pi CASSCF wavefunctions describe alternating positive and negative carbon 2p_pi spin polarization localized most strongly near the radical center, together with increasing C-C bond-length alternation toward the chain ends. Relative CASSCF spin populations (largest positive site normalized to 1) are C3: terminal 1.000, central -0.343; C5: C1 0.75, C2 -0.31, C3 1.00; C7: C1 0.64, C2 -0.30, C3 1.00, C4 -0.42; C9: C1 0.47, C2 -0.24, C3 0.81, C4 -0.39, C5 1.00. The CASSCF distributions are qualitatively close to RCCSD(T) benchmarks, while both DFT functionals delocalize spin too evenly and UHF is severely spin contaminated.
Other: CASSCF/6-31G* optimized unique C-C distances (angstrom) are C3 1.390; C5 1.367/1.421; C7 1.358/1.436/1.394; C9 1.353/1.445/1.379/1.412. For allyl, CASSCF also gives central C-H 1.078 angstrom, averaged terminal C-H 1.074 angstrom, and the tabulated C-C-C angle 124.7 degrees. The authors use experimental EPR hyperfine ratios through the McConnell relationship to benchmark carbon spin-density ratios: full-pi CASSCF is good qualitatively, RCCSD(T)/UCCSD(T) are closest for C3-C7, and absolute ab initio proton hyperfine constants can still be poor. CASSCF C11 and C13 results provide the largest feasible multireference benchmarks; the paper's C41H43 neutral-soliton calculations use only ROHF/UHF/BLYP/B3LYP and are therefore context, not a CAS entry. Those large-chain DFT calculations overestimate the experimental 18-carbon soliton half-width, whereas ROHF makes it too short. No spin-orbit Hamiltonian or spin-spin term is included.

active_space_protocol: CIS first requested four doublet excited states in each D2 model to identify the two lowest transitions with appreciable oscillator strength and their dominant orbitals. Separate state-specific CASSCF gradient calculations were then performed for experimental transition 1 and transition 2 at both D2 and D2h radical-cation equilibrium geometries. Active spaces were progressively enlarged until predicted Raman spectra were stable; the reported CAS(3,4) and CAS(1,3) are the smallest stable choices. The selected configurations have weights close to one.
nroots_per_mult: CIS requested four doublet excited states for convergence; two bright doublet B3 (D2) or B1u (D2h) states were selected and treated in separate state-specific CASSCF calculations.
electronic_structure_description: The open-shell radical cation has 12 pi and two n orbitals, with the two highest-energy orbitals of n type. Both strong visible states are nearly pure one-electron pi-pi* doublet transitions. In D2h, state 1 is chiefly 4b1u(beta)-to-4b2g(beta) and state 2 chiefly 4b2g(alpha)-to-5b1u(alpha); their CIS coefficients are 0.933 and 0.844. The active orbitals and nodal patterns are shown explicitly in Figure 3.
Other: CASSCF energies for the D2 model are 1.79 eV (694 nm) for state 1 and 2.97 eV (418 nm) for state 2; D2h values are 1.83 eV (678 nm) and 3.63 eV (342 nm). CIS predicts 1.97/3.53 eV in D2 and 2.03/3.49 eV in D2h, with oscillator strengths about 0.62/0.32-0.34. Experimental radical-cation bands peak near 900 and 470 nm. Ionization shifts the N-ring and inter-ring stretching fundamentals by +43 and +54 cm^-1. Of the out-of-plane modes activated only by D2 symmetry, ring mode 16a near 415 cm^-1 is predicted to be Raman-intense but is absent at both probe wavelengths, supporting D2h planarity in solution. The four H/D isotopomers are consolidated as isotopic probes, not separate compounds.
