geometry_source: Each isomer was optimized in this work at CASSCF(8,8); DH, cc-pVDZ and cc-pVTZ basis comparisons were evaluated. The paper provides skeletal drawings but no complete Cartesian or internal coordinates.
method: CASSCF; active-space variational two-electron RDM with DQG and DQGT N-representability conditions; second-order multireference perturbation theory
software: GAMESS for RHF/CASSCF/MRPT2; custom active-space 2-RDM code with RRSDP
basis_set: Dunning-Hay double-zeta (DH), cc-pVDZ and cc-pVTZ
active_space_orbital_description: All six aromatic pi orbitals plus the sigma and sigma* combinations at the two aryne radical centers.
active_space_protocol: Full molecular aryne space CAS(8,8), used identically for conventional CASSCF, DQG/DQGT variational 2-RDM and MRPT2 comparisons. DQG imposes two-particle/two-hole/particle-hole positivity; DQGT adds the partial three-particle T2 condition. Ortho/meta/para connectivities are consolidated in one chain-length row.
nroots_per_mult: one singlet ground state per positional isomer
electronic_structure_description: Multireference character grows as radical centers separate: CASSCF/cc-pVTZ HOMO/LUMO occupations are 1.83/0.17 (ortho), 1.67/0.33 (meta), and 1.23/0.77 (para). DQGT closely reproduces these values, whereas DQG overcorrelates sigma and undercorrelates pi orbitals, most visibly for para.
Other: With the DH basis, CASSCF meta-minus-ortho and para-minus-ortho gaps are 18.5 and 26.0 kcal mol^-1; DQG gives 13.8/24.4, DQGT 17.9/26.0 and MRPT2 14.0/20.5. DQG's apparent closeness to MRPT2 is described as fortuitous cancellation between N-representability overcorrelation and missing dynamic correlation. Partial three-positivity reduces relative-energy errors from roughly 4.4-4.7 to 0.5-0.6 kcal mol^-1 and absolute errors by about an order of magnitude.
reference_short: Greenman and Mazziotti, J. Chem. Phys. 130, 184101 (2009)
notes: No SI is cited or found. Three positional isomers are kept together to avoid over-splitting the paper's chain-length comparison; their connectivity-specific results remain explicit. For model 2, 6-s-cis PSB has lambda_max 385 nm at SA-CASSCF, 392 nm at MRCI and 393 nm after Davidson correction; 6-s-cis-11-cis gives 387, 394 and 395 nm. The corresponding RPA values are 405 and 406 nm. Longer model 4 gives MRCI values of 493 and 497 nm for the same two isomers, demonstrating the large red shift with conjugation length.

RPA and MRCI differ by at most about 3% in the reported benchmarks, motivating RPA for the much larger real chromophores. The benchmark also shows why truncated models are hazardous: adding conjugated double bonds lengthens nominal single bonds, shortens double bonds through delocalization and shifts absorption strongly. The full retinal/SB/PSB structures, vibrational frequencies, isomer stabilities, torsional frontier-orbital curves, solvent microclusters and full-system absorption maxima are B3LYP, MP2, CIS or RPA results—not CASSCF/MRCI—and are not represented as separate multireference rows. electronic_structure_description: Furan is closed-shell 1A1. Direct C-O opening gives triplet 3A'' L-furan (structure 4) 322 kJ mol^-1 above furan at CASPT2/0 K and singlet biradical structures near 370-371 kJ mol^-1; the lowest singlet is sigma1pi1 rather than the higher closed-shell carbene-like sigma2 state. The viable minor channel proceeds through 1,2-H-transfer TS20 (280), cyclic singlet carbene 21 (264), ring-opened singlet biradical 23 (309), and C-C fission TS24 (352) to ketene+acetylene (225 kJ mol^-1). The dominant channel proceeds through alternative H-transfer TS25 (288), cyclic carbene 26 (279), formyl-allene intermediates 28/30 (130/118), and concerted TS31 (279) to CO+propyne (129). All values are CASPT2/cc-pVTZ plus CASSCF ZPVE relative to furan at 0 K.
Other: The direct singlet/triplet ring-opening routes have only about 0.1/7.6 s^-1 upper-bound rates at 1400 K and are excluded from the kinetic model. The ketene+acetylene cyclic-carbene route is 234 s^-1 and the formyl-allene route 629 s^-1 at 1400 K; their multistep Arrhenius fits are approximately 1.5x10^15 exp(-344 kJ mol^-1/RT) and 5.94x10^13 exp(-294.1 kJ mol^-1/RT) s^-1. Formyl allene decomposes overwhelmingly to CO+propyne rather than HCO+propargyl. A separate formyl-propyne route has TS34 at 356 kJ mol^-1 and only 2.8 s^-1. Methyl abstraction has 73/76 kJ mol^-1 0-K barriers to 2-/3-furyl, a combined 9.7x10^13 exp(-96.9 kJ mol^-1/RT) rate, and explains methane despite 506/514 kJ mol^-1 furan C-H bond enthalpies. The fitted model uses 82 reactions and reproduces shock-tube furan/major-product profiles; it slightly changes the dominant initiation activation energy from 294.1 to 292.9 kJ mol^-1, lowers the minor-channel A factor from 1.5x10^15 to 9.0x10^14 s^-1, and lowers the abstraction activation energy by 9 kJ mol^-1. CASPT2 underbinds triply bonded products, overestimating CO+hydrocarbon and ketene+acetylene reaction enthalpies by about 25-30 kJ mol^-1 versus experiment, so G2(MP2) is better for those closed-shell thermochemical balances. Conversely, CASPT2 is preferred at biradical/bond-fission structures where Q1 is large and single-reference methods collapse or disagree.

electronic_structure_description: Against experimental transition energies of 19 531, 23 474, 25 707, 28 090 and 33 222 cm-1 from the 6A1g ground term, bare CASSCF with the minimal CAS(5,5) gives 24 968, 28 969, 30 527, 36 137 and 40 044 cm-1; NEVPT2 reduces these to 20 388, 25 248, 27 584, 30 603 and 36 512, and SORCI to 18 064, 23 006, 26 528, 28 995 and 34 389. NEVPT2 on the larger CAS(9,12) gives 19 375, 23 891, 26 638, 29 992 and 36 014 cm-1 - close to the CAS(5,5) NEVPT2 values. The semi-empirical exchange charge model gives 19 718, 23 692, 25 584, 28 748 and 32 626. AILFT parameters: Dq = 814 cm-1 at CASSCF and 796 at NEVPT2 against an experimental 750; Racah B = 1088 and 923 against 820, C = 3933 and 3655 against 3150, with free-ion B0 = 1138 and 978 against 960 and C0 = 4092 and 3696 against 3325, the reduction being the nephelauxetic effect of covalence. The spin-orbit constant, obtainable only from CASSCF, is 314 cm-1 in the crystal and 322 for the free ion against experimental 320 and 335. The g factor is 1.99980 at CASSCF, 1.99972 at NEVPT2, 1.99961 at SORCI, 2.00162 by sum over states and 2.0001 by perturbation theory, against a measured 2.0009.
Other: Enlarging the active space from five orbitals to twelve, in exactly the way the standard prescription advises - adding the ligand eg orbitals and the second d shell - moves the NEVPT2 transition energies hardly at all, and the authors give the reason: the oxide ligands are barely covalent, and ligand orbitals matter most for covalent ligands. compound_name: 5-diazo Meldrum's acid (DMA) photochemical Wolff-rearrangement network: DMA, diazirine, carbene I, and ketene I
geometry_source: DMA S0/S1 minima, the S2/S1 and S1/S0 conical intersections, and diazirine were optimized at 3SA-CASSCF(12,11)/6-31G*; carbene-I boat/chair and ketene I were optimized at 3SA-CASSCF(10,8)/6-31G*. The dynamics used full-dimensional on-the-fly CASSCF energies/gradients from Wigner-sampled initial conditions in the gas phase. The attached XYZ is the source's DMA-S0 minimum.
method: Three-state-averaged CASSCF with global-switching on-the-fly trajectory surface hopping; production dynamics at 3SA-CASSCF(12,11)/6-31G*, with 3SA-CASSCF(10,8) for the N2-loss carbene/ketene stationary structures; MRCI+Q and MS-CASPT2 single-point validation
software: MOLPRO 2009.1 for electronic-structure calculations; authors' in-house global-switching dynamics program
active_space_orbital_description: Production CAS(12,11): four pi and three pi* orbitals of the six-membered ring, one diazo-group pi/pi* pair, and the C2-N9 sigma/sigma* pair. The detached-N2 carbene-I and ketene-I stationary structures instead used CAS(10,8); the source does not enumerate that smaller space orbital by orbital.
active_space_protocol: S0, S1, and S2 were averaged together in 3SA-CASSCF(12,11) for all DMA/diazirine minima, both conical intersections, and every on-the-fly trajectory energy and gradient. MRCI+Q and MS-CASPT2(12,11) single points checked those CASSCF profiles. After N2 loss, carbene-I boat/chair and ketene-I used 3SA-CASSCF(10,8), with corresponding MS-CASPT2(10,8) and MRCI checks. The different spaces belong to one connected reaction-network protocol and are consolidated in this row, not split into geometry or correction-stage rows.
electronic_structure_description: At the DMA-S0 geometry, vertical S1/S2 energies are 3.71/6.24 eV at CASSCF, 3.45/5.73 eV at MS-CASPT2, and 3.50/5.80 eV at MRCI. At the S2/S1 conical-intersection geometry, the S1/S2 energies are 4.02/4.02 eV at CASSCF, 3.60/3.73 eV at MS-CASPT2, and 3.65/3.77 eV at MRCI; at the S1/S0 intersection they are 2.52/2.52, 2.29/2.49, and 2.36/2.42 eV, respectively. The reported MS-CASPT2 stationary-point energies are DMA-S0 0.00, DMA-S1 2.34, S2/S1 intersection 3.67, S1/S0 intersection 2.39, and diazirine 1.73 eV; on the separately referenced N2-loss surface, carbene-I boat is 0.00, chair -0.42, and ketene I -2.06 eV. Among 196 S2-launched trajectories, 135 returned to DMA, 6 formed diazirine, 3 formed ketene concertedly, and 52 formed ketene stepwise through carbene I (35 formed carbene in S1 and 17 in S0). Corresponding branch ratios are 68.9%, 3.1%, 1.5%, 17.9%, and 8.7%. Fitted S2 population-decay components are 17 +/- 2 and 67 +/- 2 fs; S1 components are 62 +/- 6 and 182 +/- 14 fs. Mean pathway times are 200 +/- 50 fs for return to DMA, 120 +/- 70 fs for diazirine, 180 +/- 80 fs for concerted ketene, 500 +/- 120 fs for the S1-carbene stepwise route, and 500 +/- 130 fs for the S0-carbene route.
Other: The active space was chosen mechanistically rather than by a bare size rule: it contains both ring pi channels, the diazo pi bond, and the breaking C-N sigma pair, allowing one SA-CASSCF reference to follow S2-to-S1 relaxation, the extended S1/S0 conical-intersection seam, N2 loss, and product branching. The authors benchmarked the production CAS(12,11) topology against an earlier CAS(10,9) study and checked every key geometry with both MS-CASPT2 and Davidson-corrected MRCI. Those correlated energies generally lower the corresponding CASSCF excitation energies by about 0.25 eV while preserving the relevant gaps, which the authors use to justify CASSCF dynamics; correlated-level trajectories were not run, so that dynamical robustness is inferred rather than directly sampled. CAS(10,8) is used only for the detached-N2 carbene/ketene stationary structures and is not presented as an active-space sensitivity test. The global-switching algorithm uses an improved Landau-Zener probability and avoids explicit nonadiabatic-coupling vectors. The central physical result is that the extended S1/S0 seam, especially whether C2-N9 is longer or shorter than about 1.7 A at hopping, separates excited-state versus ground-state carbene formation and makes the stepwise ketene channel dominant over the synchronous concerted channel.

active_space_orbital_description: The baseline ten-orbital construction begins from the five 3d orbitals on each Mn center. As proton-coupled electron removal proceeds, the optimized spaces change to include singly occupied ligand ring-pi orbitals and, in structures 4-5, oxyl oxygen-p orbitals; structures 6-7 include the O-O pi* orbital plus ring-pi and Mn-d orbitals. Structure 5 required CAS(4,6) because the last four orbitals in a ten-orbital attempt had low occupations. ESI Figs. S5-S6 show the structure-2 octet CAS(7,10) orbitals and the excluded doubly occupied core d orbital 69.
active_space_protocol: Initial orbitals were generated and reordered case by case from ROHF, valence virtual orbitals, Boys/symmetry-localized orbitals, or combinations thereof. CAS(8,10) was physically selected for resting structure 1, with test spaces expanded through 12, 14, and 16 orbitals by adding ligand ring-pi/pi* and bridging-hydroxo orbitals; the added occupied orbitals retained NOONs of at least 1.95-1.98 and were therefore returned to the doubly occupied space. Structures 2-7 then used electron-count-adjusted CAS(7,10), CAS(6,10), CAS(5,10), CAS(4,6), CAS(6,10), and CAS(6,10), respectively. A CAS(7,7) test for structure 2 removed three nearly empty orbitals and retained the sextet ground-state ordering. MRMP2(7,10) used the corresponding CASSCF wavefunctions and optimized geometries for structure 2.

electronic_structure_description: All intermediates have multiple low-lying spin states. CASSCF relative energies in kcal mol^-1 are: structure 1 nonet 0.000, septet 0.020, quintet 0.028, triplet 0.035; structure 2 sextet 0.000, quartet 0.056, octet 0.333, doublet 0.414 (MRMP2: 0.000, 0.002, 0.014, 0.017); structure 3 triplet 0.000, singlet 0.012, quintet 0.071, septet 0.276; structure 4 doublet 0.000, quartet 0.285, sextet 5.805; structure 5 single-point singlet 0.000, triplet 0.002, quintet 0.466, while state-specific optimizations put triplet 0.009 below singlet; structure 6 triplet 0.000, quintet 0.488, singlet 0.793, septet 3.156; structure 7 triplet 0.000, quintet 0.353, singlet 0.395, septet 2.278. Low-spin states become increasingly competitive after oxyl formation, so nominally spin-forbidden high-spin pathways may be accessible on nearly degenerate surfaces.
Other: The orbital analysis identifies ligand participation throughout the PCET cycle. Hydrogen removal in structure 2 promotes one ring-pi orbital to single occupation while a Mn-d orbital drops into the doubly occupied core. Both ring-pi orbitals are singly occupied in structure 3. Structures 4 and 5 exhibit Mn(IV)-O radical, rather than Mn(V)=O, character through singly occupied oxyl-p contributions; structure 5 contains two such moieties. O-O coupling in structure 6 produces a filled sigma bond and singly occupied O-O pi* orbital, an approximately 1.5 bond order, and an O-O distance of 1.283 A. Structure 7 retains the singly occupied O-O pi* orbital during water-assisted Mn-O cleavage. The changing ring-pi occupations correlate with out-of-plane ligand bending and the butterfly-like structure 6. CASSCF total energies of different intermediates are explicitly not compared because their optimized active orbitals differ; the reaction-energy profile shown in the paper is ROHF/ZAPT2 context.

The lowest SO-NEVPT2 Tb 5D4 component is 22306.68 cm-1, only 2011 cm-1 below antenna T1; the paper's abstract, diagram and conclusion assign back-energy transfer and simultaneous ligand/Tb emission. Complete 7F6-0 and 5D4 crystal-field component energies are retained in ESI Tables 2-3. Antenna phosphorescence is about 0.36 s-1, with about 92% vibronic intensity. One main-text sentence says BET 'cannot occur' for this complex, but that contradicts the abstract, pathway diagram, immediate simultaneous-emission explanation, and conclusion; the entry follows the consistently stated BET assignment and preserves this source inconsistency in notes.

Its photochemical branch contains singlet/triplet 2-furoylnitrene and 2-furylnitrene states, but individual roots, intermediates, transition states, intersections, and products are consolidated as one reaction-network system
Other: CASPT2 vertical excitations of 1-S0 are S1 4.00 eV (f=0.0008), S2 4.79 (0.1988), S3 5.07 (0.0010), and S4 5.10 (0.1334); the first bright value is close to experiment (4.66 eV). Thermal Curtius rearrangement is concerted (1.86 eV barrier versus 2.33 eV stepwise), whereas photoexcited 1-S1 at 3.12 eV takes the stepwise N2-loss path over only 0.05 eV to 2-S1, then decays through 2-(S0/S1)x to nitrene 2-S0 or isocyanate 3-S0. Furoylnitrene 2 has a 0.10 eV singlet-triplet gap; 2-furylnitrene 4 has triplet 0.56 eV below open-shell singlet and a 0.17 eV route to cyanoacrolein. SOC at 2- and 4-(S0/T1)x is 1.00 and 0.24 cm-1

method: Full-valence CASSCF correlation-energy decomposition compared with a Hartree-Fock-node/fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo (FNDMC) decomposition. RHF/UHF stability energies supply the spin-symmetry-breaking correction Delta; CCSD(T) extrapolated to the CBS limit approximates exact reference energies. Natural-orbital dynamic/non-dynamic correlation indices were evaluated with CASSCF and FCI, and Slater-Jastrow FNDMC used a single RHF determinant node. Published all-electron FCI and CASSCF energies were shifted to the ccECP energy scale for the cross-method comparison.
software: GAMESS for CASSCF/FCI and natural-orbital indices; Gaussian 09 for RHF/UHF and CCSD(T); QMCPACK for FNDMC
basis_set: CASSCF(14,8) and CASSCF(14,16)/cc-pVQZ; CCSD(T)/CBS extrapolation from cc-pVXZ (X = 3,4,5) with ccECPs; FNDMC RHF orbitals in aug-cc-pVTZ with ccECPs and a 0.0025 au time step. Published all-electron CASSCF/FCI values were adjusted by the all-electron-to-ECP RHF energy difference.
relativistic_treatment: Correlation-consistent ccECPs replaced atomic cores in the CCSD(T)/CBS and FNDMC reference calculations; the paper does not present this as a separate relativistic correction.
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(14e,8o) contains the full F2 valence space. CAS(14e,16o) adds one correlating partner orbital for every orbital in the original eight-orbital valence space.
active_space_protocol: Source-explicit full-valence-versus-extended comparison: CAS(14,8) is crowded, with effectively one empty orbital and maximum excitation degree two for 14 electrons, so it under-recovers non-dynamic correlation toward dissociation. CAS(14,16) adds a complete correlating partner shell and recovers more correlation, but that extra recovery is dominated by unwanted dynamic correlation at shorter distances. The authors judge CAS(14,8) the less inaccurate space for correlation-energy decomposition, not a generally converged electronic-structure space.
nroots_per_mult: Ground-state dissociation/stretching curve only; no state averaging or excited roots are reported.
electronic_structure_description: RHF/UHF instability appears above about 1.4 angstrom, and the HF-node non-dynamic fraction rises toward roughly 50% of total correlation at dissociation. CAS(14,8) follows the qualitative growth but lies below the FNDMC non-dynamic reference in the stretched region because its active space is too restrictive. CAS(14,16) lowers the total energy substantially but exceeds the reference non-dynamic component at all sampled distances, producing non-negligible hidden dynamic correlation, especially at short F-F separations.
Other: F2 shows why lower variational energy is not automatically better for a CASSCF-based dynamic/non-dynamic partition: the double-shell CAS(14,16) is more correlated but less clean as a non-dynamic reference, while CAS(14,8) is undercomplete at dissociation yet less contaminated overall. Both active spaces and the full bond scan are consolidated into one physical-system row.

XMS-CASPT2 overestimates saddling while all the DFT functionals underestimate it. active_space_orbital_description: largest space CAS(32,34): the entire porphyrin pi system plus the orbitals of CAS(14,18); progression of four spaces detailed in active_space_protocol
active_space_protocol: A four-space progression that is itself the key result. CAS(8,11): five Fe 3d orbitals, five correlating d' (double-shell) orbitals and one sigma(Fe-N) bond. CAS(12,15): adds the four Gouterman pi frontier orbitals, shown to be crucial for stabilizing the triplet over the quintet. CAS(14,18): NOT an extension of (12,15) - instead it adds four Fe 4s4p orbitals and the remaining three sigma(Fe-N) bonds on top of (8,11), deliberately omitting the Gouterman pi orbitals. CAS(32,34): the largest, containing the entire pi system together with the CAS(14,18) orbitals. CAS(32,34) is too large for conventional CASSCF, so Stochastic-CASSCF optimized its orbitals. Active-space design for transition-metal spin gaps, stated explicitly: small CASSCF-optimized spaces are CAS(6,5) - the five Fe 3d orbitals with six electrons - and CAS(6,10), which adds the five correlating d' (double-shell) orbitals to capture 3d double-shell correlation. Large spaces (over 30 electrons in 30+ orbitals) are built from DCSD natural orbitals whose occupations deviate strongly from 0 and 2, with the explicit requirement that both spin states get a similar space - if an orbital type matters for one spin state it is included for both, so the states are balanced. FCIQMC then supplies the CI vectors inside these large spaces to tailor the distinguishable-cluster/coupled-cluster amplitudes.
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 3Eg (triplet), stabilized over 5A1g (quintet). Quintet-triplet spin gap dE = E(Q) - E(T), a few kcal/mol with the triplet below the quintet. At CAS(32,34): tailored TDCSD-F12a and TCCSD(T)-F12a both give 5.8 kcal/mol; recent Stochastic-MRCISD on the same CAS(32,34) (correlating 96 electrons in 159 orbitals) gives 6.8 kcal/mol; CCSD(T)-embedded CAS(32,34)+dF12 gives 5.7 and DCSD-embedded 3.6 kcal/mol. Largest doubles amplitude in CAS(32,34): 0.242 (LS/triplet) and 0.221 (HS/quintet) - much more multiconfigurational than the octahedral complexes.
Other: The clearest active-space lesson in the paper: the entire porphyrin pi system must be in the space to stabilize the triplet ground state. Smaller CASs erroneously predict a quintet ground state; only once the full pi system is included (via the Gouterman orbitals and ultimately CAS(32,34)) does the correct triplet-below-quintet ordering emerge, already at the Stochastic-CASSCF level, and tailoring plus F12 enlarges the gap further. Small active spaces demonstrably reduce tailored-method accuracy here - fixed amplitudes in a small space shrink the TCCSD(T) gap far below CCSD(T) - so large active spaces are indispensable when multiconfigurational character is high. All the large-CAS(32,34) tailored methods agree with each other to within a fraction of a kcal/mol.

electronic_structure_description: Singlet ground state with the triplet 17.9 kcal/mol higher (CCSD(T)/CBS(T-Q)). formula: He; N2; O2; F2 among others
geometry_source: equilibrium geometries for the absolute energies; dissociation curves for the dissociation-energy errors
method: CBS[H], a basis-set-incompleteness correction that dresses the electronic Hamiltonian with an effective short-range electron-electron interaction, based on a local mapping between the Coulomb operator projected onto a finite basis and a long-range error-function interaction with a local range-separation parameter; unlike the earlier correction of Giner et al. it uses no short-range correlation density functionals. active_space_protocol: helium: HF, CAS(2,5)SCF and CAS(2,14)SCF references. The active spaces for the molecular test set are not stated in the main text.
electronic_structure_description: Basis-set-incompleteness corrections to the helium correlation energy (mHa), CBS[H] / DBBSC / exact, against the exact energy of -2.903724 Ha. With a CAS(2,5)SCF reference: DZ -8.3 / -9.5; TZ -3.7 / -3.7; QZ -1.8 / -1.6; 5Z -1.0 / -0.9; 6Z -0.6 / -0.5, exact -3.5, -1.3, -0.6, -0.3 for TZ through 6Z. With CAS(2,14)SCF: DZ -16.1; TZ -3.3 / -3.6; QZ -1.5 / -1.8; 5Z -0.8 / -1.0; 6Z -0.6 / -0.5. With HF: DZ -9.0 / -12.3; TZ -3.9 / -5.1; QZ -1.9 / -2.3; 5Z -1.1 / -1.3; 6Z -0.7 / -0.8. From cc-pVTZ onward the CASSCF-based CBS[H] correction agrees with the exact value to within 0.2 mHa and stays sub-millihartree (at most 0.5 mHa) for larger bases; both corrections are nearly independent of the reference CASSCF wave function, as they should be, while HF-based errors exceed 0.5 mHa. The poor cc-pVDZ performance is attributed to projecting the short-range interaction operator onto the Hilbert space spanned by that basis. For the molecular set, CBS[H]-corrected AC0 and NEVPT2 correlation energies in a basis of cardinal number X (from X = 3) approach the uncorrected values in the (X+1) basis, so triple-zeta corrected results match uncorrected quintuple-zeta ones. CBS[H] works equally well for AC0 and NEVPT2. In cc-pVTZ the DBBSC-corrected relative energies stay within 1.5 mHa for every molecule while N2 is a clear CBS[H] outlier; conversely for O2 and F2, AC0-CBS[H] reaches 0.5 mHa at triple-zeta where DBBSC exceeds 1 mHa. In cc-pVDZ-F12 the CBS[H] relative-energy errors are smaller on average than in standard cc-pVDZ, and NEVPT2-CBS[H] there approaches uncorrected NEVPT2 in cc-pVTZ-F12.

electronic_structure_description: The electronic coupling VAB is 0.072 eV for the high-spin basal-plane dimer and 0.065 eV for the high-spin c-direction dimer, dropping to 0.010 eV for the low-spin basal-plane case. Since the couplings are similar in magnitude between the two processes, the three-orders-of-magnitude difference in mobility comes entirely from the reorganization energy, which is what the geometry rather than the active space determines. The contrast with hematite is the paper's own control: there, hole and electron mobilities are comparable.

geometry_source: computational and experimental combined: the Fe-Cb and Fe-CO distances were optimized at the CASPT2 level by stepwise energy scans with 0.01 and 0.02 A steps and parabolic interpolation, with all three Fe-CO distances kept equal and every other parameter fixed at the crystallographic values. First-order relativistic mass-velocity and Darwin corrections were included, and a basis set superposition error correction was applied in the (12,12) optimization. Optimized Fe-Cb 1.790 A, 1.783 A with the relativistic correction and 1.82 A with the BSSE correction; Fe-CO 1.797 A and 1.786 A. The BSSE-corrected Fe-Cb distance is about 0.03 A longer than the electron-diffraction value and 0.05 A longer than the X-ray value, while the CASPT2 Fe-CO distance is close to experiment.
software: MOLCAS-3 for the CASSCF and CASPT2 calculations; Gaussian 94 and GAMESS for the RHF, UHF and CAS(10,10) geometry optimizations
basis_set: ANO in MOLCAS: (17s12p9d) contracted to [6s4p3d] for iron, (10s4p3d) to [3s2p1d] for carbon and oxygen and (7s) to [2s] for hydrogen, with the carbon 1s and the iron 1s, 2s and 2p orbitals frozen in CASPT2. In the Gaussian and GAMESS calculations a Dunning-Huzinaga valence double zeta basis was used for C, O and H, with the argon core of iron replaced by a Hay-Wadt effective core potential and its double-zeta valence basis, one d polarization function of exponent 0.75 on the cyclobutadiene carbons and an additional diffuse d function on iron
active_space_orbital_description: twelve electrons in twelve orbitals. Ten of them follow a published general rule for transition metal compounds: the two singly occupied iron 3d(xz) and 3d(yz) orbitals paired with the two singly occupied cyclobutadiene pi orbitals, and the three doubly occupied 3d orbitals - dxy, dx2-y2 and dz2 - each paired with a combination of a 4d correlating orbital and a CO orbital. The remaining two are the lowest and highest cyclobutadiene pi orbitals, added to obtain the correct ordering of the singlet states. CAS(12,12) natural orbital occupation numbers, bonding against antibonding partner: 1.977/0.025 for the cyclobutadiene pair, 1.929/0.070 for dz2 with a CO combination, 1.924/0.073 for dx2-y2, 1.921/0.078 for dxy, and 1.895/0.107 and 1.894/0.107 for the two Fe-Cb pairs.
active_space_protocol: (10,10) following the general transition-metal rule - five 3d orbitals each with a correlating partner - used for the geometry optimization; (12,12) adding the two remaining cyclobutadiene pi orbitals, required for the correct ordering of the singlet states
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: closed-shell singlet, though the restricted Hartree-Fock wavefunction is unstable over a wide range of Fe-Cb distances. The lowest broken-symmetry unrestricted solution dissociates to triplet cyclobutadiene plus triplet Fe(CO)3; higher broken-symmetry solutions break symmetry within the cyclobutadiene ring as well and correspond to excited wavefunctions dissociating to singlet fragments. The CASPT2 binding energy of Fe(CO)3 to cyclobutadiene is 95.7 kcal/mol relative to square triplet cyclobutadiene and 90.3 kcal/mol relative to the rectangular singlet. The rotational barrier of the Fe(CO)3 group against the ring is exactly zero at RHF, UHF and CASSCF, in agreement with experiment and with extended Huckel predictions that such barriers should be very small for M(CO)3 fragments on even-membered carbon rings. The CAS(12,12) occupations show that correlation in the Fe-CO bonds is almost as important as in the Fe-Cb bond, and that correlation within the cyclobutadiene ring is the least important of the three.

The restricted Hartree-Fock wavefunction of the complex is unstable over a wide range of iron-cyclobutadiene distances, and the unrestricted solutions break symmetry in the Fe-Cb bond, localizing electrons on the iron and on the ring. The author's conclusion is stated flatly: the Hartree-Fock orbitals that break symmetry are the ones that should be in the CASSCF active space, and the lowest-energy broken-symmetry solution shows the most important non-dynamical correlation in the molecule. The evidence is that the broken-symmetry natural orbitals and the CAS(10,10) natural orbitals have very similar contours and come out in the same ORDER, and that feeding the broken-symmetry natural orbitals in as CASSCF starting orbitals gives very good convergence - the CAS-UNO procedure. The occupation numbers show the difference between the two descriptions clearly: the broken-symmetry solution over-polarizes, giving 1.595/0.404 for the Fe-Cb pair where the CASSCF gives 1.894/0.107, but it puts the right orbitals in the right order. Two orbitals then have to be ADDED beyond that rule: the remaining pair of cyclobutadiene pi orbitals, needed to get the ordering of the singlet states right, giving (12,12) - even though their own correlation contribution is small, with occupations of 1.977 and 0.025. The CASSCF Fe-CO distance is much longer than experiment, which the author attributes to the basis set and to the absence of dynamic correlation; the CASPT2 values are close. electronic_structure_description: Two minima are found lying on entirely different potential energy surfaces, corresponding to short-bond and long-bond isomers of the same spin state and symmetry, so interconversion cannot proceed over a single barrier on one surface. At CASSCF(8,6) and NEVPT2(8,6) the two curves cross at several points, indicating avoided crossings; at MRCI-CASSCF(8,6) they cross at a distance shorter than either minimum, leaving two complete separate pathways, which the authors attribute to the larger number of configurations included. Wiberg bond indices give a Be-Be bond order above one, so the bonding is multiple; the short-bond isomer has the higher vibrational frequency, consistent with its stronger bond. The triplet state is more stable than the singlet at the DFT level but shows no bond-stretch isomerism.

geometry_source: a hybrid quantum-mechanical / molecular-mechanical cluster representing the reconstructed surface, the two parts joined by the SIMOMM link-atom scheme and the cluster edges saturated with hydrogen; the reaction is followed as a scan in the O-O distance
method: CASSCF on the quantum region of a QM/MM cluster, used because breaking the O-O bond passes through a region of near-degenerate levels that a single-determinant treatment distorts
basis_set: the authors' N21-3** set for the production calculations, with N31-6** used as a check
relativistic_treatment: none
active_space_orbital_description: two electrons in two orbitals - the bonding and antibonding pair of the O-O bond being broken
active_space_protocol: the minimal space for a single bond dissociation, and the paper's justification for it is a convergence test rather than an argument: the barrier and the reaction energy were recomputed for four small bare clusters - the two-atom dimer clusters with each combination of silicon and germanium, and a nine-silicon cluster - at both this space and a four-electron, four-orbital one, and in both basis sets. The barriers move by at most 0.09 eV between spaces in the smaller basis and by 0.04 eV in the larger, except for one mixed cluster where the four-orbital space with the smaller basis is an outlier. The reaction energy is more sensitive, changing sign for the nine-atom cluster. What the test establishes is that the two-orbital space suffices for the barrier, which is the quantity the paper reports.
electronic_structure_description: Chemisorbed dioxygen lying across the addimer, dissociating by O-O bond scission with an activation barrier of 0.18 eV. The three addimer compositions give barriers within 0.04 eV of one another - 0.18, 0.17 and 0.14 eV for the germanium, mixed and silicon dimers - so the composition of the dimer barely matters. On the bare, unembedded dimer clusters the corresponding barriers are 0.39 to 0.49 eV in the same basis and space.

What the calculation then shows is that the barrier is not a property of the adsorbate or of the dimer's composition at all - all three compositions give the same value within 0.04 eV - but of the embedding: removing the surface strain by computing the bare dimer cluster more than doubles it. The authors read the composition-independence as evidence that the dissociation is electron-transfer driven.

notes: The chemisorption step that precedes dissociation releases about 6 eV and is non-dissociative; only the subsequent O-O bond breaking is computed here. electronic_structure_description: Chemisorbed dioxygen lying across the addimer, dissociating by O-O bond scission with an activation barrier of 0.17 eV. The three addimer compositions give barriers within 0.04 eV of one another - 0.18, 0.17 and 0.14 eV for the germanium, mixed and silicon dimers - so the composition of the dimer barely matters. On the bare, unembedded dimer clusters the corresponding barriers are 0.39 to 0.49 eV in the same basis and space.
Other: The two-orbital space is doing the one thing a single determinant cannot: following the O-O bond through the region where its bonding and antibonding levels become near-degenerate, which the authors identify as the source of the geometric distortions that uncorrelated calculations produce along this path. The authors read the composition-independence as evidence that the dissociation is electron-transfer driven.

compound_name: the octahedral FeH6 4- complex ion, the transition metal hydride unit of the Mg2FeH6 crystal
ligand_set: six hydride ligands in an octahedron, with the surrounding crystal represented by a Madelung field
point_group: Oh, with the calculations carried out in the D2h subgroup for technical reasons
geometry_source: the Fe-H distance optimized at each computational level; the rest of the crystal represented by the Madelung field of the infinite Mg2FeH6 lattice, computed by placing the whole negative charge at the metal and then iteratively redistributing it over the complex according to a Mulliken population analysis
method: SCF, CASSCF and contracted CI, with a multireference analogue of the Davidson correction added to the CI energies to account for higher excitations
basis_set: the SDZC set (1) of Tatewaki and Huzinaga for the metal, with the 3d and 4s shells each split into two functions and one diffuse p (0.09242 for iron) and one diffuse d function added. The metal 1s, 2s, 3s, 2p and 3p core orbitals are frozen in their atomic shape and not optimized in the MCSCF
active_space_orbital_description: two spaces were used. The first has only the bonding and antibonding orbitals of Eg symmetry active - four electrons in four orbitals, specified in D2h as (1,1,1,1,1,1,1,0 / 4,0,0,0,0,0,0,0) for inactive and active orbitals per irreducible representation. The second adds the nonbonding d orbitals of T2g symmetry and their d* counterparts, giving ten electrons in ten orbitals, (1,1,1,0,1,0,0,0 / 4,0,0,2,0,2,2,0)
active_space_protocol: the larger space was not planned but diagnosed: the CI calculation on top of the four-electron CASSCF showed that excitations from the nonbonding T2g d orbitals to d* orbitals were important, so a second CASSCF was run with those orbitals active as well. The authors describe this as bringing some pure atomic correlation into the CASSCF itself. Both CI calculations correlated all 18 valence electrons and used four reference configurations
electronic_structure_description: With 18 valence electrons the ion is very likely a closed-shell 1A1g ground state, and the calculations confirm it. The Fe-H distance shortens systematically with correlation: 1.69 A at SCF, 1.63 with the four-electron CASSCF, 1.59 after CI on those orbitals, 1.60 with the ten-electron CASSCF and 1.56 after CI on those - the last identical to the value from neutron diffraction on the Mg2FeH6 crystal. The iron d population rises in parallel from 8.1 to 8.5. The agreement with experiment on both the bond distance and the totally symmetric vibrational frequency supports the model of the crystal as negatively charged metal-hydride complexes in a magnesium ion framework, with the conventional +2 magnesium charge giving the complex a 4- charge.
Other: A textbook instance of letting the CI tell you what the CASSCF space is missing. The first space contains only the Eg bonding and antibonding pairs, the obvious choice for a covalent metal-hydride bond; the CI built on it then reveals large excitations out of the nonbonding T2g d orbitals, so those and their virtual partners are promoted into a second CASSCF. The effect on the answer is not in the CASSCF distance - 1.63 versus 1.60 A - but in what the subsequent CI can do with it: 1.59 A from the small space against 1.56 A from the large one, and only the latter matches neutron diffraction. Note also what carries the crystal here: not a larger cluster but a Madelung field, iterated on the charge distribution, with the same field used for every geometry whenever conformations are compared.
reference_short: Lindberg, Noreus, Blomberg & Siegbahn, J. Chem. Phys. 85, 4530 (1986)

compound_name: the FeH6 2- complex ion, the alternative charge state of the Mg2FeH6 hydride unit
ligand_set: six hydride ligands in an octahedron, embedded in a Madelung field computed for a 2- charge on the complex, corresponding to Mg+ rather than Mg2+
point_group: Oh, calculations carried out in D2h
geometry_source: the Madelung field for this case determined from a charge distribution with -2 on the iron centre
method: SCF, CASSCF and contracted CI with a multireference Davidson correction
basis_set: Tatewaki-Huzinaga SDZC set for iron with split 3d and 4s shells and added diffuse p and d functions; metal core orbitals frozen in atomic shape
active_space_orbital_description: the same construction as for the 4- complex - bonding and antibonding metal-hydride orbitals, extended by the nonbonding T2g d orbitals and their d* partners - applied to a complex with two fewer electrons, so the two removed electrons come out of one of the t2g, a1g, eg or t1u orbitals
active_space_protocol: the space follows the 4- complex; what changes is the electron count and hence which configurations compete for the ground state
electronic_structure_description: Ligand field theory places the nonbonding t2g orbitals highest and so predicts a triplet ground state from a t2g^4 configuration, and the calculations confirm it: the states arising from eg, a1g and t1u configurations lie more than 150 kcal/mol above 3T2g. Because a triplet complex would not be diamagnetic, the 2- charge state is excluded for the iron compound, leaving the conventional Mg2+ picture with a 4- complex.
Other: The value of this row is negative evidence, and the space is what makes it usable. Because the same active orbitals are used as for the 4- complex, the 150 kcal/mol separating the t2g^4 triplet from the eg, a1g and t1u alternatives is a comparison between states described on equal footing rather than an artefact of tailoring a space to each configuration - which is what lets the paper rule the 2- charge state out on the strength of the observed diamagnetism. Contrast the nickel compound in the same study, where the 2- charge state cannot be excluded and turns out to be the interesting case.

compound_name: the square-planar NiH4 2- complex ion, the transition metal hydride unit of the Mg2NiH4 crystal in its 16-valence-electron charge state
ligand_set: four hydride ligands, compared in square-planar, slightly twisted (10 to 20 degrees) and pseudotetrahedral (90 degree twist) arrangements, embedded in a Madelung field
point_group: D2 for the twist-angle comparison; D2h for the bond-distance optimizations of the planar structure
geometry_source: twist angle scanned at fixed Ni-H distance of 3.07 a.u.; Ni-H distance then optimized for the planar complex at each computational level, in a field computed by placing the whole 2- charge on the nickel atom
method: CASSCF followed by contracted CI correlating all 16 valence electrons, with three and two reference configurations respectively for the two CI sets
basis_set: Tatewaki-Huzinaga SDZC set for nickel with the 3d and 4s shells each split into two functions, one diffuse p (0.1122) and one diffuse d function added; metal core orbitals frozen in atomic shape
active_space_orbital_description: three spaces were used for the planar complex. The first has all the Ni-H bonds and their antibonding partners active together with the d and d* orbitals of A1g symmetry, since that d orbital mixes slightly with the bonding orbital of the same symmetry: (1,0,0,0,0,1,1,0 / 4,2,2,2,0,0,0,0). The second has only the bonding and antibonding in-plane d orbitals active, a four-electron space. The third extends the second to all five pairs of d and d* orbitals: (1,1,1,0,0,0,0,0 / 4,0,0,2,0,2,2,0)
active_space_protocol: the three spaces separate two different correlation effects deliberately - bond correlation, through the Ni-H bonding and antibonding pairs, and atomic d correlation, through the five d/d* pairs - so that their contributions to the bond distance can be read off independently
electronic_structure_description: For the singlet the planar structure is the most stable, 16 kcal/mol below the 90-degree twisted form at CI level, though the potential surface is very shallow near planarity - twisting by 10 degrees costs only 0.5 kcal/mol and by 20 degrees only 2.0. At 90 degrees the 3B3 triplet lies below the planar singlet by 4.6 kcal/mol at CASSCF level. The Ni-H distance is 1.60 A with the four-electron space, unchanged at 1.60 A when the three pairs of bonding and antibonding orbitals involving Ni 4s and 4p are added, 1.57 A after CI on those orbitals, 1.57 A directly from the CASSCF with all five d/d* pairs active, and 1.56 A after CI on those. The nickel d population stays near 9.1 to 9.2 throughout. A NiH4 2- complex is a formal Ni(II) species and would be square planar, comparable to the square-planar PtH4 units found in K2PtH4 and Na2PtH4; the 18-valence-electron NiH4 4- complex, formally Ni(0), would instead be tetrahedral. A 2- complex implies a +1 charge on magnesium, unexpected but possible if magnesium retains an electron in a conduction-band-like state, which could also explain the compound's residual paramagnetism.
Other: The three-space design is what makes this a useful data point rather than just a number: adding the Ni 4s and 4p bonding pairs to the four-electron space changes the bond distance by nothing at all, while adding the five atomic d/d* pairs changes it by 0.03 A - so for nickel the shortening comes from atomic d correlation, not from bond correlation. The contrast with the iron complex in the same paper is explicit and is the paper's own summary: for nickel, including atomic d correlation already at the CASSCF level has essentially no effect on the final CI bond distance, whereas for iron it does. Note also the failure recorded next door: for the 18-electron NiH4 4- complex, CASSCF calculations to correlate the bonds ran into convergence problems at the tetrahedral geometry and were abandoned, so that species was treated at SCF and CI only.
reference_short: Lindberg, Noreus, Blomberg & Siegbahn, J. Chem. Phys. 85, 4530 (1986)
notes: system_class cluster-model: a complex ion in a Madelung field standing in for the Mg2NiH4 crystal. metal_ox_state and d_electron_count left empty: the paper calls this formally a Ni(II) complex but reports a Mulliken d population near 9.1, and warns that Mulliken analysis is unreliable here. active_space_nel and active_space_norb record the ten-electron spaces; the smaller four-electron space is described in active_space_orbital_description. The NiH4 4- complex from the same paper gets no row: CASSCF would not converge for it and only SCF and CI were performed. software not stated.

geometry_source: geometry optimized by ab initio molecular dynamics simulated annealing at both GVB and CASSCF levels, followed by constant-temperature AIMD runs to assess pseudorotation; the pseudorotation pathway also optimized
method: ab initio molecular dynamics with generalized valence bond (GVB) perfect pairing and CASSCF wavefunctions; vibrational frequencies computed for the resulting structures
active_space_orbital_description: the CASSCF wavefunction includes all doublet-state configurations of the five valence electrons in five orbitals. The GVB wavefunction places four of those electrons in two GVB pairs, each described by two natural orbitals with perfect singlet pairing, and the fifth in a singly occupied orbital, so the GVB wavefunction contains a subset of the configurations present in the CASSCF.
active_space_protocol: (5,5) full valence for CASSCF; GVB perfect pairing as a strict subset of the same configuration space
electronic_structure_description: The Li5 cluster is found to have a planar structure and pseudorotates on a picosecond or faster timescale at temperatures as low as 77 K. It is therefore likely that the pseudorotating Li5 observed in earlier EPR experiments at 77 K is planar rather than the trigonal bipyramid originally suggested.
Other: Because the GVB wavefunction is a strict subset of the (5,5) CASSCF configuration space, running the dynamics at both levels isolates exactly what the extra configurations contribute to the pseudorotation - a cleaner comparison than benchmarking against an unrelated method. | Five valence electrons in five orbitals is the whole valence space of an alkali pentamer, so this is a genuinely complete treatment rather than a truncation, which is what makes the structural conclusion against the experimental trigonal bipyramid assignment worth making. | The result is dynamical, not just structural: pseudorotation on a picosecond timescale at 77 K means the EPR experiment sees an averaged structure.

The number of active electrons was set to four, corresponding to the two Si-Si bonds of the sigma-conjugated system. All three silicon 1s core orbitals were frozen as determined by the ground-state SCF. The reference wavefunction and orbitals came from an average CASSCF over all the 1A1, 1B2, 1A2 and 1B1 states of interest

electronic_structure_description: Ground term: closed-shell singlet in C2v. Three states of valence character are found below the first Rydberg state at 7.20 eV - contradicting the previous assignment and meaning the first broad band in the observed spectrum is entirely valence in character. The dipole-forbidden transitions to the 1 1A2 and 4 1A2 states lie at 6.89 and 8.52 eV. The 4s, 4p and 3d members of the Rydberg series converging to the first ionization potential fall between 7.20 and 8.62 eV, and those converging to the second between 7.82 and 9.61 eV. Only MS-CASPT2 reproduced the observed excitations accurately, because only it separated the valence and Rydberg states effectively.
Other: A striking ratio: four active electrons in fifteen active orbitals. The electron count is fixed by the chemistry - the two Si-Si sigma bonds of the sigma-conjugated backbone - while the orbital count is set by what the excited states need to reach, namely the Si-Si sigma*, Si-H sigma* and the whole 4s/4p/3d Rydberg manifold. That asymmetry is the design, not an accident, and it is why the paper can address valence-Rydberg mixing at all. The methodological finding is that having the space is not sufficient: average CASSCF over these states mixes Rydberg and valence character strongly (as it had for n-tetrasilane), single-state CASPT2 does not fix it, and 'only the MS-CASPT2 method gave an accurate description of the observed electronic excitations since it provided an effective separation of the valence and Rydberg states'. The consequence for the chemistry is a reassignment: three valence states lie below the first Rydberg state, so the first broad absorption band is entirely valence, not Rydberg as previously assigned. Two supporting details worth copying - the 2s2p2d Rydberg functions are placed at the charge centroid of the CATION ground state, not the neutral, and a 0.05 level shift removes intruder states at a cost of under 0.1 eV in the excitation energies.

point_group: C1 (gauche and anti biradical structures; C2v/Cs only at the closed ring)
geometry_source: CASSCF optimized: CAS(8,6)/6-31G* routinely, CAS(12,10)/6-31+G* for the improved surface, and GVB-CAS(12,12)/6-31G* where the (12,12) space is too large for CASSCF optimization. Crossing points located with the conical-intersection algorithm in Gaussian 94, which optimizes the lowest point on the (n-2)-dimensional intersection hyperline; state-averaged orbitals were used for both the intersection optimizations and the spin-orbit couplings.
method: CASSCF, GVB-CAS, and multireference MP2 single points (CASMP2 by the method of Peasley et al. for the (8,6) and (8,8) spaces; CASPT2 by the method of Roos for the (12,10) space)
basis_set: 6-31G* for the routine CAS(8,6) and GVB-CAS(12,12) work; 6-31+G* for CAS(12,10); cc-pVDZ for recomputed CAS(8,6) barrier heights
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(12,10) = the minimal (8,6) space (Chart 1) extended by the C-O sigma/sigma* orbitals (Chart 2). Related spaces used in the same paper: (8,6), the stated minimum needed to describe the topology of the surfaces; (12,12), obtained by adding a pair of 'virtual' n* orbitals to (12,10); (8,8), the (12,12) space minus the sigma/sigma* orbitals, used for MP2 single points on GVB-CAS(12,12) geometries; and (4,4), the (8,6) space without the doubly occupied oxygen orbitals, used for frequencies.
active_space_protocol: Deliberate hierarchy rather than one space. An (8,6) space is stated to be the MINIMUM needed to describe the topology of the surfaces, and its energetics can be corrected by CASMP2 single points — but CASMP2 gradients are unavailable, so improving the GEOMETRIES requires enlarging the space instead, which is why the C-O sigma/sigma* orbitals were added to give (12,10). The further (12,12) space (adding two virtual n* orbitals) is too large for CASSCF geometry optimization, so those structures were optimized with GVB-CAS keeping the four C-O sigma orbitals in the GVB space, and CAS(8,8)/MP2 energies (without the sigma/sigma*) were computed at those structures. Frequencies at every critical point used a (4,4) space at CASSCF/6-31G*, with (8,6) frequencies at four selected points (a, b, m, q) for the thermal corrections in Table 1. Spin-orbit couplings use a one-electron operator with the effective nuclear charges of Koseki et al. (C 3.6, O 5.6).
electronic_structure_description: Ground state S0 and lowest triplet T1, labelled by pi-electron count: the 1(4pi) singlet biradical surface, the 3(3pi) triplet biradical surface (about 2 kcal/mol below 1(4pi)) and the 2pi singlet/triplet states. Ring-opening barrier TS1 (a gauche structure, b) has an activation energy of ca. 17.6 kcal/mol uncorrected, 16.3 kcal/mol thermally corrected, against an experimental threshold of 22 kcal/mol for unsubstituted dioxetane. A syn MAXS saddle point lies some 6 kcal/mol above TS1. The lowest 1(4pi) biradical BIRS (anti, structure j) lies 9 kcal/mol below TS1 and is unstable to C-C cleavage — its fragmentation barrier could not be fully optimized. The anti minimum on the 3(3pi) surface, BIRT (structure m), lies 5-6 kcal/mol below TS1. At the best level (CAS(12,10)/6-31+G* + MP2 + thermal correction) the triplet fragmentation transition state TS2 (structure q) lies 20.3 kcal/mol above the reactant, 16.5 kcal/mol thermally corrected, so TS1 and TS2 are both about 16.5 kcal/mol. Spin-orbit coupling is large, ca. 60 cm-1, throughout the singlet/triplet crossing region, implying facile intersystem crossing along a crossing 'line' spanning the ground-state O-O cleavage valley a few kcal/mol above it.
Other: The paper is built around the fact that a bigger active space and a perturbative correction are not interchangeable here. CASMP2 on an (8,6) reference fixes the energies but cannot fix the GEOMETRIES, because CASMP2 gradients do not exist — so dynamic correlation had to be smuggled into the optimization by enlarging the space instead, adding the C-O sigma/sigma* pair to reach (12,10). Pushing further to (12,12) with two virtual n* orbitals broke CASSCF optimization entirely and forced a GVB-CAS compromise in which the four C-O sigma orbitals sit in the GVB rather than the CAS space, with the subsequent MP2 energies then computed in a (8,8) space that DROPS the sigma/sigma* orbitals again — so the (12,12) geometries and the (8,8) energies do not share an active space. A second trap: the two multireference MP2 corrections used are not the same method — CASMP2 (Peasley et al.) for the (8,6) and (8,8) spaces and CASPT2 (Roos) for (12,10), differing mainly in the zeroth-order Hamiltonian, so numbers from different rows of Tables 1 and 2 are not strictly comparable. Frequencies rest on a much smaller (4,4) space than the energies, and near surface degeneracies made some of them unreliable (flagged in the table). Even at the best level the O-O cleavage barrier converges to ~16.5 kcal/mol against an experimental 22 kcal/mol, so the remaining error is not removed by any of these active-space extensions.

notes: Reinvestigation of the classic dioxetane chemiluminescence mechanism. Cr(CO)6 was shown in earlier work to be well described by a 10/10 space built from the metal 3d orbitals and their bonding and antibonding counterparts - an occupied e_g (CO sigma) and t_2g (Cr 3d) shell and a virtual e_g (Cr 3d) and t_2g (CO pi*) shell. electronic_structure_description: Stationary points were located on the A~ 1B2 excited state surface and their geometries compared side by side against TD-DFT structures. Other: The planarity question is really a question about a stationary point's Hessian, and that is why the method matters: CIS is documented to get proton-transfer energetics wrong through missing dynamical correlation, so the shape of the surface near the C2v structure cannot be trusted from it. The CAS(10,10) over the ring pi system gives geometries, CASPT2 gives energies, and the numerical Hessian decides the character of each point. Note the acknowledged limitation that CASPT2 enters only as single points, so the surface curvature itself is CASSCF-quality.

On the triplet surface: I(Be,T) 49.3 with a much shorter M...O distance of 1.818 A; TS(Be,T) 45.9; III(Be,T) -51.2; the ionic-region minimum IV(Be,T) -3.3 and TS(Be,a,T) 13.8, giving a 17.0 kcal/mol barrier from IV. The calculated singlet barriers decrease down the group in the same order as the metal ionization potentials fall: IP(Be) 9.32 > IP(Mg) 7.65 > IP(Ca) 6.11 eV.
Other: Beryllium is the extreme of the series and shows most clearly what the constant-orbital-count space is buying. The entrance complex sits at a Be...O distance of 4.602 A on the singlet surface but only 1.818 A on the triplet — a 2.8 A difference between two states described by the same twelve orbitals, which is only possible because the space is defined by orbital index rather than by a fixed chemical picture of the bonding. The triplet entrance complex lies 49.3 kcal/mol up, so the singlet channel dominates. No previous report of the Be + N2O reaction existed, so these numbers have no independent check — worth remembering given that the analogous Mg surface came out qualitatively different from the earlier single-reference treatment.  The paper contains a direct methodological claim about why the active space matters here: an earlier MP2/CCSD(T) study of Mg + N2O found a TWO-STEP mechanism through a stable cyclic NNOMg intermediate, whereas the CASSCF(12/12) surface is a SINGLE-STEP process. The authors' reasoning is that 'at least two electronic configurations are important in the intermediate regions ... single-configuration-based methods may result in highly distorted PESs', and they point at the natural-orbital occupation numbers of the key MOs as the evidence. The physical origin is a charge transfer: passing over the barrier, the ground adiabatic state changes from a neutral configuration to an ionic one in which an electron moves from the metal s or p orbital into the in-plane 2p-pi orbital of N2O, so the wave function in the barrier region is 'dominated by both the neutral and the ionic configurations'. A space that cannot hold both descriptions at once will place the barrier and, as here, can invent or destroy an intermediate. Two cautions for reuse. First, the small CASSCF(12/12) barriers on the TRIPLET surface (I(T) -> TS(T)) disappear entirely once MRMP2 dynamic correlation is applied, so the triplet channel is barrierless and the CASSCF triplet barriers are artefacts. Second, the singlet-triplet crossing structures V(S/T) were located at CASSCF with MRMP2 energies evaluated afterwards, and the authors warn that 're-optimization of the corresponding structures at the correlated levels of theory might lower their energies with respect to the asymptotes' — so the crossing-point energies are upper bounds, and the calcium one was found with a smaller (6/6) space still.

Two features of the CAS[10,12] make that possible. The double shell of 3d' correlating orbitals is what keeps the high-spin and low-spin states balanced — without it the differential radial correlation between a t2g(6) and a t2g(4)eg(2) configuration is not recovered and any derived charge difference would be biased toward one state. The two ligand-based eg-like orbitals are what let sigma donation appear explicitly in the wave function, so that the metal charge is a computed quantity rather than an artefact of the orbital partition. The relocalization step is the second essential piece: because it is a unitary transformation it changes no observable, yet it converts the delocalized CASSCF orbitals into atomic-like ones from which valence-bond configuration weights and charges can be read directly. Other: Compound 4 is the transferability test: the same CAS[10,12] recipe is applied to a completely different coordination sphere, N4O2 rather than N6, with two oxygen donors replacing two nitrogens. Because the space is defined by symmetry and orbital character (five 3d, five 3d' correlating, two ligand eg-like) rather than by naming particular ligand orbitals, it carries over to the new donor set without modification, and the resulting Gamma of 270 K again tracks the observed hysteresis. That portability is the practical virtue of the double-shell-plus-eg construction over a hand-picked space, and it is what allows the paper to claim its strategy extends to chemical changes in the coordination sphere.  The active space here is the canonical spin-crossover construction and the paper uses it for an unusual purpose: not to compute a spin-state energy gap but to extract ATOMIC CHARGES for a Madelung-field model of crystal cooperativity. Two features of the CAS[10,12] make that possible. The double shell of 3d' correlating orbitals is what keeps the high-spin and low-spin states balanced — without it the differential radial correlation between a t2g(6) and a t2g(4)eg(2) configuration is not recovered and any derived charge difference would be biased toward one state. The two ligand-based eg-like orbitals are what let sigma donation appear explicitly in the wave function, so that the metal charge is a computed quantity rather than an artefact of the orbital partition. The relocalization step is the second essential piece: because it is a unitary transformation it changes no observable, yet it converts the delocalized CASSCF orbitals into atomic-like ones from which valence-bond configuration weights and charges can be read directly. The resulting charge redistribution is large — on iron, 1.45 in the low-spin state against 1.92 in the high-spin state for compound 1, a change of 0.47 e — and it is precisely this difference that drives the polarization term. The methodological caution for reuse is that these are single-point calculations on experimental X-ray geometries of the isolated molecular unit, so the charges carry whatever the crystal structure determination carried, and the Madelung analysis then reintroduces the environment as fixed point charges rather than self-consistently.
reference_short: Kepenekian, Le Guennic & Robert, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2009, 131, 11498
notes: Included specifically to validate the approach beyond the Fe(II)N6 family; hysteretic behaviour in N4O2 environments had been reported only recently at the time of writing. correlation_correction: None reported beyond the CASSCF itself; the 3d' double shell inside the active space supplies the radial correlation.

active_space_protocol: A single CAS[10,12] is used for every complex, and its composition is stated explicitly: '(i) the mainly Fe 3d character orbitals extended with a set of virtual orbitals of the same symmetry (so-called 3d' orbitals) and (ii) two occupied eg-like symmetry orbitals with mainly ligand character. Thus, a CAS[10,12] including 10 electrons in 12 active orbitals is used in the calculations.' That is the five 3d orbitals plus a double shell of five 3d' correlating orbitals, plus two ligand-based eg-like orbitals that carry the sigma donation. Calculations are performed on the isolated basic unit of each compound taken from the experimental low-spin and high-spin X-ray structures, not on optimized geometries. After convergence the valence MOs are relocalized into atomic-like orbitals to expose the charge-transfer contributions in the wave function expansion; this transformation leaves any observable expectation value unchanged and affords a valence-bond type analysis from which configuration amplitudes and atomic charges are derived. The paper stresses that finely balanced basis sets are necessary to describe spin-crossover energetics correctly.

geometry_source: Conformational landscape explored at B3LYP/6-31+G(d), with the four most stable conformers retained. For the excitation energies the four conformers were reoptimized at CASSCF/cc-pVDZ; SA-CASSCF optimizations of the second-root geometries provided the adiabatic S1 energies. Harmonic frequencies computed at B3LYP/6-31+G(d), B3LYP/6-31G(d,p) and B3LYP/6-311+G(2d,p) with anharmonic corrections from a single level.
method: CASSCF geometry optimization with state-averaged CASSCF and multistate CASPT2 (MS-CASPT2); B3LYP, MP2 and TD-OLYP for comparison
software: GAMESS for the DFT and MP2 geometries and frequencies
basis_set: cc-pVDZ for the CASSCF and MS-CASPT2 calculations; 6-31+G(d), 6-31G(d,p) and 6-311+G(2d,p) for the DFT and MP2 work; TZ2P(DZP) for TD-OLYP
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in eight orbitals spanning a configuration space of dimension 1764: four orbitals (bonding and matching antibonding) localized chiefly on the carbonyl part of the amide and acetyl functional groups, and four originating from the degenerate e1g and e2u HOMO and LUMO of the benzene ring of the phenylalanine side chain.
active_space_protocol: A single CASSCF(8,8) is used for all four conformers, and its content is stated orbital by orbital: 'Four of the active orbitals (bonding and the matching antibonding interactions) were localized chiefly in the region of the carbonyl part of the amide and acetyl functional groups, whereas the remaining four originate from the benzene degenerate e1g and e2u highest occupied (HOMO) and lowest unoccupied (LUMO) molecular orbitals.' The space spans a configuration space of dimension 1764 and 'effectively encompassed all of the chromophores of interest for describing a few lowest excited states'. Geometries were reoptimized at CASSCF/cc-pVDZ, then state-averaged CASSCF over the FOUR lowest equally weighted roots was performed at those geometries; SA-CASSCF optimizations of the second-root geometries gave the adiabatic S1 energies. Three separate numerical safeguards were applied at the MS-CASPT2 stage: the C, N and O 1s cores were frozen; an IMAGINARY level shift of 0.10 au removed intruder states 'emerging mostly in the first and the third excited state', after which 'the reference weights in the excited states approached to within 7% of that in the ground state (around 0.60)'; and an IPEA shift of 0.10 au — deliberately BELOW the recommended 0.25 au — was used 'to mitigate the problems of overestimating the stability of open shells in CASPT2'. Oscillator strengths combine CASSCF transition dipole moments in the length representation with MS-CASPT2 energy differences.
nroots_per_mult: 4 equally weighted roots in the state-averaged CASSCF
electronic_structure_description: The extended beta-strand conformer. CASSCF(8,8)/MS-CASPT2/cc-pVDZ excitation energies in eV with oscillator strengths (length representation, x100, in parentheses): vertical T(v) for state 1 is 4.827 (0.25), state 2 is 5.946 (5.00) and state 3 is 6.809 (88.5); the adiabatic T(0) for state 1 is 4.707. The experimental value for state 1 is 4.650 eV. TD-OLYP/TZ2P(DZP) gives a vertical energy of 5.133 eV (0.64) for the corresponding state. The dominant intensity lies in state 3, whose oscillator strength of 0.885 is more than two orders of magnitude above that of the lowest state. Geometric parameters at B3LYP/6-31+G(d), B3LYP/6-311+G(2d,p) and MP2/6-311+G(2d,p) are tabulated. Amide A band frequencies at B3LYP/6-31G(d,p), harmonic then anharmonic: NH(Phe) 3587/3403, symmetric NH2 3582/3421, antisymmetric NH2 3721/3539 cm-1. Amide I frequencies: amide I(1) harmonic 1729 with intensity 355 and anharmonic 1698 cm-1, dominated by CO(1) stretch (0.76); amide I(2) harmonic 1760 with intensity 269 and anharmonic 1732 cm-1, dominated by CO(2) stretch (0.70).
Other: The beta(a) conformer gives the best agreement with the measured origin, 4.707 eV adiabatic against 4.650 eV observed, a 0.057 eV error that is about as good as MS-CASPT2 on an (8,8) can be expected to deliver for a system this size. What makes the comparison meaningful across conformers is that the eight orbitals — four carbonyl bonding/antibonding pairs from the amide and acetyl groups, four benzene e1g/e2u frontier orbitals — are the same set at every geometry, so conformer-to-conformer differences in excitation energy reflect the hydrogen-bonding environment rather than any change in the correlated space. The spread across all four conformers is only 0.086 eV vertically, which is precisely why a consistent space matters: a differently constructed space per conformer could easily produce artificial differences of that size. The most valuable thing in this paper is that the active space is used to DISPROVE a set of states predicted by another method. TD-DFT with GGA functionals returns 14 of its 15 lowest excited states as charge-transfer states appearing in quasi-degenerate pairs, reflecting quasi-degeneracies among the phenylalanine antibonding orbitals. The authors dismiss these as artefacts with an argument that turns entirely on the space: 'These low-lying CT states must be considered illusive, knowing that the CASSCF active space comprises all of the orbitals necessary for describing them and that they are still absent from the CASSCF/MS-CASPT2 spectrum in the 4.8-7.0 eV region.' The state is absent from a calculation whose space contains the orbitals required to build it: the eight orbitals are the amide/acetyl carbonyl set plus the benzene e1g/e2u frontier pair. The reference weight is about 0.60 in the ground state, with the excited states within 7% of it. Achieving that consistency required the imaginary level shift; without it the first and third excited states suffered intruders. The reduced IPEA shift of 0.10 au against the recommended 0.25 au is a second deliberate departure, chosen because the standard value overstabilizes open shells — a reminder that the CASPT2 zeroth-order Hamiltonian is itself a tunable part of the protocol and must be reported alongside the space.
reference_short: Doslic, Kovacevic & Ljubic, J. Phys. Chem. A 2007, 111, 8650
notes: One of four low-energy NAPA conformers classified by the Ramachandran scheme. The extended beta-strand forms are contrasted with the gamma-L forms supporting a seven-membered C7 ring backbone conformation. Anharmonic corrections of -2.01, -1.92, -1.86 and -1.70 kcal/mol were computed for the four conformers. Conformer-specific experimental data come from R2PI and IR spectroscopy. correlation_correction: Multistate CASPT2 with the C, N and O 1s cores frozen, an imaginary level shift of 0.10 au and an IPEA shift of 0.10 au (reduced from the recommended 0.25 au).

compound_name: E-Azobenzene — photoisomerization from the n-pi* and pi-pi* singlets
geometry_source: Fully unconstrained CASSCF geometry optimizations and minimum energy path computations, with single-point CASPT2 on the optimized structures. Conical intersections located by minimizing the two-root state-averaged CASSCF energy in the (n-2)-dimensional intersection space orthogonal to the branching-space directions x1 and x2.
method: CASPT2//CASSCF — CASSCF optimizations and minimum energy paths with single-point CASPT2 corrections; CASSI for transition dipole moments
active_space_orbital_description: Fourteen electrons in twelve orbitals: ten pi-system orbitals and electrons plus the two doubly occupied nitrogen lone pairs.
active_space_protocol: The paper opens its active space discussion with a statement of principle — 'The active space choice is a crucial step in a CASSCF calculation' — and then gives the composition: 'our choice was to include 10 orbitals and electrons of the pi system plus the two doubly occupied nitrogen lone pairs, resulting in an active space of 12 orbitals and 14 electrons.' So (14,12): the full azo/phenyl pi manifold plus both nitrogen lone pairs, the latter being what makes the n-pi* states representable alongside the pi-pi* ones. The state-averaging protocol is layered. Geometry optimizations and minimum energy paths use single-state CASSCF 'when possible; otherwise, when root flipping problems occurred, state average calculations have been the choice'. Conical intersections are optimized by minimizing the TWO-ROOT state-averaged CASSCF energy in the (n-2)-dimensional intersection space orthogonal to the branching directions. But the reported energies come from a much broader average: 'at all the interesting geometries, a state average CASSCF procedure, with equal weights between the involved states of the singlet manifold (the first nine singlet states in E-CPD and in Z-CPD), has been used to generate molecular orbitals, energies, and the reference functions for subsequent CASPT2 calculations.' An imaginary level shift of 0.2 au was applied to all state-averaged CASPT2 computations to eliminate intruder states. Oscillator strengths combine CASSI transition moments with CASPT2 energy differences.
nroots_per_mult: Nine equally weighted singlet roots for the orbitals, energies and CASPT2 reference functions; two-root state averaging for the conical intersection optimizations; single-state CASSCF where root flipping allowed it

software: MOLECULE (integrals); ALCHEMY with ENERGY (HF and CI); a CASSCF program from the cited literature

The bond is only safely attributed to (3d)9(4s)1 at distances up to 4.2 a.u., where the CASSCF Ni configuration is still closer to (3d)9 than to (3d)8. | That same error propagates straight into the dissociation energy: the raw CASSCF value, taken as the energy difference between the equilibrium distance and 12.0 a.u., is 1.07 eV, and only after adding back the 1.28 eV atomic correlation difference does it reach 2.35 eV against the experimental 2.36. ligand_set: six oxide ions of the MnO6 octahedron, with the surrounding crystal replaced by point charges
point_group: the MnO6 unit is slightly distorted from a regular octahedron; the embedding lowers the symmetry further
geometry_source: the experimental x = 0.4, 10 K crystal structure (I4/mmm, a = 3.8645 A, c = 20.065 A), with the slight buckling of oxygens out of the a-b plane neglected; no geometry optimization
method: CASSCF on an embedded cluster, with UHF on the same cluster for comparison; natural orbitals and their occupation numbers computed from the spin-resolved first-order density matrix to characterize the wave function
basis_set: the Schaefer et al. sets, Mn (14s,9p,5d)/[8s,5p,3d] and O (10s,6p)/[6s,3p], with the most diffuse Mn s function removed because it extends too far over the neighbouring oxygens
active_space_orbital_description: the nine highest-energy oxygen 2p orbitals together with the five manganese 3d orbitals
active_space_protocol: the space is built to answer the question the paper asks: whether the oxygen orbitals that lattice models routinely omit actually matter. Including all nine high-lying O 2p orbitals alongside the full 3d shell is what lets a hole on oxygen appear if the wave function wants one, and lets the answer differ between the two charge states. The embedding is a point-charge array over 3x3x3 units of the a(bxc) cell, with +2.4 at both Sr and La sites and +3.4 at neighbouring Mn sites to represent the random occupation at x = 0.4, and the Evjen method applied at the faces, edges and vertices of the outermost cell; starting orbitals came from restricted Hartree-Fock.
electronic_structure_description: Essentially a single-configuration system: all natural-orbital occupation numbers are essentially integral, and CASSCF and UHF give almost the same charge and spin densities (Mulliken charge on Mn 2.631 with spin 3.857 at CASSCF, 2.611 and 3.889 at UHF). The highest occupied orbital is Mn d(3z2-r2). The first excited state is obtained simply by promoting an electron from d(3z2-r2) to d(x2-y2), making this a textbook E x e Jahn-Teller system.
Other: This cluster is the control case. Its near-integral occupations establish that a correlated treatment buys nothing for nominal Mn(III), which is why the contrast with the (MnO6)8- sibling - where the same active space produces heavily fractional occupations - can be attributed to the extra hole rather than to the method or the embedding.

geometry_source: transition states for both the singlet and the triplet dissociation channels located by CASSCF and MCSCF; the singlet-triplet crossing seam mapped as a function of the N2-NH distance and the NNH angle
method: CASSCF and MCSCF to locate the transition states, with the largest configurations from the CASSCF calculations then used as the reference for MCSCF-CI calculations
basis_set: 94 contracted Gaussian-type functions, of s, p and d symmetry on N and s and p on H
active_space_orbital_description: the 4a' to 12a' and 1a'' to 3a'' orbitals - nine orbitals of a' and three of a'' symmetry - holding either all 16 valence electrons or the 10 valence electrons exclusive of the N 2s electrons
active_space_protocol: a fixed twelve-orbital window (4a'-12a', 1a''-3a'') with two electron counts: all 16 valence electrons, or 10 valence electrons with the N 2s electrons left out. Running both is the point - it tests whether the nitrogen 2s correlation affects the location of the singlet-triplet crossing seam that the whole spin-selectivity argument rests on.
nroots_per_mult: the lowest singlet (1A') and lowest triplet (3A'') surfaces of HN3 and the seam between them
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: X 1A', planar at equilibrium. At the point of lowest singlet-triplet crossing the N2 and NH bond distances are identical to those in the isolated N2 and NH molecules in both X 3Sigma- and a 1Delta, so the dissociation is vibrationally adiabatic; the seam lies nearly perpendicular to the direction of steepest descent on both sides, so little rotational torque is exerted on the NH fragment, as observed. The terminal N-N and N-H bonds are nearly perpendicular at the crossing, making the energy almost independent of the dihedral angle and so preserving planarity. A barrier in the singlet channel was located at a trans HN3 geometry with angle HNN = 90 degrees and angle NNN = 165 degrees at an interior N-N distance of about 4.5 bohr, beyond the singlet-triplet crossing; it lies about 2000 cm-1 above the crossing and about 1000 cm-1 above the N2 + NH(a 1Delta) asymptote, and arises from electronic constriction - at long range the 10a' and 2a'' orbitals are equally occupied by the NH 2p electrons, but the 10a' orbital becomes unfavourable in the presence of N2 through Fermi repulsion with the N2 2p_sigma orbitals.
Other: The active space exists to locate a crossing seam, not to get an energy right, and the symmetry argument built on it is what the paper is really for: because the HN3 ground-state wavefunction and the I_z S_z term of the spin-orbit Hamiltonian are both symmetric under reflection in the molecular plane, only NH product states whose total electronic-plus-rotational wavefunction is also symmetric can be formed, so only the F1 and F3 multiplets of NH(X 3Sigma-) are populated - exactly as the infrared multiphoton dissociation experiments find. The two electron counts on the same twelve orbitals are a built-in check that the seam location does not depend on correlating the nitrogen 2s shell.
