Calculations are state-specific at the ground state; no enlargement or reduction test is reported
multiplicities_studied: doublet, the ground state, treated state-specifically
nroots_per_mult: one - the calculations are state-specific at the ground state, with no state averaging
electronic_structure_description: Doublet ground state whose wavefunction is dominated at 87 percent by the single configuration (dxy)2(dyz)2(dxz)2(sigma_eq)2(sigma_ax)2(px)1(sigma*_ax)0(sigma*_eq)0, with under five percent from any other configuration, giving a formal Co-N bond order of 1.0. The natural orbitals show exactly one sizeable Co-N bonding interaction, the axial sigma bond between Co d(z2) and N p(z) at 40 percent Co and 53 percent N. Perpendicular to it, Co d(xz) and d(yz) stay practically nonbonding with occupation numbers of 1.95 and 1.97 and 90 and 97 percent Co character. The singly occupied orbital is centred on the nitrene nitrogen p(x) at 84 percent N with an occupation number of 1.03, and the spin density reproduces its shape, giving a spin population of +0.88 on nitrogen - close enough to unity to establish an N-centred radical. The Co-N bond is correspondingly long at 1.80 angstrom, matching the well-characterized cobalt(III) imidyl [Co(TPP)(NNs)]
Other: Here the multireference overturns a density-functional orbital assignment, and the direction of the DFT error is too much covalency. For the iron-nitrene, B3LYP identifies the second singly occupied orbital as an Fe-N pi antibond, pi*(x), which would mean two Fe-N pi bonds and hence a metal-nitrido-like description. The CASSCF natural orbitals show instead that this orbital is essentially pure metal - 94 percent Fe d(xz) with an occupation number of 1.01 - and the paper states plainly that the density-functional picture 'is an overestimation of the Fe-N covalency', since two Fe-N pi bonds are not feasible for a nitrene. The conclusion is generalized into a transferable recommendation: 'DFT-based orbitals require careful interpretation and verification through multiconfigurational methods, like CASSCF for the iron-imido or imido-like complexes'. The verdict is delivered despite, not because of, strong multireference character. The leading configuration carries 87 percent weight for the cobalt doublet and 82 percent for the iron triplet, with under five percent from any other configuration in the cobalt case - by the configurational-mixing measure these are ordinary single-reference wavefunctions. What the CASSCF supplies is not a correction for static correlation but a correct set of natural orbitals and occupation numbers. The active space is targeted and itemized orbital by orbital, with the double shell built in: three metal 3d nonbonding orbitals, the axial sigma and sigma* pair formed between metal d(z2) and the nitrene nitrogen p(z), the equatorial sigma and sigma* pair formed between metal d(x2-y2) and the porphyrin nitrogens, and the nitrene nitrogen p(x) - eight orbitals doing named jobs - plus five metal 4d orbitals added explicitly 'to account for the double d-shell correlation', giving thirteen in all. The two complexes are described as 'balanced' active spaces differing only by the one electron that distinguishes them, eleven for cobalt and ten for iron. Against that, there is no dynamic-correlation step at all: no NEVPT2, no CASPT2, nothing beyond the variational wavefunction, and no enlargement or contraction test, so the occupation numbers and orbital percentages on which the whole imidyl-versus-imido-like distinction rests are uncorrected and untested. The calculations are also state-specific on the ground state only - one doublet for cobalt, one triplet for iron - so no excited state is available to check the description against, and no relativistic Hamiltonian is named. For this complex the multireference confirms rather than overturns the established picture - the imidyl assignment was already in the literature - which is what makes it the control that gives the iron result its force: the same space, the same code and the same analysis reproduce the known answer on one metal and change it on the other

point_group: C2v state labels are used throughout - A1, B1 and B2 - with the z axis taken collinear with the C-I bond

Real-time TDDFT with Ehrenfest nuclear dynamics run separately in CP2K to demonstrate dissociation explicitly
software: ORCA 5.03 for all static multireference work; CP2K for the real-time TDDFT Ehrenfest dynamics
basis_set: segmented all-electron relativistically contracted SARC-DKH-TZVP on iodine and relativistically recontracted def2-DKH-TZVP on all other atoms; a mixed Gaussian and plane-wave dual-space basis for the CP2K dynamics
relativistic_treatment: second-order Douglas-Kroll-Hess one-particle Hamiltonian with a finite-size Gaussian-like nucleus model
soc_included: yes, and it is the entire subject: spin-orbit coupling matrix elements and SOC-corrected transition moments from the DKH2-transformed spin-orbit mean-field operator including spin-other-orbit and spin-own-orbit terms with a DFT-like local correlation term, treated throughout in a quasi-degenerate perturbation theory framework
active_space_orbital_description: the recommended space is ten electrons in nine orbitals: the six benzene pi orbitals, the occupied and virtual sigma orbitals of the C-I bond, and the out-of-plane pz lone pair of iodine. Three other spaces were run for comparison - (8e,8o) with benzene pi plus the C-I sigma/sigma* pair only; (10e,9o)-LP with the in-plane px/y iodine lone pair added instead of the pz; and (12e,10o) with both iodine lone pairs - and a six-orbital benzene-pi-only space was tried and rejected
active_space_protocol: A stepwise enlargement in which every step is justified by a named failure of the previous one. The six-orbital benzene pi space suggested by TD-DFT was rejected because it gives an almost zero spin-orbit coupling matrix; the C-I sigma and sigma* pair was added because the dissociation cannot be described without it, giving (8e,8o); the iodine lone pairs were added because (8e,8o) misses low-lying states carrying very large couplings to the ground state. The paper states explicitly that these orbitals 'has to be included during CASSCF orbital optimization for efficient orbital mixing, not only in the final CAS-CI stage'. State averaging is over six low-lying singlets and nine low-lying triplets, the number 'chosen based on level spacing to include all near-degenerate energy states and provide efficient mixing in spin-coupling'
nroots_per_mult: 6 low-lying singlet roots and 9 low-lying triplet roots in every space compared
electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell aromatic iodide whose ground state is dominated by a single CAS-CI configuration with weight above 0.99 regardless of the active space chosen. With the recommended (10e,9o) space the lowest six triplets lie at 3.752, 4.876, 4.884, 5.035, 6.982 and 7.068 eV above the ground state, with averaged spin-orbit coupling matrix elements to the ground state of 0.926, 6.63, 0.106, 1286.754, 4.571 and 0.122 reciprocal centimetres - the fourth triplet, T4 of B2 symmetry, carrying a coupling three orders of magnitude larger than any other. That state is dissociative along the C-I coordinate. It cannot be reached directly from S1 B1 by intersystem crossing because of spin-orbit selection rules, but is easily populated by coupling from other triplets, the squared matrix element from T1 A1 being 4965.7 reciprocal centimetres squared. T1 A1 is stable near equilibrium but dissociative at long range. The conclusion is that iodobenzene cannot phosphoresce because every strongly spin-orbit coupled triplet sublevel leads to dissociation - confirmed by explicit Ehrenfest dynamics
Other: Four active spaces are run at fixed root set on the same molecule. Across them the excitation energy of the strongly coupled triplet moves by about half an electronvolt while its spin-orbit coupling moves by a factor of six hundred. Across the four post-CASSCF treatments at fixed space the energy moves 5.035 to 4.523 eV while the coupling moves only 1287 to 1160 reciprocal centimetres, about ten percent. Two spaces of identical size differ in one orbital: (10e,9o)-LP, which adds iodine's in-plane px/y lone pair, gives a coupling of 2.085 reciprocal centimetres for the fourth triplet, while (10e,9o)-Pi, which adds the out-of-plane pz orbital that can mix with the benzene pi system, gives 1286.754 for the same state, at the same electron count, orbital count, root set and code. Adding the second lone pair on top of the pz, to reach (12e,10o), then changes that coupling by only four percent. The space also decides which state carries the coupling: the very large matrix element sits on T4 in the (8e,8o) and pz-containing spaces but moves to T5 in the in-plane-lone-pair space, so the state ordering itself is active-space dependent. The six-orbital benzene pi space that linear-response TD-DFT points to 'leads to an almost zero-defined SOC matrix in CASSCF and all post-CASSCF methods', which would leave phosphorescence available only through spin-vibronic Herzberg-Teller coupling. Strongly contracted NEVPT2 returns spin-orbit coupling matrix elements identical to CASSCF to every printed digit - 1286.754 and 635.898 reciprocal centimetres - because a non-quasi-degenerate perturbative correction shifts state energies without touching the wavefunctions the coupling is built from; only the quasi-degenerate variant, which rotates the states, and SORCI+Q, which rebuilds the wavefunction, move those numbers at all. The ground state is over 99 percent one configuration in every one of the four spaces. On procedure, the extra orbitals 'has to be included during CASSCF orbital optimization for efficient orbital mixing, not only in the final CAS-CI stage' - enlarging the CI expansion after the orbitals are fixed is not the same thing as enlarging the active space.
reference_short: Rublev, Boldyrev & Scheiner, J. Phys. Chem. A 2023, 127, 4927-4933
notes: The heavy-atom effect does deliver a very large spin-orbit coupling here, but every triplet sublevel that carries it is dissociative along the C-I coordinate, so the molecule cannot phosphoresce. The argument is a composite of three independent pieces - multireference vertical energies and couplings, an unrelaxed potential energy scan showing the dissociative character, and RT-TDDFT Ehrenfest dynamics in a different code showing the dissociation explicitly - and the paper is clear about which piece does what. Intersystem-crossing accessibility is argued through Fermi golden rule proportionality to squared coupling matrix elements together with spin-orbit selection rules, not by computing rates. Note a printing artefact in Table 1: the row labelled S0 to T7 in the two pz-containing columns repeats the T1 values exactly and should not be read as a seventh state. The recommended production protocol is QD-SC-NEVPT2 on the (10e,9o) space with the benzene pi system, the C-I sigma and sigma*, and the pz lone pair. Three corrections are compared at fixed active space: SC-NEVPT2, QD-SC-NEVPT2 and SORCI+Q. For the strongly coupled triplet they give excitation energies of 4.966, 4.694 and 4.523 eV against 5.035 eV at bare CASSCF, and couplings of 1286.754, 1299.534 and 1159.658 reciprocal centimetres against 1286.754 - the SC-NEVPT2 value being numerically identical to CASSCF because that correction cannot alter the wavefunction from which the coupling is computed. QD-SC-NEVPT2 is the one the authors recommend.

For 3B1: re 2.4955 a0 and alpha_e 126.571 degrees with TZ, Te 12 165.341, T00 11 834.295 against 11 695 +/- 15 empirical, nu1 874.077, nu2 514.574, nu3 748.155 cm-1 against empirical 1090 +/- 80 and 555 +/- 15. method: a controlled comparison of eight electronic structure methods - SA-CASSCF, SS-CASPT2, MS-CASPT2, XMS-CASPT2, MRCI, FOMO-CASCI, MR-CISD/OM3 and SI-SA-REKS - crossed against several nonadiabatic algorithms (Landau-Zener surface hopping, fewest-switches surface hopping, AIMSWISS), to separate the influence of electronic structure from that of the coupled electron-nuclear algorithm
software: BAGEL for the CASPT2 simulations; other packages per method

active_space_orbital_description: two sigma(CC), pi(CO), n(O), pi*(CO) and two sigma*(CC)
active_space_protocol: (8,7) - two sigma(CC), pi(CO), n(O), pi*(CO), two sigma*(CC) - used for every method except SI-SA-REKS. The choice was triangulated three ways rather than assumed: previous studies of this molecule, automated selection with the AutoCAS code, and the authors' own benchmarking of potential energy surfaces and absorption spectra. Two reduced spaces appear for practical reasons: (2,4) for the cheaper ground-state sampling, and (2,2) containing only n(O) and pi*(CO) for SI-SA-REKS, which has no other space implemented. All CASPT2 calculations used a 0.5 a.u. level shift, tested to be insensitive across a wide range. Only S0 and S1 were treated, equally weighted in the SA-CASSCF state-averaging
Other: The paper's central result is that the electronic structure method matters far more than the nonadiabatic algorithm. Excited-state lifetimes across the ab initio family span nearly a factor of two: XMS-CASPT2 39 fs, MS-CASPT2 54 fs, FOMO-CASCI 58 fs, SA-CASSCF 68 fs - a spread the authors call surprising given that the underlying potential energy surfaces differ negligibly. Semiempirical MR-CISD/OM3 is fastest at 36 fs (within XMS-CASPT2 error bars); SI-SA-REKS is an outlier at 90 fs whose population transfer stops abruptly at 140 fs. CO release quantum yields: all ab initio methods agree within error bars and sit close to the experimental 0.73 (intensity-weighted average); MR-CISD/OM3 overestimates at 0.89; SI-SA-REKS fails outright at 0.20 (the authors could not reproduce the 0.44 +/- 0.11 previously published for that method). All ab initio methods find the polymerization channel at least once while the DFT and semiempirical ones never do. By contrast the coupled electron-nuclear algorithms give identical quantum yields within statistical error and consistent population transfer, with FSSH and LZSH essentially equivalent - so when conical intersections are well defined the cheaper LZSH is sufficient.

point_group: C2v (with Cs calculations for the A' and A'' roots)
geometry_source: minima and transition states located with analytic CASSCF gradients and numerical Hessians; intrinsic reaction coordinate and approximate minimum energy path calculations used to verify connectivity; intersection seams located by fitting diabatic surface regions with bicubic splines and minimizing the surface difference
method: CASSCF with analytic gradients for stationary-point optimization and numerical Hessians for characterization, refined by CASPT2 (standard correction and the G1/G2/G3 variants)

active_space_orbital_description: full valence, the same space as in Part I
active_space_protocol: Full valence CAS(17,12) throughout, matching Part I so the two mechanisms are directly comparable. Two-state-averaged CASSCF was used for the lowest two roots of each Cs symmetry (A' and A''); in C2v the first root of each of A1, B1, A2 and B2 was taken, except at the I2 intersection where the first and second roots were needed because two states of the same symmetry are involved. Dynamic correlation from CASPT2 using the G2 variant. A deliberately reduced CAS(7,6) with 6-31G(d) was used in GAUSSIAN 98 purely to identify the two coordinates defining each conical intersection - a cheap auxiliary space for a topological question rather than an energetic one
nroots_per_mult: two state-averaged roots per Cs symmetry; first root of each C2v irreducible representation
Other: High barriers were found for the direct C2v-insertion mechanism: 3.11 and 2.54 eV. These are much higher than the barriers for the indirect Cs-insertion mechanisms reported in Part I, so the direct C2v insertion is not competitive. electronic_structure_description: Open-shell HOMO-LUMO biradical formed by electron transfer from flavin to the N3'-protonated 3'base of the (6-4) photoproduct. In both cases dynamic correlation moves the answer by more than the difference between the states being compared, so no conclusion about which tautomer or intermediate is populated survives at the CASSCF(2,2) level alone. The excitation spectra are handled with a different and larger space chosen by the POCAS (principal orbital CASSCF) scheme rather than by hand, and its size is not stated in the main text — so the ground-state energetics in Tables 2 and 3 and the excitation energies discussed alongside them do not come from the same active space. A useful internal consistency check the paper does report: the two flavin hydroquinone local-excitation energies come out at 2.65 and 3.32-3.34 eV in every model with a closed-shell ground state, so the POCAS/XMCQDPT2 protocol is at least stable across cluster models.

compound_name: BeBr, 14 Lambda-S states and the 30 Omega states they generate
point_group: Cinfv, replaced by C2v for the calculations
geometry_source: potential energy curves computed point by point and fitted; spectroscopic parameters from the vibrational levels
method: CASSCF followed by internally contracted MRCI with the Davidson correction (icMRCI+Q), with core-valence and scalar relativistic corrections and CBS extrapolation; spin-orbit coupling by the state-interaction approach with the Breit-Pauli Hamiltonian
basis_set: aug-cc-pVQZ (AVQZ) for all the potential energy curves - (22s,17p,13d,3f,2g) contracted to [8s,7p,5d,3f,2g] on Br and (13s,7p,4d,3f,2g) to [6s,5p,4d,3f,2g] on Be - with AVTZ/AVQZ CBS extrapolation (denoted TQ); cc-pVTZ for the scalar relativistic correction and all-electron cc-pCVTZ for both the core-valence and the spin-orbit calculations
relativistic_treatment: third-order Douglas-Kroll Hamiltonian approximation at the cc-pVTZ level
active_space_orbital_description: nine outermost MOs (five a1, two b1, two b2) holding two valence electrons from the Be 2s orbital and seven from the Br 4s4p orbitals; the inner 30 electrons occupy fifteen closed-shell MOs (eight a1, three b1, three b2, one a2) corresponding to the 1-7 sigma, 1-3 pi and 1 delta MOs
active_space_protocol: (9,8) eight outermost MOs (4 a1, 2 b1, 2 b2) first, then (9,9) after one extra a1 MO was included. The enlargement was forced by curve behaviour, not by energetics: with eight active MOs the curves could be computed near equilibrium but broke down as the internuclear separation increased, and adding the ninth orbital made them smooth. All reported results use CAS(9,9).
nroots_per_mult: 14 Lambda-S states from the first two dissociation channels Be(1Sg)+Br(2Pu) and Be(3Pu)+Br(2Pu): eight doublets (X 2Sigma+, 2 2Sigma+, 3 2Sigma+, 1 2Sigma-, A 2Pi, 2 2Pi, 3 2Pi, 1 2Delta) and six quartets (1 4Sigma+, 2 4Sigma+, 1 4Sigma-, 1 4Pi, 2 4Pi, 1 4Delta); 30 Omega states follow with spin-orbit coupling
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: X 2Sigma+, with Te 0.0, Re 1.9508 angstrom, omega_e 715.43 cm-1 (measured 715), omega_e x_e 0.7427 cm-1, Be 0.54710 cm-1 and De 26873.58 cm-1; its leading configuration is (core) 8sigma2 9sigma2 4pi4 10sigma1 with 5pi, 11sigma and 12sigma empty, and the Omega component X 2Sigma+_1/2 has Te 0.0, Re 1.9588 angstrom, omega_e 713.72 cm-1 and De 26234.58 cm-1, 99.95 percent pure. The first well of A 2Pi sits at Te 26703.56 cm-1 (Re 1.9760 angstrom, measured 1.9765; omega_e 704.12, measured 702; De only 4503.80 cm-1) and its second well at 26776.43 cm-1 with Re 4.2907 angstrom and De 96.79 cm-1. Higher states: 2 2Pi 33726.89, 2 2Sigma+ second well 35284.57 and first well 47663.16, 1 4Sigma+ 45371.55, 1 4Delta 46691.25, 1 4Sigma- 47322.24, 1 2Delta 47367.01, 1 2Sigma- 47752.41, 1 4Pi 48721.17, 2 4Sigma+ 48791.18 and 3 2Sigma+ 48845.36 cm-1. Without spin-orbit coupling 3 2Pi and 2 4Pi are repulsive; with it 1 4Pi, 2 4Pi, 3 2Pi and 2 4Sigma+ are repulsive instead, A 2Pi and 2 2Sigma+ keep their double wells either way, and 1 4Sigma+, 1 4Sigma-, 1 2Pi and 2 2Pi are inverted.
Other: Two findings a reader choosing this space should carry away. First, the ninth active orbital exists only to keep the curves from breaking down at long range - the space was sized by dissociation behaviour rather than by energy accuracy, and the paper shows in supplementary figures what the A 2Pi, 1 4Pi and 2 4Sigma+ curves look like without the core-valence correction to make the same point. Second, which states are repulsive changes when spin-orbit coupling is switched on: the spin-free calculation calls 3 2Pi and 2 4Pi repulsive, the spin-orbit one calls 1 4Pi, 2 4Pi, 3 2Pi and 2 4Sigma+ repulsive, so a CAS(9,9) result read without spin-orbit coupling would misclassify two states. Basis convergence on the fixed space: AVDZ to AVTZ to AVQZ raises Te of A 2Pi by 736 cm-1, CBS adds 242 more, and the Davidson correction lowers it by up to 979 cm-1.
reference_short: Shi, Niu, Sun and Zhu, Mol. Phys. 112, 1670-1683 (2014)
notes: Very little experimental spectroscopy exists for BeBr and the two measured values quoted for the ground state are flagged in the source as not accurate, so most term energies here are predictions. compound_name: s-indacene, S0 and S1 minima and the S0/S1 conical intersection
point_group: D2h; all geometry optimizations were constrained to the D2h framework symmetry
geometry_source: optimized in this work: S0 and S1 minima at CAS12/cc-pVDZ, and the same minima plus the S0/S1 conical intersection at CAS6/6-31G*, all under D2h constraint. The S0 minimum has transannular bonds of about 1.448 A; on excitation to S1 those lengthen to about 1.51 A while the 7-7a bond linking the central benzene to the outer allyl fragments compresses from about 1.42 to 1.40 A, and continuing along that coordinate reaches the conical intersection. The S1 structure has two long transannular bonds near 1.5 A and a uniform perimeter near 1.4 A. For comparison, a low-temperature X-ray structure of the tetra-tert-butyl derivative gives ring bond lengths of 1.394-1.395 and 1.434 A with no significant deviation from D2h, against MP2/6-31G* values of 1.397 and 1.429 A.
method: CASSCF geometry optimization with two active spaces, plus CASPT2 single points at the CAS12 geometries correlating all electrons with no frozen core; conical intersection searches carried out at the smaller space only, since they are impractical with the full pi space. State-averaged orbitals were used for the S1 minimum and the intersection at the CAS6 level. The hybrid MMVB method - an MM2 sigma framework with the active conjugated electrons in a Heisenberg Hamiltonian over neutral valence-bond configurations, parametrized against CASSCF/4-31G - was run in parallel for comparison.
software: Gaussian for the CAS6 calculations, MOLPRO for the CAS12 calculations, and MOLCAS for the CASPT2
basis_set: cc-pVDZ for the CAS12 and CASPT2 calculations; 6-31G* for the CAS6 calculations
active_space_orbital_description: CAS12 is the full pi valence space, twelve electrons in twelve pi molecular orbitals. CAS6, six electrons in six pi orbitals, is the smallest space found capable of describing S0 and S1 simultaneously, and it was selected by inspecting the CAS12 natural orbital occupation numbers and keeping the orbitals with fractional occupations.
active_space_protocol: (12,12) the full pi valence space, used for the S0 and S1 minima and as the CASPT2 reference; (6,6) the six pi orbitals of most fractional CAS12 occupation, selected as the smallest space describing both states at once and used for the surface exploration and the conical intersection search, which is impractical with the full space
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: S0 (1Ag); the excited state is B3g. Total energies in Eh at the D2h optimized geometries, given as CAS6/6-31G* / CAS12/cc-pVDZ / CASPT2/cc-pVDZ (the last at the CAS12 geometries) for S0 then S1: at the S0 minimum -459.03542 / -459.18834 / -460.62604 and -459.00339 / -459.16651 / -460.59399; at the S1 minimum -459.02292 / -459.17929 / -460.62039 and -459.00936 / -459.17657 / -460.60331; at the S0/S1 intersection, located only with CAS6, -458.99790 and -458.99658 (state-averaged orbitals). The 0-0 excitation energies come out at 16.4 kcal/mol (CAS6) and 7.4 kcal/mol (CAS12), both below the experimental near-infrared transition of the tetra-tert-butyl derivative at about 9270 cm-1, i.e. 26.5 kcal/mol; adding dynamic correlation through CASPT2 raises every computed energy difference, bringing the 0-0 value to 14.3 kcal/mol. The intersection lies about 5 kcal/mol above the S1 minimum and about 4 kcal/mol above the Franck-Condon point on S1. The S0 structure has pronounced open-shell character - four allyl radical units coupled to an overall singlet - with HOMO and LUMO occupations of 1.59 and 0.45 at CAS12 and 1.79 and 0.22 at CAS6, close to a previously published 1.60 and 0.45; the S1 structure has singly occupied B2g and B1g orbitals. Experimentally the S1 lifetime of the tetra-tert-butyl derivative is 18 +/- 4 ps with a fluorescence quantum yield below about 1e-4.
Other: The active-space reduction here is done by an explicit and reusable criterion rather than by intuition: a conical intersection search with the full twelve-orbital pi space is impractical, so the CAS12 natural orbital OCCUPATION NUMBERS at the D2h structures are inspected, and the smallest space that still describes S0 and S1 simultaneously turns out to be the six orbitals carrying fractional occupations - six electrons in six pi orbitals. The reduction is then validated rather than assumed, by comparing CAS6 and CAS12 geometries and relative energies at the S0 and S1 minima before trusting CAS6 for the intersection search. What the comparison shows is that the reduction is safe for geometry and character but expensive in energy: the 0-0 excitation is 16.4 kcal/mol with the small space against 7.4 with the full one, a factor of more than two, and CASPT2 on the CAS12 reference moves it back up to 14.3, all against a measured 26.5 kcal/mol for the tetra-tert-butyl derivative. So both spaces underestimate the gap badly and the small space happens to land closer for the wrong reason. The deeper finding concerns the character of the states, and it is a warning about method rather than about space: MMVB and CASSCF both predict a conical intersection at a comparable place, but they assign S0 and S1 OPPOSITE character, disagreeing by nearly 100% in relative energies where the same comparison on styrene agreed to within 10%. The authors argue the CASSCF ordering is right but concede that with energy differences of a few kcal/mol a definitive answer needs a multireference treatment beyond what they did. The underlying reason the system is hard is visible in the occupations: the S0 minimum is not a closed shell at all but four allyl radicals singlet-coupled, with a HOMO occupation of 1.59 and a LUMO occupation of 0.45, which is also the accepted explanation for s-indacene's extreme reactivity.

notes: The active-space columns record CAS12, the full pi valence space and the CASPT2 reference; CAS6, used for the intersection search, is in active_space_protocol. The natural orbital occupation tables (Tables 1 and 2) are misaligned in the extracted text, so only the HOMO and LUMO occupations the running text states in words are recorded. The experimental transition energy, lifetime and fluorescence yield are for the tetra-tert-butyl derivative (TTBI), not for the parent s-indacene, and the X-ray bond lengths are likewise for that derivative. The author list is taken from a running header in the extracted text and should be checked against the original if cited precisely. formula reflects the compound's identity; the paper states only the name.

method: State-averaged CASSCF and multistate CASPT2; conical intersection and intersystem crossing point optimization; spin-orbit coupling evaluated at the ISCs with the atomic mean field integral (AMFI) approximation and an effective one-electron Fock-type spin-orbit operator
software: MOLCAS 6.2 (CASSCF, CASPT2, SOC); Gaussian 03 (conical intersection optimizations, B3LYP, MP2)

A reduced CASSCF(10,8) space was used for the surface crossings, containing all the pi-type orbitals, the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the N-N bond, and the two nitrogen lone-pair orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The paper opens the point with 'the selection of the active space is a crucial step for the CASSCF and CASPT2 calculations' and then writes the ground-state configuration out orbital by orbital before naming which entries enter the space, so the choice is fully auditable. TWO spaces are used for two purposes: the larger (14,11) for stationary points and vertical excitations, and a smaller (10,8) 'in order to get a balance between the precision and the computational cost' for locating the conical intersections and intersystem crossing points, that smaller space being defined by chemical function (all pi orbitals, the N-N sigma/sigma* pair that breaks, and both nitrogen lone pairs) rather than by energy window. The (14,11) choice is then validated against measured structure: the optimized bond parameters agree with experiment, which the authors state 'means that our selection of the active space is reliable'.
electronic_structure_description: Ground state 1(1)Ag. Vertical excitations at SA-CASSCF(14,11)/cc-pVTZ then MS-CASPT2: 1(1)Au 4.01 then 3.62 eV (f = 0.00506), 1(1)Bg 5.90 then 5.46 eV (f = 0), 1(1)Bu 8.54 then 6.40 eV (f = 0.76518), 1(3)Au 3.69 then 3.39 eV, 1(3)Bu 3.25 then 3.70 eV. The 34500 cm-1 band is assigned to 1(1)Au from 1(1)Ag, principally a nitrogen lone pair to pi3* promotion; the 44150 cm-1 band to the symmetry-forbidden 1(1)Bg transition, whose observed oscillator strength of about 0.003 comes from vibronic interaction. Natural orbital occupations for 1(1)Bg are 1.97, 1.99, 2.00, 1.95, 1.78, 1.21, 1.83, 0.44, 0.03, 0.01, 0.78, from which the authors conclude the CASSCF wavefunction has multireference character. Critical points relative to the S0 minimum (CASSCF then CASPT2, eV): S1 minimum 3.02/2.32, T1 minimum 3.06/2.16, T1-NNTS 6.76/5.79, T2 minimum 2.57/2.64, T2-NNTS 3.26/3.12, two H2CN(1(2)B2) fragments 1.80/2.28, H2CN(1(2)B2) plus H2CN(1(2)B1) 6.34/5.81, and the crossings S1/S0(1) 6.51/6.14, S1/S0(2) 6.42/5.99, S1/S0(3) 3.58/2.45, S1/T1/T2 3.26/3.18. Ground-state N-N is 1.398 A, shorter than a typical 1.45 A N-N single bond, and C-N 1.288 A, slightly longer than a typical 1.25 A double bond, reflecting conjugation between the two H2CN moieties.
Other: Two things here should stop anyone reusing these numbers uncritically. First, dynamic correlation REORDERS the two lowest triplets: at SA-CASSCF T2 (1(3)Bu) lies at 3.25 eV BELOW T1 (1(3)Au) at 3.69 eV, but MS-CASPT2 pushes T2 up to 3.70 eV and T1 down to 3.39 eV, swapping them. The labels T1/T2 in Table 2 are therefore assigned on the CASSCF ordering, and the T1/T2 minima at 3.06/2.16 and 2.57/2.64 eV cross the same way. Any mechanistic statement about which triplet is reached first depends entirely on which level is trusted. Second, the largest correlation correction of all is on 1(1)Bu, which falls from 8.54 to 6.40 eV — a 2.14 eV shift, against 0.39-0.44 eV for the other singlets — so the bright state is precisely the one the CASSCF space describes worst. Reference weights are uniformly healthy (0.82-0.86), so this is a genuine correlation effect and not an intruder problem. Note also that the CASPT2 level shift is not the same across the paper: 0.2 hartree for the vertical excitations in Table 1 but 0.0 hartree for the critical points in Table 2, so the two tables are not on a common footing and their energies should not be mixed. Finally, the surface crossings were located in the smaller (10,8) space while the stationary points come from (14,11), so the crossing energies in Table 2 rest on a different space from the minima they are compared against.

method: CASSCF(12,12) geometry optimization/frequencies and RS2C-CASPT2(12,12) potential energies; CASSCF singlet-triplet crossing and CAS(8,8) Pauli-Breit SOC; CCSD(T)/DFT comparison; 300 K BOMD
basis_set: 6-311+G(d) and aug-cc-pVTZ for CASSCF/CASPT2; 6-311+G(d) for crossing/SOC; B3LYP/6-31G(d) for dynamics
relativistic_treatment: Pauli-Breit Hamiltonian for SOC with rigorous one- and two-electron terms
active_space_orbital_description: All orbitals arising from valence C/N p atomic orbitals. In the Cs subgroup used to construct the tetrahedral-like singlet wave function, the explicit set is 8 a' orbitals (7a'-14a') plus 4 a'' orbitals (3a''-6a''); eight lower orbitals remain inactive/doubly occupied.
active_space_protocol: Common CAS(12,12) CASSCF geometries and RS2C-CASPT2 energies treat the entire singlet/triplet PES consistently at 6-311+G(d) and aug-cc-pVTZ. The leading CI coefficient is 0.94, supporting a multireference treatment. The 1A'/3A'' crossing uses CASSCF(12,12) geometry/energy, while SOC at that geometry is reported from CAS(8,8); the smaller orbital list is not specified. One tetrahedral connectivity row consolidates singlet isomerization, fragmentation, crossings, method variants, and dynamics frames.
nroots_per_mult: Lowest singlet and triplet surfaces around the dissociation crossing; state-average details not stated
electronic_structure_description: This high-energy C3v isomer is analogous to tetrahedral N4 but contains a carbon vertex and triangular N3 base. Its reactant configuration differs from the 1CN-+1N2 product configuration, and the spin-allowed dissociation TS mixes the two, making two-bond fragmentation orbital-symmetry forbidden. The equilibrium leading CI coefficient of 0.94 confirms non-negligible multireference character.
Other: Best CASPT2(12,12)/aug-cc-pVTZ energy is -201.83967532 Eh, 64.2 kcal mol^-1 above triplet chain 3NCNN-. Concerted dissociation through 1TS6/P1 lies at -201.77237323 Eh (106.4 relative to the triplet ground), hence a 42.2 kcal mol^-1 barrier; ring isomerization via TS5/6 is about 45 kcal mol^-1. Fragmentation releases 136.8 kcal mol^-1 at the CCSD(T) comparison level. The CASSCF(12,12) singlet-triplet crossing lies only 1.3 kcal mol^-1 above the singlet dissociation TS but is off the minimum-energy path; its geometry has C-N 1.381/1.581/1.581 A and N-N 1.293 A, and CAS(8,8) SOC is only 18.5 cm^-1, so ISC does not lower the operative barrier. A 300 K BOMD trajectory retains the structure for at least 25 ps. Carbon doping therefore leaves a ~42 kcal mol^-1 effective barrier, larger than the ~28 kcal mol^-1 ISC-limited stability of tetrahedral N4.
reference_short: Gao and Ding, RSC Adv. 2, 11764-11776 (2012)
notes: Exact ESI was recovered via Internet Archive and stored under papers/si/W2044016542. geometry_source: Potential curves giving Re, De, omega_e, the dipole moment and its derivative
method: State-averaged CASSCF, then MRCI(SD) with single and double excitations from all CASSCF configurations, with the Langhoff-Davidson size-consistency correction (+Q) estimating quadruple excitations
basis_set: the WB-MEFIT and HF-MEFIT pseudopotentials with their optimized (8s7p6d)/[6s5p3d] GTO valence basis sets, and the Hay-Wadt and LaJohn relativistic effective core potentials with their uncontracted optimized (5s5p4d) sets; all augmented with a single f function of exponent 3.0
relativistic_treatment: 16-electron energy-adjusted pseudopotentials, quasirelativistic (WB-MEFIT) and nonrelativistic (HF-MEFIT), compared with the Hay-Wadt and LaJohn relativistic effective core potentials
active_space_orbital_description: the molecular orbitals derived from the metal nd and (n+1)s atomic orbitals - 4d and 5s for Ru, 5d and 6s for Os - together with the hydrogen 1s; the same space is used for the CASSCF and for the subsequent correlation treatment
nroots_per_mult: seven low-lying states: 4Sigma-, 4Pi, 4Delta, 4Phi, 6Sigma+, 6Pi and 6Delta. The CASSCF expansions run to about 120 configurations; the MRCI(SD) expansions to 580000-770000 configurations for the quartets and 96000-170000 for the sextets
electronic_structure_description: Seven low-lying states computed - 4Sigma-, 4Pi, 4Delta, 4Phi, 6Sigma+, 6Pi and 6Delta - with term energies compared at CASSCF, MRCI(SD) and MRCI(SD)+Q levels for each pseudopotential. All three relativistically corrected pseudopotentials give a qualitatively similar picture with only minor differences, and both the nonrelativistic HF-MEFIT pseudopotential and the relativistic effective core potentials give 4Sigma- as the ground state, agreeing with the experimental assignment.
Other: The state ordering is the quantity of interest and it moves between CASSCF, MRCI(SD) and MRCI(SD)+Q on the same seven-orbital space, which is why all three levels are plotted rather than the last alone. That the ground state comes out 4Sigma- with a nonrelativistic pseudopotential as well as with three relativistic ones means the assignment is not being carried by the relativistic treatment. State averaging is used here for a specific structural reason rather than for balance alone: it allows the pi orbitals of Pi states and the delta orbitals of Delta states to be treated under an equivalence restriction in C2v, where the two components would otherwise be inequivalent. The space itself is the minimal chemically meaningful one - metal nd and (n+1)s plus the hydrogen 1s, seven orbitals - and it is kept identical across every pseudopotential being compared, which is what makes the comparison a test of the potentials rather than of the reference. The accuracy limits are stated at the atomic level: with the quasirelativistic WB-MEFIT pseudopotential the Ru 4d7 5s1 5F to Ru+ 4d7 4F ionization potential comes out 6.73 eV against a spin-orbit-averaged experimental 7.37, and the Os 5d6 6s2 5D to Os+ 6s1 6D ionization potential 7.57 eV against 8.77.
reference_short: Andrae, Haussermann, Dolg, Stoll & Preuss, Theor. Chim. Acta 77, 123-141 (1990)
notes: Active electron count is arithmetic from the stated composition: the metal nd and (n+1)s valence electrons - eight for both Ru (4d7 5s1) and Os (5d6 6s2) - plus the hydrogen 1s electron. d_electron_count reflects the free-atom configuration; the paper assigns no formal oxidation state. method: CASSCF stationary points and RHF closed-shell stationary points; CASPT2N single-point energies and local two-dimensional CASPT2N biquadratic surface approximations
software: Gaussian 94 revision D.2 for RHF/CASSCF optimizations and frequencies; MOLCAS 3 and 4 for CASSCF energies and CASPT2N
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(4,4) for closed-shell reactant/product contains the pi/pi* pairs of the two exocyclic double bonds. active_space_protocol: Optimize closed-shell 11/16/TSAR with RHF and open-shell TSE/DIR/TSP with CAS(6,6), then evaluate every structure by CASPT2N with the electronically sufficient space. electronic_structure_description: The singlet diradical path competes with a nominally concerted aromatic path. CASSCF over-stabilizes DIR-11 below reactant and underestimates the barrier by about 15 kcal/mol; CASPT2 dynamic correlation raises it and gives near-degenerate one- and two-step barriers, slightly favoring the two-step route. Natural-orbital diradical characters for reactant/TSE/TSAR/DIR/TSP/product are 0.07/0.39/0.46/0.89/0.49/0.07.

compound_name: the vinoxy radical, CH2CHO, at the non-planar X-A conical intersection
point_group: C1 - the molecule is highly twisted at the intersection
geometry_source: the conical intersection geometry taken from earlier SA-CASSCF work with a double-zeta basis; two-dimensional cuts of the potential surfaces computed around it by freezing the inactive coordinates at that geometry. The two active coordinates are the H1-C1-C2-O torsion and the C1-C2-O angle
method: three-state state-averaged CASSCF for the adiabatic surfaces, followed by diabatization, feeding quantum dynamical propagation through the intersection to examine how the initial momenta determine the outcome
basis_set: cc-pVTZ on all atoms
active_space_orbital_description: five electrons in five orbitals: the molecular orbitals corresponding to the CO, CC and C2-H3 bonds, together with the 2p orbitals centred on the C1 carbon and on oxygen
active_space_protocol: state-averaged over three states, because the dynamics passes through an intersection of two of them and the third has to be described on the same footing; the orbitals are chosen by naming the specific bonds and atomic p orbitals involved rather than by a valence rule
electronic_structure_description: At this conical intersection the radical is highly twisted, deformed along two coordinates - the H1-C1-C2-O torsional angle and the C1-C2-O bending angle - which together span the branching space. Two-dimensional cuts of the surfaces around the intersection are computed in that subspace, and the conditions on the initial momenta that determine passage through it are investigated.
Other: A five-electron, five-orbital space is about the smallest that can carry a genuine three-state average, and here it is sized by the dynamics rather than the spectroscopy: two-dimensional surface cuts dense enough to propagate a wavepacket on. The active space contains exactly the three bonds and two p orbitals that the twisting deformation modulates, which is what lets a space this small describe an intersection that is non-planar - a geometry a symmetry-based orbital selection could not have been built for.

point_group: C2h (trans) and C2v (cis) ground-state minima; Cs for the inversion transition state TS1 and C2 for the twisting transition state TS2
geometry_source: Ground-state cis, trans, TS1 and TS2 geometries optimised by CASSCF(6,5) with 6-31G(d,p) in HONDO. cis (1A1): P-P 2.192, P-H 1.408 angstrom, HPP 99.7 degrees, torsion 0.0; trans (1Ag): P-P 2.182, P-H 1.409, HPP 95.2, torsion 180.0; TS1 (1A', planar inversion): P-H 1.415 and 1.376, HPP 100.4, torsion 180.0; TS2 (1A, twisting): P-H 1.411, HPP 94.7, torsion 91.6 degrees. Excited-state geometries were instead optimised by UHF-SCF/6-31G(d,p) under a planarity constraint, and for the 2 3B, 2 1A and 2 1B states, which SCF cannot treat, the geometries were assumed: the 3A structures were reused for 2 1A, while for 2 1B and 2 3B the internal coordinates were interpolated linearly in the torsional angle between the UHF-SCF cis and trans values.
method: CASSCF (ground-state reaction-path geometries); UHF-SCF (excited-state geometries); MRD-CI with Langhoff-Davidson correction (all energies)
basis_set: 6-31G(d,p) for all CASSCF and UHF-SCF geometry work; McLean-Chandler [5s3p1d]/[2s1p] contraction for every MRD-CI energy
active_space_orbital_description: The five frontier orbitals n-, n+, pi, pi* and sigma*
active_space_protocol: The space is specified only as the six electrons in the five frontier orbitals n-, n+, pi, pi* and sigma*, with no selection criterion, orbital-energy window or test of a larger space, and its sole use is to generate the four ground-state stationary geometries. The validation offered is external: the CASSCF transition-state geometries are said to agree essentially with earlier MCSCF work, and the resulting MRD-CI barriers of 274 and 152 kJ/mol sit inside the spread of three earlier studies (277/141, 301/151, 278/131 kJ/mol). Energies never come from the CASSCF wavefunction: all of them are MRD-CI built on restricted Hartree-Fock orbitals in a configuration space of at most about 15000 determinants, Langhoff-Davidson corrected toward full CI, with second roots taken for the 2 3B, 2 1A and 2 1B states. The active space therefore constrains the geometries of the closed-shell ground state only, and every excited state in the paper rests on single-reference UHF-SCF geometries instead.
nroots_per_mult: the CASSCF step treats the closed-shell ground state only; the MRD-CI step covers six singlets (1A1/1Ag ground, 1A2, 1B1, 1B2 for cis and 1Bg, 1Bu, 1Au for trans) and six triplets (3B2, 3A2, 3B1 for cis and 3Bu, 3Bg, 3Au for trans), plus the twisted 3B and 1B minima and the second roots 2 3B, 2 1A, 2 1B
electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell singlet ground state with two minima; MRD-CI places trans (1Ag) below cis (1A1) by 11.0 kJ/mol, 10.1 kJ/mol with zero-point correction, a smaller gap than the 14.6, 16.7 and 15.1 kJ/mol of earlier work. Barriers from trans: 274 kJ/mol for planar inversion through TS1 and 152 kJ/mol for nonplanar twisting through TS2, falling to 265 and 144 kJ/mol with zero-point corrections, so the twisting path dominates and its barrier lies below both the H-P and P-P bond dissociation energies of 304 and 271 kJ/mol. Planar excited states, with P-P and P-H bond lengths in angstrom, HPP angle in degrees and MRD-CI energy relative to trans 1Ag in kJ/mol, and 0 or 1 marking an energy minimum or maximum along the torsion - cis: 3B2 (pi-pi*) 2.284 / 1.408 / 97.8 / 191 (max), 3A2 (n+-pi*) 2.228 / 1.408 / 99.8 / 314 (min), 3B1 (n--pi*) 1.987 / 1.397 / 121.5 / 354 (min), 1A2 (n+-pi*) 2.248 / 1.408 / 101.0 / 368 (min), 1B1 (n--pi*) 2.000 / 1.417 / 117.7 / 417 (max), 1B2 (pi-pi*) 2.216 / 1.406 / 98.7 / 486 (max); trans: 3Bu (pi-pi*) 2.272 / 1.408 / 94.3 / 182 (max), 3Bg (n+-pi*) 2.094 / 1.398 / 105.6 / 236 (min), 1Bg (n+-pi*) 2.118 / 1.401 / 105.6 / 298 (max), 3Au (n--pi*) 2.123 / 1.406 / 104.9 / 471 (min), 1Bu (pi-pi*) 2.207 / 1.406 / 94.7 / 470 (max), 1Au (n--pi*) 2.130 / 1.419 / 105.0 / 479 (min). The pi-pi* states lengthen P-P by 0.15-0.23 angstrom; excitation out of the n+ lone pair affects the cis form far more than the trans; and the n--pi* states of the cis form have P-P bonds shorter than the ground state, which the authors tie to their unusually large HPP angle. The twisted minima are 3B at a torsion of 89.8 degrees with P-P 2.203 angstrom and 1B at 107.0 degrees with P-P 2.373 and P-H 1.488 angstrom, at 157 and 266 kJ/mol (152 and 261 with zero-point corrections).
Other: State correlations along the torsion are not what a naive cis-trans mapping would give, because pi* is a2 in cis but bu in trans: the n+-pi* state is A2 in cis and Bg in trans while n--pi* is B1 in cis and Au in trans, so A and B states must cross. The 3B minimum correlates with the planar 3B2 and 3Bu pi-pi* states at both ends, but the open-shell singlet 1B minimum correlates with 1Bg (n+-pi*) on the trans side and with the much higher 1B1 (n--pi*) on the cis side - a point the authors emphasise as overlooked by earlier work. Curve crossings appear between 2 3B and 3A near 100 degrees and between 1B and 2 1A near 30 degrees; the authors note these are conical crossings computed under an imposed C2 constraint and would become avoided crossings once the symmetry is released, and leave that unexamined. That is the cleanest possible arrangement for the quantities this paper reports, because ionization potentials and detachment energies are differences of total energies between charge states, and any change in the orbital set between them would contaminate those differences with a change of reference rather than a change of physics. The space is fourteen valence electrons in thirteen molecular orbitals for the neutral, corresponding to the valence atomic sp orbitals of the carbon and nitrogen atoms plus the hydrogen 1s, comprising ten a' and three a'' orbitals under the assumed planar Cs symmetry; the anion carries fifteen electrons and the cation thirteen in the same thirteen orbitals. Because it is the full valence space, no orbital-selection judgement is involved and there is nothing to converge -- the only remaining question is dynamic correlation, and the paper is explicit that comparing the CASSCF and CASPT2 energies shows the dynamical correlation effect must be considered. The magnitude is large and state-dependent, which is the substantive active-space-related finding here: for the neutral, CASSCF and CASPT2 adiabatic energies are 0.702 against 0.738 eV for the 1A' state, essentially agreeing, but 2.041 against 1.556 eV for the 2 1Sigma+ state, 3.822 against 3.315 for 2 1A'', and 5.307 against 4.824 for 3 1A' -- shifts approaching half an electronvolt that reorder nothing but change every transition energy well beyond spectroscopic tolerance. So a full valence space is a necessary but not sufficient reference here; the authors correspondingly compute transition moments at CASSCF but excitation energies, which they describe as very sensitive to dynamic correlation, at CASPT2, mixing the two levels within a single oscillator strength. A second point concerns what the space has to accommodate. The states are far from uniformly single-reference: for the neutral, 2 1A'' is described by three configurations with coefficients -0.435, -0.428 and 0.504, 2 3A' by 0.448 and 0.833, and 3 1A' by 0.341 and 0.809, while the ground state sits at -0.939. A space that could not have carried those multiple configurations would have failed selectively, on exactly the excited states the paper is about. Finally, a caveat on the geometries the space was optimized under: all states of all three species were assumed to have planar Cs symmetry, and several stationary points turn out not to be minima under that assumption. The 2 2A' state of the anion has an imaginary frequency of 474.3i and is unstable, and linear configurations of both ions carry imaginary bending frequencies that resolve into Renner-Teller pairs -- for the cation, X 2A' and 2Pi(2A'') are separated by only 0.009 eV, degenerate at linearity. Energies read from this table are therefore tied to a symmetry assumption that the vibrational analysis partly contradicts.

active_space_orbital_description: Fifteen valence electrons in the same thirteen full-valence molecular orbitals used for the neutral radical, the electron count being increased by one relative to the neutral.
active_space_protocol: A full-valence complete active space: the wave function includes all excitations of the valence electrons in thirteen molecular orbitals corresponding to the valence atomic sp orbitals of the carbon and nitrogen atoms and the 1s orbital of hydrogen, namely ten a' and three a'' orbitals. The same active orbitals were used for all three charge states, with the active electron count increased by one for the anion and decreased by one for the cation. Oscillator strengths are defined as f = 2(TDM)^2 dE/3, with transition dipole moments computed at CASSCF and the excitation energies, described as very sensitive to dynamic correlation, computed at CASPT2.
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: X 2A''. The ground state has the dominant leading configuration [core](4a')2(5a')2(6a')2(7a')2(8a')2(1a'')2(9a')2(2a')alpha with a coefficient of 0.946, and is created from the neutral X 3A'' state mainly by adding a single electron to the slightly antibonding 9a' orbital, which increases its antibonding interaction and elongates the bond lengths. Following the analysis of linear triatomic Renner-Teller molecules, the anion is classified as a type D Renner-Teller molecule: following the in-plane imaginary bending eigenvector stabilizes the 2A'' component of the 2Pi state to the nonlinear X 2A'' ground state, and following the out-of-plane one stabilizes the 2A' component to a nonlinear geometry, with the larger in-plane imaginary frequency implying greater distortion from linearity for the X 2A'' state. The ground state is strongly bent at 109.3 degrees with a barrier to linearity of 0.575 eV, while the excited 2A' state has an obtuse angle of 143.3 degrees and may be termed quasilinear, its barrier to linearity being only 0.006 eV. Calculated harmonic frequencies for X 2A'' are 2845.5, 1975.0, 1031.9, 1001.5, 493.7 and 494.9 per cm, agreeing well with earlier theoretical values. All frequencies are real and the optimized states are confirmed stable except 2 2A', which has an imaginary frequency of 474.3i and is therefore unstable. The first adiabatic and vertical detachment energies are slightly lower than the experimental adiabatic value of 2.014 eV, and are separated by 0.442 eV because the 9a' orbital is not strictly nonbonding; the adiabatic and vertical detachment energies to the 1A' state are 2.507 and 2.505 eV against an experimental adiabatic value of 2.518 plus or minus 0.008 eV, and the vertical detachment energies to the 1A'', 2 1A', 2 1A'', 2 3A'', 3A', 2 3A' and 3 1A'' states are 3.458, 5.698, 5.779, 6.016, 6.777, 7.092 and further values.
Other: The active space is a full-valence space, defined once and then carried unchanged across all three charge states -- the same active orbitals were chosen for the anion and cation as for the neutral radical, with the active electron count simply increased or decreased by one. That is the cleanest possible arrangement for the quantities this paper reports, because ionization potentials and detachment energies are differences of total energies between charge states, and any change in the orbital set between them would contaminate those differences with a change of reference rather than a change of physics. The space is fourteen valence electrons in thirteen molecular orbitals for the neutral, corresponding to the valence atomic sp orbitals of the carbon and nitrogen atoms plus the hydrogen 1s, comprising ten a' and three a'' orbitals under the assumed planar Cs symmetry; the anion carries fifteen electrons and the cation thirteen in the same thirteen orbitals. Because it is the full valence space, no orbital-selection judgement is involved and there is nothing to converge -- the only remaining question is dynamic correlation, and the paper is explicit that comparing the CASSCF and CASPT2 energies shows the dynamical correlation effect must be considered. The magnitude is large and state-dependent, which is the substantive active-space-related finding here: for the neutral, CASSCF and CASPT2 adiabatic energies are 0.702 against 0.738 eV for the 1A' state, essentially agreeing, but 2.041 against 1.556 eV for the 2 1Sigma+ state, 3.822 against 3.315 for 2 1A'', and 5.307 against 4.824 for 3 1A' -- shifts approaching half an electronvolt that reorder nothing but change every transition energy well beyond spectroscopic tolerance. So a full valence space is a necessary but not sufficient reference here; the authors correspondingly compute transition moments at CASSCF but excitation energies, which they describe as very sensitive to dynamic correlation, at CASPT2, mixing the two levels within a single oscillator strength. A second point concerns what the space has to accommodate. The states are far from uniformly single-reference: for the neutral, 2 1A'' is described by three configurations with coefficients -0.435, -0.428 and 0.504, 2 3A' by 0.448 and 0.833, and 3 1A' by 0.341 and 0.809, while the ground state sits at -0.939. For the cation the authors state the criterion explicitly, noting that the leading-configuration coefficients for X 2A', 2Pi(2A''), 4Pi(4A') and 4A' are all above 0.90, indicating single-reference character, while the other states show obviously multireference character. A space that could not have carried those multiple configurations would have failed selectively, on exactly the excited states the paper is about. Finally, a caveat on the geometries the space was optimized under: all states of all three species were assumed to have planar Cs symmetry, and several stationary points turn out not to be minima under that assumption. The 2 2A' state of the anion has an imaginary frequency of 474.3i and is unstable, and linear configurations of both ions carry imaginary bending frequencies that resolve into Renner-Teller pairs -- for the cation, X 2A' and 2Pi(2A'') are separated by only 0.009 eV, degenerate at linearity. Energies read from this table are therefore tied to a symmetry assumption that the vibrational analysis partly contradicts.
reference_short: Zhao, Zhang & Sun, J. Phys. Chem. A 2008, 112, 12125
notes: Detachment energies are defined as differences of total energies: the adiabatic detachment energy as the optimized neutral minus the optimized anion, and the vertical detachment energy as the neutral at the optimized anion geometry minus the optimized anion. Geometrical parameters agree closely with earlier work at QCISD/6-311G(d,p). correlation_correction: CASPT2 single points at the CASSCF-optimized geometries.

point_group: D2d minimum and D2h conformer (D2d treated in the C2v Abelian subgroup for CASSCF/CASPT2)
geometry_source: CASSCF/CASPT2 calculations used TPSS-optimized geometries from Gaussian 03. TPSS employed an SDD small-core pseudopotential/basis for Ce and cc-pVDZ for C/H. The D2-constrained optimization relaxed to D2d and was a minimum; D2h had one imaginary frequency (i35.9 cm^-1) and lay 0.13 eV above D2d at TPSS. Reported D2d metrics are Ce-C(br) 2.50 A, Ce-C(alpha) 2.72 A, Ce-C(beta) 2.86 A, mean Ce-C 2.70 A, ligand fold 25.6 degrees, and twist 90.04 degrees.
method: CASSCF(12,16) followed by CASPT2 energies for the two lowest singlet and triplet roots of every working-point-group irrep; IVO-RHF input orbitals; natural-orbital occupation and f-density analysis; transition oscillator strength at CASPT2
basis_set: All-electron ANO: Ce (25s22p15d11f)/[9s8p5d4f], approximately cc-pVQZ quality; C and H ANO sets of cc-pVDZ quality
relativistic_treatment: Second-order Douglas-Kroll scalar-relativistic Hamiltonian with all-electron ANO basis sets
active_space_orbital_description: The active space contains six initially occupied and ten initially virtual IVO-RHF orbitals. It extends the earlier cerocene CAS(8,14) by adding the higher-lying ligand pi1 level because the pi2-pi1 gap falls to 1.17 eV (D2d) or 1.06 eV (D2h). It explicitly includes the relevant ligand pi1/pi2 manifold and permits occupation of any of twelve Ce 4f/5d levels. D2d/C2v active occupied counts are A1=2, A2=2, B1=1, B2=1 and active virtual counts 2,2,3,3. D2h active occupied counts are Ag=1, B1g=1, B2g=1, B3g=0, Au=1, B1u=1, B2u=0, B3u=1 and active virtual counts 1,1,1,1,1,1,2,2.
active_space_protocol: For D2d, MOLCAS calculations used C2v while orbital mixing newly allowed by symmetry reduction was monitored and eliminated. For both conformers, compact input virtuals came from the improved-virtual-orbital RHF procedure. The two lowest singlet and triplet roots of each irrep were computed: 16 states for D2d/C2v and 32 for D2h. Ground-state state-average sizes from one through six were tested; natural occupations were substantially more stable than configuration weights. CASPT2 frozen-orbital counts were D2d/C2v A1=17, A2=4, B1=9, B2=9 and D2h Ag=11, B1g=3, B2g=4, B3g=4, Au=1, B1u=6, B2u=5, B3u=5. Spin-orbit coupling was explicitly neglected as expected to be weak from prior CeCOT2 work.
nroots_per_mult: D2d/C2v: 8 singlet and 8 triplet roots; D2h: 16 singlet and 16 triplet roots; two roots per irrep and multiplicity (24 roots per multiplicity across both conformers)
electronic_structure_description: The D2d conformer has a strongly multiconfigurational 1A1 ground state. Its antibonding a2 orbital of dominant Ce f-delta character has occupation 0.383 and the corresponding bonding a2 orbital occupation is 1.608 (deoccupation 0.391); all other active-orbital deviations are at most 0.052. The first excited singlet is the degenerate B1/B2(E) pair at 0.87 eV; the lowest triplets B1/B2 lie at 0.88 eV and the A1 triplet at 1.16 eV. The computed bright singlet transition is 2.35 eV with oscillator strength 0.345, versus the experimental broad band at 2.34 eV. D2h has a strongly multiconfigurational 1Ag ground state 0.24 eV above D2d, with antibonding au occupation 0.378 and bonding au occupation 1.612 (deoccupation 0.388); its first excited 1B2g state is 0.93 eV above that conformer's ground state. Several D2h B1g, Au, and B1u excited states of both multiplicities are also strongly multiconfigurational and include ligand-to-metal charge transfer. Natural-orbital analysis gives total Ce 4f density n_f=0.78 +/- 0.04, close to experiment 0.87 +/- 0.05 and below the authors' prior cerocene value 0.90 +/- 0.04; comparison B3LYP gives only 0.62 +/- 0.01. The authors therefore describe CePn2 as formally Ce(IV) with substantial ligand-to-metal density transfer rather than a ground state dominated by an integer pi3 f1 configuration.
reference_short: Kerridge and Kaltsoyannis, C. R. Chimie 13, 853-859 (2010)
notes: One entry was created for the one distinct CePn2 composition/connectivity, consolidating both conformers, all 48 roots, state-average sizes, and DFT comparisons. compound_name: 9H-Adenine, ground and first singlet excited state geometries
geometry_source: Ground and first singlet excited state geometries optimized at CASSCF(4/4)/6-31G, at CIS/6-31G, and with a semiempirical AM1 configuration interaction treatment using the same four-orbital restriction; one excited state geometry reoptimized at CIS/6-31G* as a basis set check
method: CASSCF with a four-electron four-orbital space for excited state geometries, compared against configuration interaction with single excitations and against a semiempirical AM1-CI treatment; INDO/S-CI spectra reported for comparison
software: GAMESS for the CASSCF calculations; Gaussian 94 for the CIS calculations; ZINDO for the INDO/S-CI spectra
basis_set: 6-31G for both the CASSCF and CIS calculations, chosen deliberately small so that geometries from different methods could be compared on an equal basis; 6-31G with added d polarization functions on the non-hydrogen atoms used as a check
active_space_orbital_description: Four electrons in four orbitals, denoted (4/4). The space contains only pi orbitals: sigma to sigma* excitations cannot be included, and the n to pi* state is not present in the restricted configuration interaction space.
active_space_protocol: A four-electron, four-orbital space used for the excited state geometry optimizations, matching the restriction used in the semiempirical AM1-CI(4/4) treatment so that the two can be compared directly. The authors note that this necessary restriction excludes sigma to sigma* excitations from the configuration interaction wave function, and that the n to pi* state was not included in the space in either four-orbital calculation.
electronic_structure_description: Both Hartree-Fock and CASSCF predict planar ground state geometries. The mean errors in bond lengths against experiment are 0.013 Angstrom at CASSCF/6-31G, compared with values quoted for AM1 and Hartree-Fock. All three methods predict a rather puckered relaxed first singlet excited state geometry. The four-orbital CASSCF and the AM1-CI(4/4) treatments both give that state pi to pi* character, whereas the single-excitation treatment gives an n to pi* state; the n to pi* state was not in the restricted configuration interaction space of either four-orbital calculation. The single-excitation optimization had serious convergence problems because the character of the first excited state changed during the optimization, and the n to pi* assignment was confirmed by starting from several different geometries. The pi to pi* state, which is the first excited state of the vertical transition spectrum, has only an almost stationary point on the potential energy surface, and it differs from the n to pi* state in the N1-C2-N3 region: the N1-C2 bond is 1.334 Angstrom in the pi to pi* state against 1.388 Angstrom in the n to pi* state, and a marked out-of-plane displacement of the C2-H2 group is found in the n to pi* state while the pi to pi* state is almost planar. In the CASSCF(4/4) geometry the largest out-of-plane displacement is for the hydrogen bonded to C8, whereas in the AM1-CI(4/4) geometry it is for the hydrogen bonded to N9. At the avoided crossing of the two excited state curves the two states are completely mixed with both n to pi* and pi to pi* character, and the vibronic coupling can be extracted as the energy difference between them there.
Other: The active space here is small enough that what it leaves out decides the answer, and the paper documents that twice over. The space is four electrons in four orbitals and contains only pi orbitals: the authors state that the necessary restriction in active space does not allow inclusion of sigma to sigma* type excitations in the configuration interaction wave function, and cite earlier work showing such excitations matter for describing the pi to pi* transitions of benzene, a case where the magnitude of dynamical correlation differs between excited states and where a single-excitation treatment fails seriously on the absorption spectrum. The consequence is visible immediately in the character of the state being optimized. For adenine, the (4,4) space and the semiempirical calculation with the same four-orbital restriction both predict the relaxed first singlet excited state to have pi to pi* character, while the single-excitation configuration interaction treatment gives an n to pi* state instead. The authors are explicit that the n to pi* state was not included in the restricted configuration interaction space in either of the four-orbital calculations -- so the disagreement is not a finding about adenine but a direct consequence of the space excluding the competing state. The single-excitation calculation, which can see both, had serious convergence problems precisely because the character of the first excited state changed during the optimization, and its identification of an n to pi* minimum was confirmed by restarting from several different geometries. The pi to pi* state, which is the first excited state of the vertical spectrum, turns out to have only an almost stationary point on the surface. That is a textbook case of a space chosen around one state producing a clean minimum for it while the real lowest state lies outside the space entirely. For 2-aminopurine the situation is different and the space is on safer ground: all three methods agree that the relaxed first excited state has pi to pi* character, and both the four-orbital and the single-excitation treatments give rather planar geometries, so the exclusion of the n to pi* state costs nothing there. The two isomers differ exactly in whether the omitted state competes, which is the physical reason the paper is about. The authors' own verdict on the method is worth recording: the two ab initio approaches are about equally demanding computationally, and the four-orbital space introduces some electron correlation in both the ground and excited states but cannot admit the sigma excitations, and on the basis of previous experience they choose the single-excitation method for the subsequent photophysics rather than the multiconfigurational one. Basis set effects were checked and found small: a 6-31G geometry reoptimized with added d polarization functions on the non-hydrogen atoms produced only minor geometric and spectroscopic changes, which is why the deliberately modest 6-31G basis was retained so that geometries from the different methods could be compared on equal footing.
reference_short: Broo, J. Phys. Chem. A 1998, 102, 526
notes: This isomer exists in two tautomeric forms in water solution, 9H and 7H, with the 9H tautomer the major component; part of the fluorescence has been attributed to the minor 7H tautomer. correlation_correction: None beyond CASSCF; the authors note the four-orbital space introduces some electron correlation in both ground and excited states but cannot admit sigma excitations.

compound_name: the MgMg2+ molecular system, symmetric Mg2+ + Mg charge transfer
point_group: Dinfh, with gerade and ungerade states classified by nuclear interchange symmetry
geometry_source: adiabatic potential energy curves computed as a function of the internuclear distance, with radial and rotational couplings between the states
method: state-averaged CASSCF followed by MRCI, with radial and rotational couplings extracted for a subsequent semi-classical dynamical treatment of the charge-transfer collision
basis_set: all-electron correlation-consistent cc-pV5Z on magnesium, chosen after tests of several atomic basis sets
active_space_orbital_description: the n = 3 (s, p, d) orbitals of magnesium - nine orbitals in all - with no electron count stated
active_space_protocol: the active space is specified only as including the n = 3 (spd) orbitals, used in state-averaged CASSCF as the reference for MRCI across the three lowest dissociation limits; no electron count is given

electronic_structure_description: The n-pi-star state is predicted to lie 0.24 eV above the bright pi-pi-star state. Conical intersections between the bright excited singlet and the ground state were located at both multireference levels. Two hundred trajectories were launched from the bright state, with maximum simulation times of 300 femtoseconds in vacuum and 350 femtoseconds in water, using 821 explicit water molecules in the solution simulations and a 0.5 femtosecond time step. In the gas phase the excited state is completely depopulated within 225 femtoseconds, and fitting gives a latency of 49.5 femtoseconds before decay begins, a decay constant of 55.2 femtoseconds and a total excited-state lifetime of 104.7 femtoseconds, comparable to the 85.5 femtoseconds of the hypoxanthine keto-N9H analogue. In water the corresponding fit gives a fractional weight of 0.291, a latency of 217.6 femtoseconds, a decay constant of 25.2 femtoseconds and a total lifetime of 242.8 femtoseconds. The decay constant is therefore larger in the gas phase than in solution, 55.2 against 25.2 femtoseconds, while the latency increases substantially from 49.5 to 217.6 femtoseconds on going into water. Of the trajectories run in water only 59 return to the ground state within the 350 femtosecond simulation. Both computed lifetimes are consistent with the experimental observation of sub-200 femtosecond decay in aqueous solution.
Other: The authors state the ideal space and then explain exactly what they gave up and why, which is the most useful form this information can take. Ideally the space should include all p orbitals perpendicular to the molecular plane, requiring twelve electrons in ten pi orbitals; to reduce cost they used ten electrons in eight orbitals instead, on the stated grounds that the two electrons and two pi orbitals omitted have the least effect on the conjugation interaction and on the selected low-lying states. So the truncation is justified by an argument about which orbitals matter for the specific states being followed, not by a general claim of adequacy, and the reader is told precisely which orbitals were dropped. The space that is used comprises the oxygen lone pair of the carbonyl moiety together with pi orbitals, which is what allows both the bright pi-pi-star state and the nearby n-pi-star state, predicted to lie 0.24 eV higher, to be represented in the same reference. What makes this record more than a truncation note is that the reduced space carries the entire dynamical result. Two hundred surface-hopping trajectories were propagated on a two-state averaged reference with this space, in vacuum and embedded in 821 explicit water molecules, and the excited-state lifetimes extracted from them are the paper's principal quantity. Those lifetimes are 104.7 femtoseconds in the gas phase, decomposing into a 49.5 femtosecond latency before decay begins and a 55.2 femtosecond decay constant, against 242.8 femtoseconds in water with a 217.6 femtosecond latency and a much shorter 25.2 femtosecond decay constant. The solvent thus more than quadruples the latency while halving the decay time, and the two effects are separately resolved only because the same space was used in both environments. Any error the truncation introduces sits in the surface topography that determines those numbers, and it cannot be corrected afterwards the way an energy can. Consistent with that, the perturbative correction is applied only to gas-phase excitation energies and not to the dynamics, so the trajectories run on uncorrected surfaces throughout. Two further points on scope. The conical intersection between the bright state and the ground state was optimized both at the multiconfigurational level and with a single-excitation multireference configuration interaction treatment, giving an independent check on the crossing geometry that the dynamics depends on. And in solution the multiconfigurational region is embedded in a molecular mechanics environment, so the active space describes a solute inside a classical bath rather than a supermolecular cluster, with the geometry optimization in solution performed at a density functional level instead.

compound_name: parent Diels-Alder reaction system: 1,3-butadiene + ethylene -> cyclohexene, with vinylcyclobutane side channel
ligand_set: 1,3-butadiene + ethylene reactant pair; concerted and anti-/gauche-diradical pathways to cyclohexene plus diradical side pathway to vinylcyclobutane
geometry_source: Reactants, products, minima, and transition states were optimized on the unmodified PES and force-modified G-FMPES at CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G** using custom FIRE optimization and climbing-image NEB. The article provides labeled molecular drawings and selected C-C bond lengths but no complete Cartesian coordinates, so no structure file is claimed.
method: CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G** generalized force-modified potential-energy surfaces with FIRE geometry optimization, climbing-image nudged elastic band minimum-energy paths/transition states, Hessian/ZPE analysis, and harmonic transition-state-theory yield estimates
software: AIMS-MOLPRO for all electronic-structure calculations, using MOLPRO version 2012.1; custom Python routines coupled to MOLPRO for G-FMPES structure optimization
basis_set: 6-31G** for CASSCF; 6-311++G** for the parallel B3LYP comparison
active_space_orbital_description: The source specifies CASSCF(6,6) but does not identify or plot the six active orbitals; an orbital assignment is therefore not inferred.
active_space_protocol: The same CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G** model was used for the concerted path, the open-shell anti- and gauche-diradical paths, and the vinylcyclobutane side path. The paper explicitly invokes singlet<->triplet switching for diradical mechanisms, but does not report root counts, state-average weights, occupation restrictions, or state-specific/state-averaged implementation details. External force on atom j was defined as f_ext(j)=P_HP[r(j)-c], with negative P_HP compressive and c the geometric centroid; this places all atoms in a common three-dimensional parabolic potential. Stationary points were optimized by FIRE and paths/transition states by CI-NEB. Hessians gave six numerical zero modes at minima and one imaginary frequency at each saddle. ZPE is included in tabulated activation/reaction energies unless the figure caption explicitly says otherwise.
electronic_structure_description: At zero external force, the CASSCF concerted route has ZPE-corrected activation/reaction energies of 45.5/-21.2 kcal/mol (B3LYP comparison 24.3/-27.6; experiment 27.5+/-2/-40.0). For the anti-diradical route, the zero-force barriers are 44.0 kcal/mol for diradical formation and 3.9 kcal/mol from anti-diradical to cyclohexene; anti is 0.4 kcal/mol below gauche. The overall gauche route is 46.3 kcal/mol: first-step barrier 41.4, intermediate only 0.9 below that transition state, and second-step barrier 5.8. Anti-route overall activation energies at P_HP=0,-0.31,-0.63,-1.25 kcal mol^-1 A^-2 are 44.0,43.6,43.0,44.3 kcal/mol. At P_HP<=-2.51 the anti minimum catastrophically merges toward cyclohexene; at the smallest tested compression (-0.31), the gauche minimum instead disappears toward vinylcyclobutane. The CASSCF concerted barrier falls with compression but does not vanish over the tested range, unlike B3LYP below -3.45.
Other: For the vinylcyclobutane side path, exact CASSCF activation/reaction energies (kcal/mol) at P_HP=0,-0.31,-0.63,-0.94,-1.25 are 42.4/+2.0, 38.1/-4.0, 35.8/-7.8, 48.4/-9.4, and 46.3/-11.9. The nonmonotonic barrier accompanies a switch in which C-C bond forms first; a persistent path kink was not removed by varying NEB spring constants over an order of magnitude, and its origin remained unknown. Under simplifying hTST assumptions (irreversible reactions, unit reactant concentration, equal prefactors, no cyclohexene<->vinylcyclobutane interconversion), the predicted vinylcyclobutane/cyclohexene yield ratios at P_HP=0,-0.63,-1.25 are 13.18,1.95,6.34e-12 at 300 K and 3.78,1.49,1.87e-7 at 500 K. Converting the force model by mean force divided by mean enclosing-sphere area gives about 68-1410 MPa for P_HP=-0.31 to -5.02. For the concerted CASSCF path, estimated reactant/TS/product pressures (MPa) are 68.4/81.7/83.4, 150.6/164.5/167.9, 230.6/248.8/252.5, 314.3/332.5/338.5, 484.8/504.4/511.6, 659.0/678.4/686.8, 838.0/856.2/864.2, 1022.8/1037.0/1043.7, and 1397.6/1406.6/1409.1 at the nine listed compressions. The authors emphasize trends rather than benchmark absolute energies: compression lowers the desired concerted barrier, generally raises exothermicity, and at high force suppresses the vinylcyclobutane yield. Spin crossing is described at the PES/path level; no SOC or spin-spin calculation is reported.

active_space_protocol: the space is the whole one-electron manifold the spectroscopy lives in, so every 4f and 5d level appears on the same footing and none is privileged; with one electron there is nothing to select and the space is fixed by the ion rather than by judgement. What is judged is what surrounds it - the cluster boundary, the model potentials and the point-charge field - and what is correlated afterwards: the cerium 5s, 5p, 4f and 5d electrons and the oxygen 2s and 2p electrons.
electronic_structure_description: With spin-orbit coupling the seven 4f levels split into two groups about 2400 cm-1 apart, at 0, 642, 1416, 2290, 2772, 3336 and 3931 cm-1, matching the 2F(5/2) and 2F(7/2) multiplets; without it they span only 0 to 2153 cm-1. The five 5d levels fall at 30901, 33234, 37736, 41157 and 53388 cm-1 - 324, 301, 265, 243 and 187 nm - with relative oscillator strengths of 1.00, 0.18, 0.32, 0.02 and 0.12; without spin-orbit coupling each sits about 1000 cm-1 lower. The lowest 4f-to-5d transition is 18439 cm-1 below the free-ion value of 49340 cm-1. Decomposing that red shift gives a centroid shift of 11947 cm-1 from the free-ion 51230 cm-1 and a crystal-field stabilization of 8382 cm-1.
Other: The calculation is what lets a site assignment be made rather than guessed: the measured excitation spectrum is a broad band with a shoulder, and only the computed level positions and intensities separate it into a dominant lowest 4f-to-5d transition and two weaker ones underneath the shoulder, with the two highest transitions buried under the host's excitonic absorption. Decomposing the shift also isolates a structural cause - the centroid shift is at least 2000 cm-1 larger here than in other cerium-doped phosphates, which the authors attribute to the one coordinating oxygen that belongs to no phosphate tetrahedron and is therefore far more polarizable by the 5d electron, while the crystal-field splitting is unremarkable.
