metal_ox_state: formally +4, but the ground state is a mixed-valence superposition of Re(IV) and Re(V) forms
ligand_set: a noninnocent dioxolene ligand, three chlorides and a triphenylphosphine oxide
geometry_source: X-ray structures determined in this work at 150 and 290 K; the room-temperature structure was used for the calculations, with tert-butyl groups replaced by hydrogens and phenyl groups by methyls in the more expensive correlated runs
method: State-averaged CASSCF followed by n-electron valence second-order perturbation theory, with spin-orbit coupling treated nonperturbatively by diagonalization over 5 quintet, 22 triplet and 25 singlet states; spin-Hamiltonian parameters extracted by the effective Hamiltonian approach, and the molar magnetic susceptibility computed from the same wave functions including both spin-orbit and Zeeman effects
basis_set: Relativistically recontracted def2-TZVP for hydrogen through barium and an all-electron relativistically contracted SARC basis of the same quality for rhenium; the initial minimal-space calculations used ANO-RCC-VDZ, with resolution of the identity and matching correlation fitting sets
relativistic_treatment: Second-order Douglas-Kroll-Hess Hamiltonian; spin-orbit coupling by the spin-orbit mean-field approximation, applied nonperturbatively
active_space_orbital_description: Six electrons in nine orbitals for the reported calculations: the five rhenium 5d orbitals together with the highest occupied, the lowest unoccupied and two further virtual orbitals of the o-benzoquinone ligand. The minimal space was four electrons in six orbitals, the five 5d orbitals plus the ligand's lowest unoccupied orbital; spaces up to eight electrons in ten orbitals were also tested.
active_space_protocol: Spaces were varied from four electrons in six orbitals up to eight in ten, and the authors report that similar results were obtained in all cases, which is the relevant check when the question is how much ligand character mixes into metal-based states. The minimal space is the smallest capable of representing the redox ambiguity: the complete metal d shell plus the one ligand orbital that can accept an electron.
nroots_per_mult: 5 quintet, 22 triplet and 25 singlet states in the reported state-averaged calculation
electronic_structure_description: A triplet ground state whose wave function has strongly multireference character: three configurations contribute substantially, and the state is a superposition of a rhenium(IV)-semiquinolate form and a rhenium(V)-catecholate form with comparable weights, the former predominating above 54 percent. The complex is therefore formally a rhenium(IV) semiquinolate but is more accurately a mixed-valence species. This matches the crystallography independently: C-O, C-C and Re-O distances at both 150 and 290 K lie between the semiquinolate and catecholate limits, giving an empirical metrical oxidation state of -1.5 for the dioxolene ligand. In the minimal space the quintet lies 0.38 eV (3060 reciprocal centimetres) above the triplet and the lowest singlet 1.36 eV (10940 reciprocal centimetres) above it. Spin-orbit coupling produces an anomalously large zero-field splitting of the pseudospin S = 1 ground state. SOC-CASSCF(6,9): D = 341 cm-1, E/D = 0.019, giso 1.78. SOC-CASSCF(6,9)/NEVPT2: D = 481 cm-1, E/D = 0.026, giso 1.77. These are consistent with the measured magnetic susceptibility from 5 to 300 K. Measured (fit of chi(T), model 2, one S = 1 centre): D = 816 cm-1, E/D = 0.31, g = 1.93. Measured (fit of chi(T), model 1, Re(IV) S = 3/2 coupled to semiquinone S = 1/2, J = -1024 cm-1): D = 572 cm-1 for Re(IV), E/D = 0.25, g = 1.94. All absorption bands in the visible region are assigned as ligand-to-metal charge transfer, with a significant intraligand contribution to the most intense band at 555 nm.
Other: The space is varied deliberately across a range and the paper reports the most reassuring possible outcome: similar results in all cases. A minimal space of four electrons in six orbitals -- the five rhenium 5d orbitals plus the lowest unoccupied orbital of the quinone -- was run first, then spaces enlarged as far as eight electrons in ten orbitals, with the reported calculations using six electrons in nine orbitals, adding the ligand's highest occupied orbital and two further virtuals. Stating that the answer is stable across that range is worth more than any single number, because the question being asked is precisely how much ligand character mixes into the metal-based states, and a result that moved as ligand orbitals were added would be an artifact of the space rather than a finding. The minimal space is defined by a clear rule -- the complete metal d shell plus the one ligand orbital that can accept an electron -- which is the smallest space capable of representing the redox ambiguity at issue. The chemical payoff is a wave function that cannot be reduced to a single oxidation state: three configurations contribute substantially, and the ground triplet is a superposition of a metal(IV)-semiquinone form and a metal(V)-catecholate form with comparable weights, the former predominating at above 54 percent. A 54-to-46 split is exactly the regime where a formal oxidation state stops being meaningful, and the calculation is what converts a qualitative suspicion of ligand noninnocence into a number. It also agrees independently with the crystallography: bond distances fall between the two limiting forms, giving an empirical metrical oxidation state of -1.5 for the ligand. Two independent lines of evidence for the same intermediate character is much stronger than either alone. A cost-driven compromise is stated plainly rather than hidden: the correlated calculations with the larger basis were too expensive on the real molecule, so tert-butyl groups were replaced by hydrogens and phenyl groups by methyls, and every reported spectrum and spin-Hamiltonian parameter comes from that truncated model rather than from the compound actually crystallized. Spin-orbit coupling is treated NONPERTURBATIVELY, by diagonalizing over 5 quintet, 22 triplet and 25 singlet states, which is necessary here because the resulting zero-field splitting is anomalously large -- 341 reciprocal centimetres at one level and 481 at the correlated level, values at which perturbative treatments of spin-orbit coupling are not valid. The 40 percent spread between those two numbers is itself informative about how much the correlation treatment matters for this property, even where it barely matters for the state composition.

compound_name: Gd(III) aqua complex [Gd(H2O)7]3+, a 4f7 ion with 7 water ligands
point_group: no point group assigned; 7-coordinate aqua complex
geometry_source: geometries optimised with the PBE0 functional and a Def2TZVPP basis on the water molecules with a Stuttgart relativistic effective core potential on the metal; ab initio molecular dynamics in CP2K 5.0 (TZVP-GTH Gaussian basis with an auxiliary plane-wave basis) provided dynamical sampling of the aqueous complexes
method: complete active space self-consistent field (CASSCF) with the D tensor from a CASSCF spin-orbit Hamiltonian treated by quasi-degenerate perturbation theory (QDPT); a multireference configuration interaction (MRCI) step on the same orbitals was also tested
software: ORCA 3.0.3 for the ZFS; CP2K 5.0 for the AIMD
basis_set: QZVP on hydrogen and oxygen; all-electron relativistically contracted SARC-DKH TZ on Gd(III) and Eu(II)
relativistic_treatment: Douglas-Kroll-Hess (DKH) formalism; spin-orbit coupling by QDPT
active_space_orbital_description: seven orbitals modelling the 4f7 configuration of the metal
multiplicities_studied: octet and sextet; couplings to quartet and doublet states were ignored
nroots_per_mult: 1 octet and 48 sextets, state-averaged in the orbital optimisation
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 8S7/2 from the 4f7 configuration, S = 7/2, splitting into four Kramers doublets. The lowest excited sextet states lie near 40000 cm-1 for Gd(III) and lower for Eu(II). For Gd(III) the 9-coordinate complex shows the smallest total splitting of the ground octet (0.0695 cm-1) and a negative D, while the 7- and 8-coordinate complexes have positive D. CASSCF(7,7)/QDPT at its own optimised geometry: D = 0.0269 cm-1, E/D = 0.2325 (Table 2). CASSCF(7,7)/QDPT at the optimised Eu(II) geometry (Gd@Eu): D = 0.0206 cm-1, E/D = 0.1170 (Table 2).
Other: The number of state-averaged roots, not the size of the (7,7) space, is what controls D here, and the paper demonstrates it: for Gd(III)(H2O)7, CASSCF with 1 octet and 48 sextets gives D = 0.02712 cm-1, and adding an MRCI step on the same orbitals changes nothing at all, because there are no excitations into or out of a 4f7 active space and the MRCI is therefore equivalent to the CASSCF. Cutting the sextet roots from 48 to the three with the largest spin-orbit matrix elements raises D to 0.199 cm-1 -- a factor of seven -- and the ground-octet splitting from 0.365 to 2.397 cm-1, while also pushing the lowest excited sextet from 40300 to 41200 cm-1. The authors conclude that three sextets are not enough, despite those three carrying the largest couplings. | A (7,7) space spanning only the 4f shell also means no ligand or charge-transfer character can enter, which is the reason MRCI adds nothing. | Swapping the geometries between the two isoelectronic ions separates the metal from its coordination environment: putting Gd(III) in Eu(II)'s optimised geometry (Gd@Eu) gives D = 0.0206, 0.0231 and 0.0088 cm-1 for n = 7, 8, 9, and Eu(II) in Gd(III)'s geometry (Eu@Gd) gives -0.0381, -0.0679 and 0.0199. The sign follows the metal rather than the geometry for Eu, but for Gd at n = 9 the swap flips D from -0.0058 to +0.0088, so no simple transferable relationship between the two isoelectronic complexes emerges.
reference_short: Khan, Pollet, Vuilleumier, Kowalewski & Odelius, Chem. Phys. 503 (2018) 56
notes: Source PDF supplied from the local ZFS project (/media/victor/disk1/claude/zfs/pdfs); recorded there as carrying its own CASSCF ZFS calculation while aimdb had never indexed it. zfs_D_calc and zfs_ED_calc are the Table 2 values for this complex at its OWN optimised geometry. The geometry-swap entries of Table 2 (Gd@Eu, Eu@Gd) are the same six species with the other ion's geometry and are recorded in Other rather than as separate rows. zfs_D_exp is empty: the paper reports no experimental ZFS for these aqua complexes. ss_included left empty -- only the spin-orbit contribution is computed, via QDPT, and couplings to quartet and doublet states were deliberately ignored. The text quotes D = 0.02712 cm-1 for this complex in the root-reduction discussion against Table 2's 0.0269; both are recorded as printed. Dynamical sampling of 899 snapshots from 10 ps of AIMD gives distributions of D and E/D for the aqueous complex rather than a single value, and D correlates with the splitting of the ground state into Kramers doublets along the cylindrical approximation. electronic_structure_description corrected (2026-10-30 multireference-ZFS completion): The Table 2 D and E/D for this complex (own geometry and the swapped geometry) were held only in properties/Other and are now stated in the prose.

active_space_protocol: A d-only CAS over the five nickel 3d orbitals, used solely to obtain the single-ion anisotropy: all 10 quartet and 35 doublet states of the configuration are computed, mixed through RASSI-SO, and passed to SINGLE_ANISO for the g tensors and zero-field splitting. The calculations are single points on B3LYP ground-state geometries. The article states the space inconsistently, describing it in the same sentence as 'eight active electrons in five active metal-based d orbitals, that is, a CAS(7,5) setup'; seven electrons is the count consistent with a d7 Ni(III) centre and with the quoted CAS(7,5), so seven is recorded here.
nroots_per_mult: 10 quartets and 35 doublets computed in the configuration interaction step, all of them mixed in RASSI-SO to give the spin-orbit states
electronic_structure_description: An electromer in which the Ni-O linkage is only a sigma bond, leaving unpaired electrons on both the Ni(II) centre and the oxygen, so that ferro- or antiferromagnetic coupling gives S = 3/2 or S = 1/2; a low-spin Ni(II) option adds a third possibility. All three electronic states were computed and the S = 3/2 high-spin form is the ground state, as expected from the unpaired electrons occupying the Ni(II) eg-like orbitals. The pi*(xz) and pi*(yz) orbitals are nearly degenerate, giving very small transition energies between them and hence a large axial zero-field splitting. State-averaged CASSCF gives D = -143.9 cm-1 with E = 6.4 cm-1. With a D of that size only the lower Ms = +/-3/2 Kramers doublet should give an X-band EPR signal, which the authors offer as the explanation for the observed doublet transitions.
Other: Formed with its electromer from a transient precursor by homolytic O-O cleavage, in which an alpha electron stays on the proximal oxygen while a beta electron leaves with the distal one. Formation of 3a/3b from that precursor is endothermic by 32.8 kJ/mol, though the overall reaction from the starting complex remains exothermic, the first step being favourable by -59.8 kJ/mol. This species and its electromer are nearly degenerate, so an equilibrium between them is expected, and the 0.154 angstrom difference in Ni-O bond length between the two raises the possibility of bond-stretch isomerism.
reference_short: B. Pandey, K. Ray, G. Rajaraman et al., Z. Anorg. Allg. Chem. 644, 790-800 (2018)
notes: The computed D of -143.9 cm-1 is described as among the highest reported for nickel complexes and is consistent with the observed trigonal bipyramidal geometry. Two caveats attach to it: the active space is the bare nickel d manifold, so the Ni-O covalency that distinguishes this electromer from the other is not in the correlated treatment at all, and the CASSCF is a single point on a B3LYP geometry, so the 1.844 angstrom Ni-O distance that defines the species is a DFT number. The zero-field splitting values themselves appear only in supplementary Table S7; the article text quotes them but gives no further detail.

As in that species the pi*(xz) and pi*(yz) orbitals are nearly degenerate, and state-averaged CASSCF gives D = -201.1 cm-1 with E = 0.067 cm-1 - a larger axial splitting and an essentially vanishing rhombicity compared with the oxyl electromer.

The wider study finds that the energetic preference for Ni(III)=O over Ni(IV)=O implies that the relevant pi bonding is destabilised in a trigonal bipyramidal arrangement just as it is in octahedral complexes. These species are proposed to perform hydrogen atom abstraction and oxo transfer; they are too reactive and transient for direct characterisation, and only indirect spectral evidence of their formation exists.

notes: The point of the paper is that the electronic structure of putative Ni(III)-oxo species is not unambiguously established, and the pair of near-degenerate electromers computed here is the answer offered: not one species but two, differing in where the unpaired electron sits and in the Ni-O bond length. The CASSCF contribution is confined to the zero-field splitting; everything else - geometries, spin-state energetics, reaction profile, spectra and reactivity - is B3LYP. Since the two electromers differ in exactly the Ni-O covalency that a d-only active space omits, the fact that it returns markedly different D values for them (-201.1 against -143.9 cm-1) comes entirely through the differing geometries rather than through any explicit treatment of the bond.

electronic_structure_description: High-spin Co(II), 3d7, S = 3/2, in a distorted octahedral {CoO5N} environment surrounded by three diamagnetic low-spin Co(III) ions. The two lowest Kramers doublets can be described by an S = 3/2 spin Hamiltonian because the next doublets lie more than 1000 cm-1 higher, and effective Hamiltonian theory then gives D = -53.6 cm-1 with E/D = 0.294, against a POLYMAGNET fit of the measured magnetization giving D = -51.3 cm-1, E/D = 0.263 and g = 2.41. The transversal magnetic moment matrix element between the ground states of opposite magnetization is 0.59, well above the 0.1 threshold for efficient tunnelling, and the computed blocking barrier is U = 120 cm-1. Experimentally the compound shows only a small out-of-phase tail at zero field and clear field-induced slow relaxation at 500 Oe
Other: One active space, one protocol, two close relatives, and a sevenfold difference in accuracy. The identical CAS(7e,5o) metal-only space, the identical DLPNO-NEVPT2 correction, the identical basis and code are applied to the octahedral Co(II) centre of each complex, and the computed axial zero-field splitting is compared against a fit of the measured magnetization. For complex 1 the agreement is excellent: D = -53.6 cm-1 computed against -51.3 fitted, about four and a half percent. For complex 2 the same protocol gives -42.7 against -31.9 fitted, thirty-four percent too large. Nothing about the method changed; what changed is the molecule. Complex 1 contains exactly one paramagnetic centre, a single Co(II) surrounded by three diamagnetic low-spin Co(III) ions, so a single-ion 3d space is the whole magnetic problem. Complex 2 contains two exchange-coupled Co(II) ions, and the paper has to compute their coupling by an entirely separate broken-symmetry DFT calculation - so the single-ion multireference is being asked to reproduce a fitted parameter that the fit itself extracted from a two-centre spin Hamiltonian including J. The article never states how the second Co(II) was handled in the CASSCF for complex 2: no diamagnetic substitution is described, no fragment is named, and the methods text refers only to 'the CoII ion' in the singular. The second finding is that the multireference tunnelling diagnostic does not discriminate between the two compounds at all. SINGLE_ANISO gives transversal magnetic moment matrix elements between the ground states of opposite magnetization of 0.59 for 1 and 0.56 for 2, both far above the 0.1 threshold at which efficient relaxation is expected - essentially the same number. Yet complex 1 is a field-induced single-ion magnet and complex 2 shows no out-of-phase signal whatever, with or without an applied field. The single-ion diagnostic is degenerate across an SMM and a non-SMM, and the factor that actually separates them - the weak Co-Co exchange in 2 opening alternative relaxation pathways - lies outside the multireference entirely and is supplied by density functional theory. The space is complete within its own terms: all possible multiplets of the d7 configuration, ten quartets and forty doublets, are included rather than an energy-window subset. And the AILFT analysis locates the difference between the two complexes in the first coordination sphere: 10Dq is evidently lower in complex 2, attributed to the change of chromophore from {CoO5N} to {CoO3N3}. Against that, the space is bare - five 3d orbitals, no ligand orbital, no second d shell - and it is never enlarged or tested in either compound, so on the complex where it fails there is no evidence about whether composition or the correction is at fault. This is the member on which the protocol succeeds, and it is also the member with exactly one paramagnetic centre - the single-ion space and the single-ion physics coincide

electronic_structure_description: Co(II) with a 4A2 ground term. The first transition energy at CASSCF + NEVPT2 is 4200 reciprocal centimetres. In the spin-orbit multiplet spectrum the last member of the spin-only model space lies at 33.1 and the first multiplet outside it at 4174 reciprocal centimetres. The projection norm for the first member of the model space is 0.98 and the resulting validity score for the spin-Hamiltonian approximation is 1704. A real compound treated at its own experimental geometry.
Other: The multireference licenses or refuses a phenomenological model rather than a cheaper computational method, and it refuses it in two cases out of twelve. The spin-Hamiltonian formalism works in a model space of fictitious spin kets |S,M> only; here the CASSCF + NEVPT2 + spin-orbit multiplets are treated as the exact answer within the complete active space of dn configurations, the relativistic states are projected back onto the spin-only subspace, and the quality of that projection becomes a quantitative test of whether the spin Hamiltonian is entitled to exist for the compound. Two criteria: the projection norm N for each multiplet, which must not stray far from 1, and the gap separating the hypothetical spin-only manifold from the rest of the spin-orbit spectrum, combined into a score S. Of twelve complexes the paper reports two clear violations and two more it calls questionable. The failure condition is named: the projection breaks down when the ground term is orbitally (quasi)degenerate and the first transition energy falls below about 1000 reciprocal centimetres, the same divergence that makes the older second-order perturbative route to the D-tensor return false D, E and g values. Worst case is the pentacoordinate cobalt(II) member with a 4E ground term, projection norm 0.69 and score 6, against 0.999 and scores in the tens of thousands for the orbitally nondegenerate manganese(II) members. The active space is metal-only and complete within itself: five d orbitals holding the dn configuration, spanning all 45, 120, 210 or 252 kets for d2/d8, d3/d7, d4/d6 and d5, with no truncation by energy window, which is what makes the projection norm meaningful. For the cobalt complexes the positive D comes chiefly from the third and fourth quartet excited states, which the paper notes are multideterminant and composed of several d-configurations; the quartet states are reached by promotion from d(xz) or d(yz) into d(z2), and a doublet contribution comes from d(xy) to d(x2-y2) promotion. Ab initio ligand field analysis shows two doubly occupied low-lying d orbitals, d(yz) and d(xz), close in energy and well separated from the singly occupied ones.
Other: The chemical argument is about ligand-field effects and is read through a space that contains no ligand orbital. The spaces are bare metal 3d shells - CAS(8,5) for the nickel(II) complexes and CAS(7,5) for the cobalt(II) ones - with no ligand orbital, no second d shell, and no enlargement or sensitivity test anywhere. The study is about how replacing a weak sigma-donor aqua ligand by a stronger sigma-donor thiocyanate in the axial positions moves the d-orbital energies, and those energies are extracted by ab initio ligand field theory from that same metal-only space, so the covalency difference between an aqua and a thiocyanate donor - the variable being manipulated - is not representable in the space. The state manifold is complete: all the multiplets of each configuration are carried, 10 triplets and 15 singlets for the d8 nickel systems and 10 quartets and 40 doublets for the d7 cobalt ones, averaged over all of them rather than over an energy window. Two extraction routes from one wavefunction give systematically different answers and the paper reports it: the zero-field-splitting parameters are taken from an effective Hamiltonian approach, but the perturbative method in the same code was also run and 'the D values extracted by this method were found to be slightly overestimated as compared to those obtained from the effective Hamiltonian method' - same space, same correction, same wavefunction, a different number with a stated direction purely from how D is projected out. The decomposition of D identifies which factor drives the trend: for the nickel series the axial parameter is resolved into contributions from the first three triplet excited states, and across compounds 1 to 5 the second and third barely move, 26.9 to 21.2 and 25.9 to 19.8 reciprocal centimetres, while the first runs -66.0 to -75.6, so the whole variation in D from -11.8 to -25.7 is carried by the first excited state, whose energy is set by the d(xy) versus d(x2-y2) splitting and hence by distortion of the equatorial pentagon. The same substitution moves the two metals in opposite directions for one reason: replacing axial aqua by thiocyanate raises the d(z2) orbital in both and so reduces the positive contributions to D from states reached by promotion into it. In the nickel complexes, where D is negative, that makes D more negative - within the daplh family -11.8 and -11.5 become -18.6, and within the daphibh family -18.4 becomes -25.7 - while in the cobalt complexes, where D is positive, the same mechanism makes D smaller: 39.4, 38.6 and 39.4 for the aqua complexes against 36.8 and 36.9 for the thiocyanate ones.

electronic_structure_description: Ni(II) d8, S = 1, in a hexacoordinate NiO4N2 environment of C2v symmetry (OC-6, shape index 3.08). The ground electronic term is orbitally nondegenerate, with the first excitation energy at NEVPT2 being 7181 reciprocal centimetres. Spin-orbit coupling splits the ground term into spin-orbit multiplets from which an effective Hamiltonian gives an axial zero-field splitting parameter of D = -14.7 reciprocal centimetres. Experimentally D is reported as -13.7 from DC magnetic data, with an effective barrier of 16 K at 0.2 T
Other: The paper defines a threshold beyond which its own computed D-parameter is meaningless and marks the offending values in its table: 'E/|D| close to the critical value of 0.33 implies that the sign of D is uncertain and D stays meaningless; problematic values are printed in italics.' The conclusions restate it - the sign of D is set by the relative positions of the three lowest spin-orbit multiplets, and 'in the case of E/D ~ 0.33, this stays uncertain'. The failure condition is tied to orbital degeneracy and predicted in advance from geometry: for pentacoordinate Ni(II) at the trigonal bipyramid (D3h, tau5 = 1) the ground term is the orbitally degenerate 3E and 'the D-parameter is undefined', with six spin-orbit multiplets in play that have 'no relationship to the spin-Hamiltonian parameters D and E'; at the tetragonal pyramid (C4v, tau5 = 0) the ground term is nondegenerate and D is positive; in between, at C2v, D runs from large negative to positive and crosses zero at tau5 about 0.2. The three complexes with 3E ground terms return the largest axial parameters in the study, -397, -510 and -544 reciprocal centimetres, and those are the cases where the spin Hamiltonian has no standing. The active space is the complete d8 manifold and nothing more - all 45 kets - the same space used by the semiempirical generalized crystal field theory run alongside it, so the two methods are compared on identical footing; but it carries no ligand orbital and no second d shell, and no enlargement or sensitivity test appears anywhere. The experimental reference varies by technique: for the trigonal-bipyramidal complex 5 the measured D is -311 from magnetometry against -535 from EPR, and for complex 6 it is -179 by EPR, -110 by far-infrared magnetic spectroscopy and -205 from calculation.

Its computed -14.7 sits close to the measured -13.7, and it is the only hexacoordinate member of the set with a reported effective barrier. Other: The paper defines a threshold beyond which its own computed D-parameter is meaningless and marks the offending values in its table: 'E/|D| close to the critical value of 0.33 implies that the sign of D is uncertain and D stays meaningless; problematic values are printed in italics.' The conclusions restate it - the sign of D is set by the relative positions of the three lowest spin-orbit multiplets, and 'in the case of E/D ~ 0.33, this stays uncertain'. The failure condition is tied to orbital degeneracy and predicted in advance from geometry: for pentacoordinate Ni(II) at the trigonal bipyramid (D3h, tau5 = 1) the ground term is the orbitally degenerate 3E and 'the D-parameter is undefined', with six spin-orbit multiplets in play that have 'no relationship to the spin-Hamiltonian parameters D and E'; at the tetragonal pyramid (C4v, tau5 = 0) the ground term is nondegenerate and D is positive; in between, at C2v, D runs from large negative to positive and crosses zero at tau5 about 0.2. The three complexes with 3E ground terms return the largest axial parameters in the study, -397, -510 and -544 reciprocal centimetres, and those are the cases where the spin Hamiltonian has no standing. All multiplets of the d4 configuration are included in the wavefunction expansion, 10 quintets, 45 triplets and 50 singlets, and the zero-field splitting and g tensor of the lowest spin-orbit state are then obtained by applying spin-orbit and spin-spin coupling operators, with Douglas-Kroll-Hess relativistic treatment. The space is not varied and no ligand orbitals are correlated, which is the usual limitation of a d-only AILFT space: covalency with the porphyrin and the axial ligands enters only through the orbital optimisation. The calculations are single points on DFT-optimised high-spin geometries. The validation is against experiment and against DFT on the same geometries: NEVPT2 gives D of about -3.5 cm-1 for both complexes while DFT gives the same sign at roughly half the magnitude, and the authors note the NEVPT2 values agree with earlier experimental and computational work. electronic_structure_description: A four-coordinate high-spin Co(II) centre in a distorted tetrahedral CoO4 environment, giving easy-plane anisotropy. The computed axial zero-field splitting is positive - 17.9 per centimetre for the S enantiomer and 18.0 for the R - against 10.0 fitted from the magnetic data, and the rhombic term is 1.8 and 1.2 against 1.0 and 1.4 fitted. The computed g tensors are (2.411, 2.441, 2.167) and (2.421, 2.436, 2.168), nearly axial in the xy plane. Effective barriers of 46(1) and 41(1) K are measured under a 1000 Oe field. The first excited quartet state dominates the D value, and this compound's larger ground-to-first-excited gap is what keeps its D small and positive
Other: The calculation gets the sign right and the magnitude consistently twofold too large, and because two compounds with opposite signs behave the same way the overshoot is measurable rather than anecdotal. Against the values fitted from the magnetic data, the computed axial zero-field splitting runs 17.9 and 18.0 per centimetre against a fitted 10.0 for the difluoro compound, and -69.2 and -66.1 against a fitted -30.0 for the dinaphthyl one. The rhombic term behaves identically: 1.8 against 1.0, and -18.8 against -8.7. Four complexes, two opposite signs, and a ratio near two in every case. Nothing here shows the factor would transfer to a third compound. The 'experimental' reference is itself a constrained fit, and the constraint is one the calculation contradicts. The footnote to the comparison table reads: 'to avoid overparameterization during fitting in PHI, g(x) was constrained to equal g(y)'. But the CASSCF/RASSI-SO g tensors for the dinaphthyl compound are 1.951, 2.523 and 3.041 - g(x) and g(y) differing by more than half a unit. The measurement against which the calculation is judged was extracted under an assumption the calculation says is false, so the twofold discrepancy is not purely a failure of theory; part of it may be the price of a rhombic system fitted with an axial model. Two enantiomers must have identical magnetic anisotropy; any computed difference is pure protocol noise. Here the computed values differ by 0.1 per centimetre for the difluoro pair and 3.1 for the dinaphthyl pair - about 0.6 and 4.5 percent - each calculation having been run on its own separately determined crystal structure. That is a direct measure of how much the answer moves with structural and numerical noise. The fitted barriers scatter far more between the same pairs - 46(1) against 41(1) K, and 63(6) against 48(2) K, differences of 11 and 24 percent - so the experiment is noisier than the calculation between systems that must be identical. D is decomposed state by state and one term dominates, which reduces the design problem to a single energy gap. 'For all four complexes, the first excited quartet state provides the largest contribution to the D value. Accordingly, the magnitude of D is closely correlated with the energy separation between the ground state and the first excited state. compound_name: Graphannulenes / carbon nanocones (13 illustrative systems including benzene, corannulene, coronene, Kekulene, and GAn(0,2) nanocones)
geometry_source: geometries optimized at (U)B3LYP/6-31G* (closed-shell singlet for GHR-predicted closed shells; triplet then broken-symmetry singlet for predicted open shells, which show a Jahn-Teller-distorting imaginary mode)
method: state-averaged CASSCF single points (lowest singlet and triplet targeted) to confirm or refute the generalized Hückel rule (GHR) prediction of the ground-state spin/shell character
basis_set: def2-SV(P) with RIJK density fitting (def2/JK auxiliary)
active_space_orbital_description: per-system pi active spaces (e.g. (8,8)) chosen from the Hartree-Fock frontier-orbital energies and degeneracies; the number of states is likewise set by the frontier degeneracy
active_space_protocol: The active space and number of state-averaged states are selected per SYSTEM from the HF orbital energies and degeneracy pattern - i.e. the generalized Hückel rule (GHR) itself dictates how big a space and how many states are needed. GHR-predicted CLOSED-shell systems (coronene, corannulene, Kekulene - 24/20/48 pi electrons) are confirmed by an SA-CASSCF wavefunction dominated by a single configuration (large leading weight); GHR-predicted OPEN-shell systems (e.g. GA4(0,2)) instead show two near-degenerate configurations of equal weight (~0.39 each), diradical character, and a Jahn-Teller distortion - analogous to cyclobutadiene. So the CASSCF confirms the GHR's shell-character predictions. The most-cited active space in the paper is (8,8).
nroots_per_mult: set per system by frontier-orbital degeneracy
Other: A generalized Hückel rule (GHR) for carbon nanocones / general polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons ('graphannulenes' - a single annulene ring merged with graphene sectors), extending the 4n+2 rule beyond simple annulenes. The GHR predicts closed- vs open-shell (aromatic vs antiaromatic/diradical) ground states from the pi-electron count and ring topology; SA-CASSCF is used to verify the predictions on 13 systems. This is the general pathology: discontinuities appear in SA-CASSCF potential energy surfaces whenever a state left out of the average crosses one that is included, and they break energy conservation in excited-state dynamics. The remedy demonstrated here is dynamical weighting with a spline, DWS3-(4,6eV)-CASSCF, which mimics SA-CASSCF while smoothly removing the discontinuities due to unweighted state crossings. Practical guidance: when choosing how many states to state-average, the risk is not only the orbital active space but which states are omitted from the average along the coordinate of interest

geometry_source: global potential energy and dipole moment surfaces computed as functions of the intermolecular separation R and the three angles; the H-shaped geometry at R = 6 a0 corresponds to the minimum of the triplet O2(X)-O2(X) potential
method: explicitly correlated multireference configuration interaction with Davidson size-consistency correction (F12-MRCI+Q) for the potentials; dipole surfaces at both MRCI and CASSCF; F12-CASPT2 also used for benchmarks. Potentials and dipole surfaces transformed to a diabatic basis with a multiple-property-based diabatization algorithm
basis_set: augmented correlation-consistent aug-cc-pVnZ (n = D, T, Q) with the corresponding standardized auxiliary basis sets
active_space_orbital_description: three nested spaces: sCAS = four electrons in the four pi* orbitals; mCAS = 12 electrons in the pi shell; lCAS = 16 electrons in the p shell. The orbital counts for mCAS and lCAS are not given numerically
active_space_protocol: Three explicitly defined choices, used as a convergence ladder: (1) sCAS — four electrons in the four pi* orbitals, the MINIMAL active space that gives a zeroth-order description of all states of interest, i.e. all states arising from the (pi)4(pi*)2 configuration of the O2 monomers; (2) mCAS — 12 electrons in the pi shell, which additionally captures the static correlation of the pi electrons, important for O2 because of the well-known Hartree-Fock instability associated with artificial breaking of inversion symmetry; (3) lCAS — 16 electrons in the p shell. lCAS is prohibitively expensive at low-symmetry geometries, so the full potential energy and dipole moment surfaces could not be computed with it; mCAS is the production space for the surfaces, with lCAS used only for benchmarks at high-symmetry geometries. Benchmarking shows the interaction energy converges reasonably smoothly, albeit slowly, with active space and basis set, so accurate energies are obtainable from affordable MRCI; the transition dipole moment behaves quite differently and depends strongly on the level of theory. Prior systematic work (their Ref. 18) comparing MRCI, CASPT2 and ACPF against CCSD(T) for the high-spin quintet suggests treating MRCI and CASPT2 as upper and lower limits to the potential respectively, with CASPT2 the more reliable; MRCI is nevertheless used here because it gives straightforward access to the transition properties needed for the dipole surface and the diabatization

electronic_structure_description: Ground term: triplet O2(X 3Sigma_g-)-O2(X 3Sigma_g-). Seven triplet states of the dimer are treated. The monomer transitions underlying the collision-induced bands are X 3Sigma_g- -> a 1Delta_g at 7883 cm-1 and X 3Sigma_g- -> b 1Sigma_g+ at 13 122 cm-1. Interaction energies for the seven triplet states are tabulated at the H-shaped geometry at R = 6 a0 using F12-MRCI+Q with all three active spaces and with mCAS F12-CASPT2, but the individual values are not reproduced here
Other: For the triplet ground state of the complex the potential energy surface agrees reasonably with previous calculations, while global EXCITED state potentials are reported here for the first time. Central caveat: the transition dipole moment surfaces depend strongly on the level of theory at which they are computed, as confirmed by the high-symmetry benchmarks, so the authors conclude that ab initio calculations of collision-induced absorption spectra cannot become quantitatively predictive until more accurate transition dipoles are available. The paper also derives the angular expansion of the surfaces and the symmetry constraints on the expansion coefficients, gives working equations for obtaining them by numerical integration over angles, and presents an interpolation scheme with exponential extrapolation to short and large separations for the R dependence

Predicted intense bands near 550, 950 and 2300 cm-1. Energies (a.u.) at 6-311++G**: CASSCF -344.242081, FOCI -344.317341, SOCI -344.385545; gap to SiNH2+ X 1A1: 123.6 (CASSCF), 158.2 (FOCI), 115.2 (SOCI) kcal/mol. Recommended scaled-CASSCF rotational constants A0/B0/C0 (GHz) for other isotopomers (Table IV): HD28Si14N+ 102.432/14.690/12.847; D2 28Si14N+ 74.982/14.131/11.890; H2 29Si14N+ 149.811/15.275/13.862; H2 30Si14N+ 149.811/15.153/13.761; H2 28Si15N+ 149.811/14.726/13.408.

geometry_source: stationary points located with CASSCF(8,8) analytic derivatives in the Dunning-Hay polarized valence double-zeta basis; minimum energy paths; Cs symmetry
method: CASSCF(8,8) derivative methods for stationary points; internally contracted CI (ICCI, variants CI1 and CI2) with a multireference Davidson correction (+Q) for the energetics; CASSCF/pVDZ harmonic frequencies for ZPE

active_space_orbital_description: the eight electrons depicted in Fig. 1(a), in six a' and two a'' active orbitals
electronic_structure_description: ICCI+ZPE relative energies vs 1CH2+N2 (kcal/mol). cc-pVQZ (CI1): min 1 (diazirine) -24.0, min 2 (diazomethane) -33.9, 3CH2+N2 -9.7. cc-pVTZ CI1: 3CH2+N2 -10.4, vdW -0.5, sp3 -4.9, sp1 4.7, min 1 -23.3, min 2 -32.9, HCN2+H 66.2; CI2: sp1 4.4, min 1 -23.3, sp2 19.8, min 2 -33.2, CH2N+N 64.3. cc-pVDZ (CI1): min 1 -21.4, min 2 -29.7, 3CH2+N2 -12.3. CASSCF/pVDZ: sp1 23.5, min 1 -3.5, sp2 40.8, min 2 -2.7, vdW -1.9, sp3 2.2. Conclusions: 1CH2+N2 gives diazomethane with no barrier and diazirine with a 5 kcal/mol barrier; diazirine -> diazomethane rearrangement barrier 20 kcal/mol relative to reactants; CH2N+N and CHN2+H endothermic by 64 and 66 kcal/mol. 0 K heats of formation 77.7 (diazirine) and 68.0 kcal/mol (diazomethane), assigned maximum error 2 kcal/mol. CASSCF/pVDZ harmonic frequencies and ZPEs in Table II. Diazirine + OH -> CHN2 + H2O computed exothermic by 28.5 kcal/mol.
Other: CASSCF/pVDZ energetics are much less reliable than ICCI: binding energies are underestimated and barriers overestimated. sp3 is a saddle point at the CASSCF level but lies below the reactants at the ICCI level, so the barrier is shifted far into the entrance channel and the diazomethane pathway is probably barrierless.

notes: One row for the whole CH2N2 reaction surface; individual stationary points have no separate rows. geometry_source: PES cut along a terminal twist coordinate with all other bonds and angles frozen at their S2 planar minimum values; AIMD initial conditions by Monte Carlo sampling of the ground-state harmonic Wigner distribution (BLYP/6-31g)
method: SA-4-CASSCF and dynamically weighted DWS3-(4,6eV)-CASSCF (dynamical weight with cubic spline, L=4, alpha=6 eV) with new analytical DW-CASSCF gradients; AIMD on S2 (pi pi*): 30 trajectories, 100 fs, 10 au timestep (adaptively decreased), electronic transitions disabled, all C-H bond lengths constrained to ground-state equilibrium values
software: MOLPRO 2012.1 (developmental Ab Initio Multiple Spawning package for the AIMD)
basis_set: 6-31G* (PES cut); 6-31g (AIMD)
active_space_orbital_description: full pi-valence active space (4 electrons in 4 orbitals)
nroots_per_mult: 4 (SA-4); DWS3-(4,6eV) dynamically weights S0-S8 so that S0-S3 carry equal weights
electronic_structure_description: SA-4-CASSCF(4/4)/6-31G* potential curves show a discontinuity of about 0.05 eV in all states at a terminal twist angle of 43 deg, where the unweighted S4 crosses S3 (included in the average). In AIMD on S2, SA-4-CASSCF(4/4)/6-31g gives total-energy discontinuities of as much as about 0.1 eV in most of the 30 trajectories; DWS3-(4,6eV)-CASSCF shows no discernible discontinuities, only a spread of about +-0.002 eV over 100 fs, arising near a terminal twist of 90 deg where S3-S2 and S2-S1 intersections occur.
Other: The discontinuity comes from the state-averaging choice, not the orbital space: a state left out of the average (S4) crossing one in it (S3) causes a discontinuous orbital change. Adding S4 to the average would remove this one, but S5 crosses S4 along other coordinates, so adding states is generally futile; DWS3-(4,6eV) reproduces the SA-4-CASSCF curves while removing the discontinuity, because S3 and S4 weights become equal at their crossing. Alpha too small stops the CASSCF converging; too large needs many extra states and deviates from SA-L results; alpha=6 eV decays like sech weights with beta=3 eV. Gradients with fixed weights only give large energy fluctuations, so the weight-derivative terms cannot be neglected. CASSCF(4/4) significantly overestimates the vertical S1-S2 gap relative to higher levels, mainly from missing dynamic correlation, and hydrogen migration seen at SA-CASSCF(4/4) needs sigma and sigma* orbitals in the active space; it was suppressed by constraining the C-H bonds so the (4/4) space could be used.
reference_short: W. J. Glover, J. Chem. Phys. 141, 171102 (2014)
notes: The author presents butadiene here only as a model to demonstrate DWS-CASSCF energy conservation, not as an accurate description of its excited-state dynamics. Multiplicity is not stated (states labelled S0-S8).

DDCI natural MOs: CASCI -468, SC-NEVPT2 -1006, PC-NEVPT2 -1029, CASPT2 -1162, DDCI -1145. Other: With the minimal CAS(2,2), the orbitals rather than the correlation method limit the MRPT2 J: singlet-CASSCF MOs give MRPT2 J far too small in magnitude (SC-NEVPT2 -587 cm-1), while DDCI natural MOs (-1006) or SA-CASSCF(2,2) MOs with weight W=0.7 on the magnetic singlet and 0.3 on the ionic singlet (SA-7/10, -1067) bring NEVPT2/CASPT2 close to DDCI and experiment; DDCI itself is almost insensitive to the orbital choice here. The SA-CASSCF magnetic MOs overlap the DDCI natural MOs best near W=0.7 (close to the maximum for 0.66<W<0.74; maximum overlaps very close to 1), equal weights overestimate the delocalisation of the active MOs, and the MRPT2 J magnitude grows as W decreases (CASCI J almost unchanged for W 60-100%). The authors attribute the failure with CASSCF MOs to orbital relaxation induced by electron correlation, which MRPT2 does not capture, leaving the ionic forms too high in energy (U around 24 eV for the systems considered); the proposed strategy is not expected to help for ferromagnetic systems. A 7:3 mixture gives magnetic orbitals with overlap >0.995 with the DDCI natural MOs, and MRPT2 J values from these SA-7/10 MOs closely resemble those obtained from the DDCI natural orbitals.
reference_short: Angeli & Calzado, J. Chem. Phys. 137, 034104 (2012)
notes: Embedded cluster model of a solid: the Cu2O7 fragment coordinates are taken from the crystal and embedded in point charges and total ion potentials simulating the Madelung potential and Pauli repulsion of the infinite crystal; not an isolated molecule. Similar MRPT2 results are obtained with triplet CASSCF or state-specific orbitals, per the authors.

geometry_source: grid of internuclear distances; long-range method used beyond R = 6 a0; SO couplings computed between Rstart and 10.9 a0
method: Long range: MRCI on undistorted MOs built as fixed combinations of atomic orbitals from a state-averaged CASSCF of the three O(3P) states, with the complete active space as reference, Boys-Bernardi counterpoise generalised to open-shell fragments; SO matrix elements at CASSCF with one- and two-electron Breit-Pauli integrals; radial derivative coupling <2 3Sigma_u+|d/dR|A 3Sigma_u+> by two-point finite difference (dR = 0.1 a0) at CASSCF and CASSCF+MRCI
basis_set: Long range and derivative coupling: van Duijneveldt (13s8p) contracted [5s4p] plus even-tempered (6d4f2g) contracted [3d2f1g], plus uncontracted diffuse s, p and outermost d; SO integrals: uncontracted (12s6p3d) cc-pVQZ primitives
active_space_orbital_description: complete 2s/2p valence space; 1s cores built from atomic 1s orbitals
electronic_structure_description: Reduced SO matrix elements at R = 7.5 a0 (Table VII, muEh; atomic limit / long-range method / short-range method), e.g. 1Pi_u-A' 3Delta_u 705 / 725 / 726, 3Pi_u-A 3Sigma_u+ 0 / -54 / -405, A 3Sigma_u+-c 1Sigma_u- -814 / -877 / -1021, 2 3Sigma_u+-5Sigma_u- 644 / 594 / 71 (atomic limit from A_exp = -0.353 mEh). Fitted asymptotic atomic SO constant A = -0.3627 mEh reproduces all fitted values at infinity within 6.4 muEh and nonzero values within 2%. A' 3Delta_u spin-orbit constants A_v: v=0 -0.3363 mEh calc vs -0.3413 expt (-1.47%), deviations generally below 4%, v=13 -0.2163 vs -0.178 (21.5%). SO couplings differ from Klotz and Peyerimhoff's by less than 15 muEh. Nonadiabatic coupling times fragment velocity (2.2e-3 a.u., from 35 mEh excess kinetic energy at the highest experimental dissociation energy, 204 nm) gives about -0.43 mEh at the peak, comparable to the spin-orbit splitting constant A = -0.36 mEh; beyond R = 9.0 a0 it is below 0.03 mEh.

electronic_structure_description: Axial (square-pyramidal) modification is lowest for triplet and quintet; planar is favoured for the singlet. CASSCF total energies (FireFly): triplet T1 -4465.532 eV, quintet Q1 -4465.50 eV. GAMESS CASSCF/IMCP-SR1 puts the quintet slightly below the triplet; the paper concludes that no unambiguous choice between M = 3 and M = 5 for the ground state can be made. XMCQDPT2(10,8)/SBKJC: the triplet spectrum (two pronounced peaks shifted to shorter wavelength than the experimental maximum, with a long-wavelength shoulder) reproduces the key-intermediate absorption much better than the quintet, especially in water; singlet transitions at 8.51 eV (axial) and above 21.96 eV (planar). Free Os4+ computed by both methods favours M = 5 (Table S11), used to argue the quintet could also be favoured for OsCl5-.
Other: Spin-state ordering depends on the basis/ECP: CASSCF with IMCP-SR1 (scalar-relativistic pseudopotentials) favours the quintet, FireFly with SBKJC favours the triplet; the authors attribute this to the relativistic pseudopotentials compressing the complex (shorter bonds with IMCP-SR1). The authors note that the XMCQDPT dynamic-correlation correction differs for states of different nature and multiplicity, so CASSCF and XMCQDPT transition energies and state orders may differ substantially; XMCQDPT results are judged more reliable, though the total-energy differences determining the level order are small, and methods including spin-orbit coupling could change the order of energy levels.

electronic_structure_description: Lowest cation state: 2B1 (D0). Vertical ionisation energies, CAS(7,8)/6-31+G* (Table 2): 2B1 7.986 eV (exp. 8.508), 2A2 8.670 eV (exp. 9.280). CAS(7,8) MECI between 2B1 and 2A2 lies 0.54 eV above the Franck-Condon point of the 2B1 state; geometry planar with a quinoid-type distortion (ortho-meta C-C bonds lengthen, other C-C bonds contract, C-O and O-H contract, C-O-H angle increases). Simulated spectrum (model energies shifted to experiment): band origins 0-0 at 8.33 eV (2B1) and 9.31 eV (2A2). After vertical ionisation into 2A2, significant population transfer within 10 fs; 2B1 population reaches a final value of 0.3 at 200 fs. Spectrum damping times 30 fs (2B1 band) and 14 fs (2A2 band); the conical intersection adds broadening to the 2A2 band. In the 2A2 band the peak at ~9.47 eV is assigned to the C-O stretch 7^1_0 (the authors disagree with the earlier assignment to the 814 cm-1 mode, nu2 in their model).
Other: CASSCF(7,8) underestimates both vertical ionisation energies (by 0.52 eV for 2B1 and 0.61 eV for 2A2) but reproduces the state ordering and the relative 2B1-2A2 energy difference; the energies were shifted to experiment for the model Hamiltonian. The fitted on-diagonal linear coupling constant kappa9 (C-C ring stretch) of 2B1 had to be changed in sign to reproduce the vibrational fine structure, which 'alludes to a failing in the CASSCF potential energy surfaces'; MP2/6-31+G* gives kappa9 = -0.214 eV, close to the altered value, 'pointing to the potential importance of electron correlation for this mode'. 2A2 points along nu7 lying off the fitted curve are attributed to 'minor failings of the low level CASSCF calculations'.
reference_short: Vibronic coupling model to calculate the photoelectron spectrum of phenol, Chem. Phys. (2018)
notes: The IE underestimates (0.52, 0.61 eV) are arithmetic from Table 2. The paper gives no rationale for the choice of active-space orbitals.

OOC (1A') minimum 170.0 kcal/mol (7.37 eV) above the OCO minimum, OOC-OCO barrier 8.5 kcal/mol (0.369 eV); OOC minimum confirmed at MRCISD+Q and CCSD(T). The covalent three-electron/three-centre-bond S0/S1 MECI found at CASSCF is lost at the SF-TD-DFT and MS-CASPT2 levels because low-energy ionic configurations missing at CASSCF are included; the photochemically relevant crossing becomes zwitterionic (ground state with 1 1Bu) and is reached directly from 1 1Bu without populating 2 1Ag. But the decomposition disagrees: SORCI gives DSOC = 2.25 and DSSC = 0.65 cm-1 (XRD 108 K) while DFT makes DSSC the larger contributor, each term being wrong by nearly a factor of two in opposite directions.
